source: Argentine passport 1940; SA death cert 1950; and Maitland Road Cemetery, Record of Interments, page 339 entry 327 - IMAGE READ 8 October 2026, FamilySearch image group 102346236 ('Maitland Cemetery Volume 21', Cemetery Records 1949-1951), image 93 of 252, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSVY-JS18; index ark 1:1:QPW2-W48F

David's great-grandfather. *** PLACE FIELD CORRECTED 14 September 2026. *** This row's 'where found' held a CITATION - "SA + Argentine records" - where the atlas expects a PLACE, so this person was missing from the map and appeared on it as a phantom location instead. The citation is kept here; the field now holds a real place. *** WHERE HE IS BURIED IS SETTLED, 8 October 2026. *** Entry 327 of the Maitland Road Cemetery Record of Interments, page 339: *** LERENA, Robert Paul ***, M.E., aged *** 76 ***, late residence *** Newlands, 7 Forth Road *** - the address on his death certificate - Roman Catholic allotment, Cemetery No. 1, *** grave 7719 C ***, depth *** 8 feet ***, position *** Bott ***, officiating *** Father Plotton ***, undertaker *** Goodall & Wms ***. The last column reads *** 'In Plot of R. P. Lerina' ***. *** SO THE PLOT WAS HIS. *** Not a space allotted at need: a grave held in his own name, which his wife had been buried in fifteen years before him and an infant three years before him. *** AND THE WHOLE GRAVE WAS READ ON 8 OCTOBER 2026. *** Maitland (Woltemade) Road Cemetery, Cemetery No. 1, Roman Catholic allotment, *** GRAVE 7719 - and the register calls it 'In Plot of R. P. Lerina', his own plot. *** Three burials, in order: *** 7719 A *** Mary Septima, 51, buried 16 Nov 1935 (p.3215 entry 163); *** 7719 B *** Careen Maria, two weeks old, died 27 June 1947 (p.4706 entry 423); *** 7719 C *** Robert Paul himself, 76, died 19 March 1950 (p.339 entry 327). *** THE DEATH CERTIFICATE SAID MAITLAND AND THE FAMILY SAID NEWLANDS, and the certificate was right *** - 'intended place of burial' turned out to be the actual one. *** AND IT WAS INDEXED AS 'ROBERT PAUL LESINA' ***, which is why no search for LERENA had ever found it. That is the seventh machine misreading of this surname this archive has documented. *** IT WAS FOUND BY NOT SEARCHING FOR THE SURNAME AT ALL: *** given name 'Robert Paul', death year 1950, collection only - 663 results, and he was the first. *** 13 OCTOBER 2026 - A MARRIAGE EXTRACT THAT SAYS 1905. *** St Dominic's, Wynberg, certified 7 April 1916: Pablo Armando Lerena and Mary Septima Taylor married *** 3rd September 1905 *** by Rev. B. W. Glynn, witnesses J. B. Worthington and H. Lautenbach. The register entry (no. 7271, entry 160) has the same day, priest and witnesses and the year *** 1911 ***; the ages 29 and 27 fit 1911, and Roque's baptism in June 1911 is 'three months before'. 1911 stands; why a 1916 extract carries 1905 is not known. The same church's own register page gives the couple's residence as 'Ebenezer Road, Wynberg' where the civil duplicate has Diep River. On the wedding invitation of 1949 he is 'Mr R. Lerena', alive. Detail on /family-papers/.

name: Mary Septima TAYLOR (LERENA by marriage)
source: GRO Bideford reg.; d. 15 Nov 1935; and a Taylor family group photograph (family papers, supplied 8 October 2026); and Northam, St Margaret, baptism register - Devon Baptisms (findmypast / South West Heritage Trust), archive reference 1843A/PR/1/16, read 8 October 2026
note: Wife of Pablo Armando. *** PLACE FIELD CORRECTED 14 September 2026. *** This row's 'where found' held a CITATION - "GRO + SA records" - where the atlas expects a PLACE, so this person was missing from the map and appeared on it as a phantom location instead. The citation is kept here; the field now holds a real place. *** AND SHE IS NOT ALONE IN GRAVE 7719, established 8 October 2026. *** The Maitland Road Cemetery Record of Interments, page 4706 entry 423, puts *** CAREEN MARIA LERENA, aged two weeks ***, in Roman Catholic allotment, Cons. No. 1, *** grave 7719 *** - the grave this archive already held for her as 7719A. The child was buried there in 1947, twelve years after Mary Septima died. *** AND THE PLOT IS NOW READ WHOLE, 8 October 2026. *** Her 7719 A is the first of three places in *** grave 7719 ***, which the 1950 register calls *** 'In Plot of R. P. Lerina' *** - her husband's own plot. Careen Maria took 7719 B in 1947 and he took 7719 C in 1950. *** AND THERE IS A FACE, from 8 October 2026. *** A studio group of twelve people and an infant, with a dog asleep on a cushion at the front, which David identifies as *** Mary Septima with her father, her mother and her siblings ***. She is the small girl at the *** lower right ***, against the knee of the seated man with full side-whiskers. *** IT IS THE ONLY IDENTIFIED LIKENESS OF HER THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS *** - of anyone in this family before the Cape. *** NOBODY ELSE IN THE GROUP IS NAMED ***, and no sibling will be matched to a face here. *** AND THEN THIS ARCHIVE OVER-READ IT AND WAS CORRECTED. *** It first said 'at least eight daughters and two sons are in the frame' and offered the number as the ordinary explanation of *** Septima ***, meaning seventh. David answered that he thought *** a grandmother or an aunt *** was in the group as well, which is the whole objection: *** a granddaughter, a niece, a daughter-in-law and a neighbour's child all photograph identically. *** Twelve figures can be counted - three male, eight female, one infant whose sex cannot be told. Daughters cannot. *** THE RECORD THAT WOULD SETTLE THE SIBLING COUNT *** is the 1891 census of Northam, already read here for the Brayleys and never counted for the Taylors. *** THE DATE IS INFERRED AND ONLY INFERRED: *** she was born 17 September 1884 and the child looks five or six, which puts the sitting about *** 1889-1891 ***; the dress agrees without narrowing it. A photographer's imprint on the mount would settle it, and the supplied image is cropped to the print. *** AND HER OWN BAPTISM WAS FOUND ON 8 OCTOBER 2026, which this archive had never had. *** *** MARY SEPTIMA TAYLOR, baptised 30 OCTOBER 1884 at NORTHAM, St Margaret ***, Anglican; father *** WILLIAM ***, mother *** MARY ANN ELLEN ***. Born 17 September 1884, so six weeks old. *** IT IS THE FIRST TIME HER PARENTS ARE NAMED TOGETHER IN A PARISH REGISTER *** rather than in a tree, a census or a birth index - and the earliest record of her own life, pre-dating her 1911 marriage at Wynberg by twenty-seven years. *** HER SIX SIBLINGS ARE ON THE SAME PAGE SERIES: *** Horace Archibald and Isabella Temple (both 1874), Margaret Helen Walker (1876), Irene (1879), Lucy Elizabeth (31 Aug 1881) and Agnes Walker (21 Aug 1889), all to the same parents. See data/taylor-baptisms-northam.tsv. *** AND HER MARRIED SURNAME IS NOW IN HER NAME HERE, because three records carry her under it *** - the Maitland burial register, the 1935 passenger list and the Johannesburg cemetery index all call her LERENA. A reader searching the surname she was buried under should find her. *** 13 OCTOBER 2026: *** she was the *** informant, 'present at the death' ***, when her mother Mary Ann Hellen Taylor died at Sweet Home Terrace, Northam, on 21 April 1900 (entry 83, registered 23 April); she was sixteen. The marriage extract of 1916 and the church register page are described under Pablo's row. *** A CANDIDATE VOYAGE, NOT ESTABLISHED: *** 'Taylor, Mary S.', wife, 42, 1st class, landed Southampton from South Africa on the Arundel Castle on 14 December 1925 for the Ladies' Carlton Club, Chesterfield Gardens, Mayfair, London - her initials and almost her age (41 by this register), but under her maiden name; it may be another woman. A colourised crop of the Taylor group photograph is on her page; the colours are the software's.

*** Her nine brothers and sisters were all found in the same index and then followed to their deaths *** - and four married surnames came out of it: Isabella Temple married *** HENRY DALLING ***, Lucy Elizabeth married *** WILLIAM NORRISH SWEET ***, Irene married *** HENRY ALBERT BURTON ***, Agnes Walker married *** ALFRED S WOOD ***. *** Mary Septima is the only one of the ten who is not in the English death index: she died at Cape Town in 1935. The citation is kept here; the field now holds a real place. *** AND HE IS ON A UNION VOTERS' ROLL, found 9 October 2026 by a route this archive had never used. *** FamilySearch's FULL-TEXT search reads the words on unindexed images; the roll gives *** 'STEMDISTRIK POLLING DISTRICT NO. 770 ... 1491 Lerena, Roque Luis Armando' ***, between Leibbrandt and Le Riche in a strictly alphabetical list. He was twenty to twenty-six across the years this roll covers. *** THESE ROLLS CARRY AN ADDRESS AND A TENURE *** - the same page's columns run Owner, Sole Tenant, Joint Tenant, Medehuurder - *** but the OCR cannot be aligned to the names, so his address needs the plate read by eye. *** A first-class lead on where he was living before Bloemfontein in 1932. *** AN ADDRESS, A TRADE AND A TENURE, 9 October 2026 - AND THE PLATE READ BY EYE BECAUSE THE OCR COULD NOT ALIGN THE COLUMNS. *** On a second roll of polling district 770 he is voter *** 1399 *** and the printed line reads '*** Lerena, Roque Luis Armando ... 14 FLORENCE VILLAS ... FIREMAN ... O ... SOLE TENANT ... E ***'. *** HE IS THE SOLE TENANT OF HIS OWN ADDRESS AT ABOUT TWENTY-TWO. *** *** AND THE DISTRICT HAS A NAME NOW: *** one line of the same page carries '*** Louis Botha Hostel, OBSERVATORY ***' and the street column runs Lower Main Rd, Trill Rd, Scott Rd, Arnold St and *** Salt River *** - *** so district 770 is OBSERVATORY and SALT RIVER, Cape Town. *** *** HIS FATHER WAS A HORSE-DEALER AND A TRAINER; HE WENT TO THE RAILWAY. *** The lines around his read Loco. Cleaner, Engine-driver, Signalman, Porter, Checker, Guard and Shunter, *** so 'Fireman' here is almost certainly a LOCOMOTIVE fireman - an inference from the company on the page, not from the word, which alone could mean a fire brigade. *** *** 13 OCTOBER 2026: *** his 1936 civil marriage entry (Duplicate Original Marriage Register no. 14/1936, Mayfair, Johannesburg, 21 September 1936) gives his trade as *** steward ***, his age as 29 overwritten 30, and his and the widow Rosaline Wilhelmina Chappell's address as 6a Bartlett Road, Mayfair West; witnesses A. W. Webber and S. Brophy. A 1997 letter says Nuno and 'Cardo' (Ricardo) lived at the Newlands house while at the Marist school; it does not name Roque.

name: Nuno Fernando LERENA
source: 1950 estate; death notice 6746/71; and three Marist Brothers testimonials, St Joseph's College, Belmont Park, Rondebosch, 1936 (family papers, supplied 8 October 2026); and Land Records: South Africa, Farm Records 1895-1955 - image ark 3:1:3QHK-F7NW-L7PV, full-text transcript read 9 October 2026; and Land Records: South Africa, Farm Records 1895-1955 - lot 210, London Street, transfer 2257(7) of 22 August 1953; image 216, ark 3:1:3QHK-N7NW-G375 - FULL-TEXT found and PLATE READ 9 October 2026; and his birth, marriage and death certificates, identity card (Pretoria 1-9-58), headstone photograph and a 1997 letter (family papers, supplied 13 October 2026)
note: Son. David's grandfather. *** PLACE FIELD CORRECTED 14 September 2026. *** This row's 'where found' held a CITATION - "SA records" - where the atlas expects a PLACE, so this person was missing from the map and appeared on it as a phantom location instead. The citation is kept here; the field now holds a real place. *** AND HE WAS AT SCHOOL AT RONDEBOSCH IN 1936, established 8 October 2026. *** Three printed *** Testimonials of Application and Diligence *** from *** MARIST BROTHERS, ST JOSEPH'S COLLEGE, BELMONT PARK, RONDEBOSCH ***, each made out to *** Master N. Lerena *** and signed by the Principal, *** Bro. Vital ***: 1 June 1936 (608 good marks against an opponent's 578, form's highest 690), 1 October 1936 (458 against 415, highest 523) and 1 November 1936 (715 against 708, highest 1045). *** HE IS THE ONLY N. LERENA OF SCHOOL AGE IN THIS FAMILY *** - born 6 October 1924, so eleven turning twelve across the three. *** WHAT THEY ADD: *** the first evidence of any Lerena's schooling; the family placed at Rondebosch in the twelve months after his mother died at Observatory in November 1935; and a *** Roman Catholic education ***, which sits beside the Corpus Christi baptisms and the Roman Catholic allotment of grave 7719. *** AND EVERY FIGURE WAS CONFIRMED *** when David put the scans in the archive later the same day: the 608 of June and the 715 of November, the two digits this archive had flagged as least certain, both held. The certificates are published on /family-papers/. *** AND HE IS IN A SOUTH AFRICAN LAND RECORD, found 9 October 2026 - the first this archive has found for anybody in this family. *** The transcript reads '... Cologne Road . Description of Property ... No. 245 ... Sq. Roods 6,600 Sq. Feet . *** Huno Fernando Lerena 6. 10. 1924 *** . Purchase Amount'. *** 'Huno' IS THE TRANSCRIBER'S NUNO, and 6.10.1924 IS HIS BIRTH DATE TO THE DAY ***, which is what identifies the entry as his. *** WHAT IT DOES NOT YET GIVE: *** the town. Cologne Road, lot 245, 6,600 square feet and a transferor read as 'Gough Cooper' are all the transcript offers, and the plate has not been opened. *** NOTE WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT OVERTURN: *** /south-africa/ says a search of the deeds registers returns no land at all - that was said of *** PABLO ARMANDO ***, is still true of him, and was never tested on his sons. *** A SECOND PROPERTY, 9 October 2026, read off the plate. *** Beside lot 245 in *** Cologne Road *** (6,600 sq ft) he holds '*** No. 210 ... 14,560 Sq. Feet ... Transferor: T/SHIP OWNERS ... Transferee: NUNO FERNANDO LERENA. 6.10.24 ***', under a street written *** LENDIN *** - *** SO WRITTEN, AND NOT RESOLVED; THIS ROW READ IT 'LONDON' FOR AN HOUR AND THAT IS WITHDRAWN *** - transfer 2257(7) *** dated 22 August 1953 ***. *** BOUGHT FROM THE TOWNSHIP OWNERS ***, which is how a new township sells its first stands. *** THE TRANSCRIBERS CALLED HIM 'HUNO' ON ONE FOLIO AND 'JAN FERNANDO' ON THE OTHER; THE CLERK WROTE NUNO BOTH TIMES, PLAINLY. *** *** AND THE DATE BESIDE HIS NAME IS AN IDENTITY DATE, NOT A TRANSFER DATE: *** this folio carries the transfer date in its own column (22.8.53), so 6.10.24 is his birth date - which the 1950 estate and death notice 6746/71 held before either land record was found. *** AND THE TOWNSHIP IS PLACED, FROM THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN FILES: *** his death notice *** MHG 6746/71 ***, read 16 September 2026, gives his residence as '*** 24 LEIDEN ROAD, GERDVIEW, GERMISTON ***', and *** COLOGNE ROAD IS A STREET IN GERDVIEW ***. *** SO HE BOUGHT TWO STANDS IN THE TOWNSHIP HE LIVED AND DIED IN ***, whose streets are named for Dutch and German cities - Leiden, Weert, Cologne. *** AND THAT SCHEME IS WHAT EXPOSED THE MISREADING: *** 'London' did not belong to it. *** HIS DEATH NOTICE ALSO NAMES NO PARENTS: *** father and mother are both blank, marked only 'Deceased' - so the one document of his that could have named *** PABLO ARMANDO *** does not. *** HIS OWN PAPERS, supplied by David 13 October 2026: ***  birth certificate A 042921 (Wynberg entry 664/24, born Sixth October 1924 at Wynberg, parents' race 'Spanish and European', issued 8 September 1954 - four weeks before he turned thirty); abridged marriage certificate 616593 (*** married 15 January 1949 at Johannesburg *** to Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen, he 24 and she 19, Catholic); abridged death certificate A 243689 (died 1 July 1971 at Germiston, coronary thrombosis, four hours, Dr Lieberberg); identity card Pretoria 1-9-58 no. 331 406051 W (the SAME NUMBER as the 1971 death notice, which settles that it is his); and the headstone, which calls him *** NUNO FERNANDO (LARRY) *** - a nickname this archive had not met. *** ONE DIGIT IN CONFLICT: *** the death certificate reads 331-406057 against 331 406051 W on the card and the notice; 051 stands on two sources, the certificate is not shown to be the one in error. *** A LETTER OF 21 AUGUST 1997 *** from Gavin Knott to Nuno's son Paul says Nuno and 'Cardo' lived at the Newlands house while at Marist Brothers College, Rondebosch; that Nuno spent about two years at Stellenbosch; that he 'joined the Air Force and served in the Western Desert'; and that Rose Theys was the writer's aunt. The Rondebosch statement agrees with the 1936 testimonials; the service is a recollection with no record seen; and the letter's 'married in Cape Town, then moved to Johannesburg' is contradicted by the certificate, which has the marriage AT Johannesburg. Detail on /family-papers/ and below. *** MORE OF HIS PAPERS, 13 October 2026: *** the printed wedding invitation confirms *** Saturday 15 January 1949 at St Joseph's, Mayfair ***, 'youngest son of Mr and the late Mrs R. Lerena' (his father alive, his mother dead since 1935), with Nuno of Mayfair and Catherine of Brakpan. A July 1971 notice from *** '12th Squadron, S.A.A.F.' *** supports the Air Force service the 1997 letter recalls - a unit, not a record. A 1971 cutting says he founded the tennis club at St Joseph's Convent in 1959 and chaired it; the family's thank-you card gives the house as 24 Leiden *** Street ***, the estate notice 'Road'.

name: Gilberto LERENA (Gilberto Justiniano LERENA LENGUAS)
occupation: CORREDOR DE COMERCIO (commercial broker), per the 1895 census; breeder and co-founder of the Argentine Stud Book
source: 1895 Argentine national census, Seccion 21; and baptism act No. 1447 of 31 Oct 1886, San Francisco de Asis - IMAGE READ; and baptism of his son Raul Alfredo Luis, Catedral Basilica de Montevideo, 10 Sep 1885 - IMAGE READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-BQZD-W
note: *** Co-founder of the Argentine Stud Book; a Group 1 at Palermo renamed for him in 1914. A Lerena at the centre of Argentine thoroughbred breeding, in the right country at the right time - and PABLO ARMANDO TRAINED AND OWNED RACEHORSES. *** Born Montevideo 24 May 1855, died 8 December 1912. His father is now documented rather than asserted: his brother Luis Eugenio's marriage act of 19 December 1864 names their parents as Don Luis and Dona Justiniana Lenguas. That he and Luis Eugenio are BROTHERS still rests on published genealogy, not on an act, and is marked secondary on the charts. *** NO PROVEN LINK TO PABLO ARMANDO. *** *** HIS PARENTS ARE NOW NAMED, 13 September 2026: LUIS LERENA and JUSTINIANA LENGUAS. *** Two independent Uruguayan parish records, entered for two different children of his, both give his parents so. That makes him A BROTHER OF LUIS EUGENIO LERENA LENGUAS - the same Montevideo household that produced the one Lerena baptism in Rosario before 1879. The racing dynasty and the Rosario thread are the same family. *** THE IMAGE IS NOW OPENED, AND IT IS PRIMARY. *** Act 1447 of 31 October 1886 baptises his daughter Maria Angelica Julia, "hija legitima de Don Gilberto Lerena y de Dona Julia Salvanach, orientales", and names the paternal grandparents "Don LUIS y Dona JUSTINIANA LENGUAS" - the same couple named as Luis Eugenio's parents in his marriage act of 1864 and his death act of 1901. *** AND THE GODMOTHER IS DONA JULIA JUANICO DE LERENA - Luis Eugenio's own wife, standing at the font for her husband's brother's daughter. *** The two households are one family acting as one. Written by Martin Perez, the same priest who wrote act 1720 for Candido Jaime that year. *** AND A SECOND ACT, FROM A DIFFERENT PARISH, SAYS THE SAME, 14 September 2026: *** the baptism of his son Raul Alfredo Luis at the Catedral Basilica on 10 September 1885 gives "abuelos paternos: Luis y Justiniana Lenguas" and "abuelos maternos: Cristobal y Angela Alvarez" - identical to act 1447, in a different year, a different parish and a different priest's hand. Its godmother is a JOSEFA LERENA otherwise unknown to this archive. *** HIS HOUSEHOLD IS NOW ASSEMBLED, 14 September 2026: EIGHT CHILDREN by Julia Salvanach *** - Gilberto (1878), Carlos (1884), Raul Alfredo Luis (1885), Maria Angelica Julia (1886), all born at Montevideo; then Maria Carlota (1890), Luis Felipe (1892), Cesar Alberto (1896) and Horacio Alfredo (1898), at Buenos Aires. *** THE LAST MONTEVIDEO BAPTISM IS 31 OCTOBER 1886 AND THE FIRST BUENOS AIRES ONE 29 OCTOBER 1890, which brackets the family's crossing between those dates *** - firmer than the "1887 to 1889" this archive read off census birthplaces. AND JUAN CARLOS IS NOT AMONG THEM. *** AND THE 1895 CENSUS SCHEDULE, READ AS A HOUSEHOLD FOR THE FIRST TIME ON 14 September 2026, GIVES HIM A TRADE: CORREDOR DE COMERCIO - a commercial broker, aged 41, casado, R. Oriental, catolico. *** This archive has had him as a breeder, which is what he is remembered for; in his own house he told the enumerator he was a broker.

He is *** 'Oriental, soltero' *** - Uruguayan and a bachelor - and the third banns were dispensed by *** Don Jacinto Vera, Vicario Apostolico. *** *** THE MACHINE INDEX OF THIS SAME ACT IS WRONG ABOUT THE BRIDE: *** it gives her a father called 'Cristobal LERENA'. The page shows *** Cristobal is a SALVANACH, her own father ***, and the surname Lerena was carried across from the padrino line. *** There is no Cristobal Lerena. ***

name: Carlos Augusto Federico LERENA Salvanach (b. 9 July 1883)
source: Informacion matrimonial, Arzobispado de Buenos Aires, Nuestra Senora del Socorro (Retiro), folio 44, 25 March 1914 - IMAGE READ; ark 3:1:939D-GD76-B; and Uruguayan civil registration and baptism giving the birth of 9 July 1883; and CEMLA, arrival Buenos Aires from Montevideo 27 May 1926
note: *** IMAGE READ 14 September 2026, and two things this row got wrong are now fixed. *** It called the record a "Retiro BAPTISM"; it is an INFORMACION MATRIMONIAL, the sworn pre-marriage enquiry. And it read the father as ALBERTO, guessing GILBERTO - *** the act says GILBERTO plainly, so the guess can stop being a guess. *** "Don Carlos Lerena, natural de la Rep. Oriental, bautizado en la Iglesia de el CORDON, Dep. de Montevideo, de treinta anos, soltero, domiciliado en Pueyrredon 1750, hijo de D. Gilberto Lerena y de Dona Julia Salvanach." He married ROSA MARIA EPPENS. This IDENTIFIES the CEMLA couple 'Carlos Lerena 41 Uruguayan' and 'Rosa M. E. Lerena 39 Argentine' arriving Buenos Aires from Montevideo 27 May 1926 - two independent sources, same couple. *** AND IT NAMES WHERE HIS BAPTISM IS: the Iglesia del CORDON, Montevideo *** - a third Montevideo parish for this family, after San Francisco de Asis and the Catedral Basilica. *** THREE REGISTER ROWS WERE THIS ONE MAN, MERGED 20 September 2026. *** This archive had him as "Carlos Augusto Federico LERENA" (born 9 July 1883, from Uruguayan civil registration), as "Carlos LERENA Salvanach" (the 1914 informacion matrimonial), and as "Carlos LERENA (b.1885, arr. 1926)" (the CEMLA crossing). *** The note above had already identified the second with the third - "two independent sources, same couple" - and the rows were never joined. *** The arithmetic settles the first: the act of 25 March 1914 calls him *** "de treinta anos" ***, and a man born 9 July 1883 is exactly thirty that March. Same parents, same birthplace, same city, and the CEMLA wife "Rosa M. E. Lerena" is *** ROSA MARIA EPPENS ***, whom the act names. And the merge exposed a file disagreeing with the register. The 1914 act calls him *** SOLTERO *** at thirty, while data/relations.tsv gave him a wife ADELA CAMIGLIA and a son AVELINO CARLOS baptised at Mendoza in 1904. *** That contradiction was already settled here and the relations file had not been told: *** the row for ROSA MARIA EPPENS has said since 14 September that her Carlos is *** NOT *** Adela Camiglia's - "two men, one name, and the register now says so on both rows". It said so on the register rows and not on the edges. The Mendoza man now has a row of his own and the edges point at him.

name: Felisa LERENA (arr. 1911)
source: CEMLA, ship INDIANA from Barcelona; and Parroquia y Vicaria de San Jose de Flores, Comuna 7, Buenos Aires City - BAPTISM No. 461 of 10 November 1912 - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:939D-G6VB-K
note: Travelling with Gregorio. *** A CANDIDATE FOR THE FELISA OF A 1912 BUENOS AIRES BAPTISM, found 11 October 2026. *** The act: *** 'PARROQUIA Y VICARIA DE SAN JOSE DE FLORES. Numero 461, Ano de 1912. En diez de Noviembre del ano del Senor mil novecientos doce, el Presbitero Don ANTONIO JENARA, por el infrascrito Cura de esta Parroquia, bautizo solemnemente, puso oleo y crisma a JUANA, que nacio el dia veinte y cinco de Junio del ano de mil novecientos doce, hija legitima de D. ELOY LERENA, natural de ESPANA, de veinte y seis anos de edad, y de Dona FELISA LERENA, natural de Espana, de veinte y un anos de edad.' *** Godparents *** GREGORIO LERENA *** and *** ROSA DEFENARI ***. *** AND THIS IS WHERE A CEMLA ARRIVAL MIGHT BECOME A LIFE - BUT IT IS NOT MERGED. *** This register holds a *** FELISA LERENA and a GREGORIO LERENA who landed together at Buenos Aires on 7 DECEMBER 1911 ***, off the *** INDIANA from BARCELONA ***, and nothing else about either of them. A Felisa and a Gregorio stand in this act eleven months later in a Buenos Aires parish. *** THE RESEMBLANCE IS REAL AND THE ARITHMETIC IS NOT CLEAN. *** The act makes Felisa *** twenty-one ***, so born about *** 1891 ***; the 1911 passenger list makes her *** 1893 ***, two years out - while the archive's OTHER Felisa, who arrived in 1923, is recorded *** 1891 ***, which matches exactly and belongs to a woman arriving eleven years too late to baptise this child unless she crossed twice. *** AND THE ROLES DO NOT LINE UP: *** the 1911 pair travelled together, which usually means husband and wife or brother and sister, but here Gregorio is the *** GODFATHER *** and the husband is *** ELOY ***, who is not on that passenger list at all. *** NOTHING IS MERGED. *** Stated so that the next session tests it rather than inherits it.

name: Juan Jose LERENA
source: CEMLA, three crossings; and Registros Consulares: Buenos Aires City - NOTARIAL RECORDS 1900-1901, folio 138, escritura No. 368 of 14 November 1900, CONSULADO DE ESPANA EN BUENOS AIRES - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:3QHV-G3XJ-XCR6
note: Made the crossing at least three times. *** AND A MAN OF HIS NAME, HIS PROVINCE AND HIS TRADE IS DOCUMENTED IN BUENOS AIRES IN 1900 - 11 October 2026. *** The Spanish consulate's notarial register holds a power of attorney granted by *** 'los hermanos Don Prudencio Benito y Don JUAN JOSE LERENA Y LERENA, mayores de edad, SOLTEROS, DEPENDIENTES, naturales de NAVARRETE, provincia de LOGRONO, vecinos de esta Capital' ***. *** EVERY ATTRIBUTE THIS ROW HAS, THAT ACT HAS TOO: *** the forename pair, the province, soltero, the commercial trade, residence in Buenos Aires, and an age that fits - a man born 1876 was 24 in November 1900, which is what 'mayor de edad, soltero, dependiente' describes. *** NOT MERGED, AND THIS IS THE STRONGEST UNMERGED CANDIDACY IN THIS REGISTER. *** CEMLA records a birthplace by *** PROVINCE, NOT VILLAGE ***, so 'Logrono' does not confirm Navarrete, and Juan Jose is a common pair of names. The archive keeps the two rows apart for the same reason it kept Vicente Lerena Diaz apart, and says so rather than quietly collapsing them. *** IF THEY ARE ONE MAN, HE WAS A BACHELOR SHOP-ASSISTANT IN BUENOS AIRES AT 24 AND STILL A BACHELOR IN TRADE, CROSSING TO SPAIN, AT 52. ***

name: Gilberto LERENA (b.1879, arr. 1928)
source: CEMLA, ship CAP. NORTE
note: *** An ARGENTINE-national Lerena born within three years of Pablo Armando, carrying the Gilberto name of the Stud Book family. Travelling with a son of the same name. *** *** CORRECTED 20 September 2026. *** This row used to end "Not in the 1895 census household of Gilberto (1854)", and that was the only thing holding it apart from another row in this register. *** It is wrong. *** Line 6 of that schedule reads *** Salvanach Lerena, GILBERTO, varon, 17, soltero, R. Oriental *** - Gilberto's eldest son, seventeen in 1895, so born 1877 or 1878, who is already here as *** Gilberto LERENA Salvanach (the younger, b.1878) ***. *** WHAT FITS, NOW THAT THE OBJECTION IS GONE: *** a birth year one out; Argentine nationality, which the Salvanach son demonstrably holds (Montevideo-born, yet in Argentine military records 1911-1936); Buenos Aires; and a marriage of 19 May 1906, against which a son born 1916 sits naturally - and that son is the *** estudiante *** of twelve travelling beside him, whom this row had noted as a curiosity without explaining. *** DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED. *** Both rows are index-level, and this archive once conflated two Arturo Lerenas on a forename and an age and retracted the branch within the hour. *** THE TEST, AND IT IS CHEAP: *** the Argentine military record carries a date of birth and the CEMLA entry carries marital status. Either one settles it. *** AND THE SON IS NO LONGER A CURIOSITY, 20 September 2026. *** Gilberto Lerena Salvanach married CIPRIANA SAENZ PENA on 19 May 1906 and a Capital Federal index names their child *** "Gilberto de Jesus del Corazon" ***. The son this row noted without explaining is a son that man demonstrably had. *** IT STILL DOES NOT CLOSE. *** That child carries no indexed birth year - a search of Argentine Lerena births 1910-1920 returns ten records and none is he - so the twelve-year-old of 1928 remains unmatched by a document.

The act calls her *** 'hija legitima' ***, so he and Maria Mercedes Razzetti were married before January 1921. *** AND THERE IS AN EDUARDO LERENA IN THIS REGISTER WHO WAS DISPENSED BANNS AT MONTEVIDEO ON 22 DECEMBER 1919 to marry a MARIA MERCEDES *** - 'RAZZELLO' in that transcript, 'RAZZETTI' on this plate, the same hand read twice. *** THIRTEEN MONTHS BETWEEN THE DISPENSATION AND THE CHILD. *** *** NOT MERGED, AND THE REASON IS NOT DOUBT ABOUT THE ARITHMETIC: *** no act yet read says this man came from Las Piedras, and this archive has been wrong before about two men of one name. name: Careen Maria LERENA
source: South Africa, Cape, Cemetery Records, 1872-2011; and Maitland Road Cemetery, Record of Interments, page 4706, entry 423 - IMAGE READ 8 October 2026. *** IMAGE SUPPLIED *** by David, not fetched from a film: there is no DGS number and no ark to give, and the page and entry number above are the locator a reader would use to order the same opening; FamilySearch image group 102346234 ('Maitland Cemetery Volume 19', Cemetery Records 1946-1947), image 208 of 255, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSVY-JS81; index ark 1:1:QP7Z-K7B8
note: Died 27 June 1947, buried in the Cape. Almost certainly of this family - the Cape Lerenas are one cluster - but no record yet ties her to a parent. Found 10 Sep 2026. *** HER INTERMENT ENTRY WAS READ ON 8 OCTOBER 2026, and it moves the grave. *** Maitland Road Cemetery, Record of Interments, *** page 4706, entry 423 ***. The line reads: surname *** LERENA ***, forename as this register has carried it, *** FE ***, age *** 2 WKS ***, late residence ending '...Victoria R[oa]d'; allotment *** ROMAN CATHOLIC ***, Cons. No. *** 1 ***, *** GRAVE 7719 ***. *** THAT IS MARY SEPTIMA TAYLOR'S GRAVE. *** This archive already held her burial as 'Maitland Road Cemetery interment register p.3215 entry 163, Nov 1935 ... Cemetery no 1, grave 7719A' - the same cemetery, the same allotment, the same number. A baby of two weeks was laid in the grave of a woman who had died twelve years before her. *** AND IT IS MAITLAND, NOT NEWLANDS. *** Work-list row 106 records the family's account, from the cemetery office via a sister, Patricia, of an unmarked grave at *** NEWLANDS *** carrying only the word LERENA and holding three people. The register puts these two at *** MAITLAND ROAD ***. *** WHAT IS NOT SETTLED BY THIS PAGE: *** whether Pablo Armando is there too. He died in 1950 and this opening is 1947, so he is not on it. *** THE FORENAME COULD NOT BE RESOLVED. *** The scan is about 1,100 pixels across a whole opening, and at that resolution 'Careen' and 'Carmen' cannot be told apart - CARMEN would be the commoner name in this family by far. The reading this register already carried is kept, and the doubt is recorded rather than resolved in favour of the likelier guess. *** THE PLATE WAS RE-READ AT FULL RESOLUTION ON 8 OCTOBER 2026 and three things changed. *** *** THE GRAVE IS 7719 B, not 7719. *** Mary Septima is 7719 A and Pablo Armando is 7719 C: this is one plot with lettered places in it, and the register names it *** 'In Plot of R. P. Lerina' ***. *** SHE WAS BURIED IN HIS GRAVE. *** That is evidence she was his, and it is not proof - a plot holder may bury a grandchild, a servant's child or a lodger's. *** THE NAME IS CAREEN, NOT CARMEN. *** The doubt recorded earlier the same day was answered by the clerk's own hand: the letter in dispute is the pointed r he writes in *** Frederick *** two lines below, and is not the three-arch m he writes in *** mary *** one line below. Carmen was the likelier name and it is not what the page says. *** AND HER LAST RESIDENCE WAS 42 VICTORIA ROAD, BELLVILLE *** - not 7 Forth Road, Newlands, where Pablo Armando and his executrix Rose Lilian Theys both lived. The family's reading that Rose Lilian Theys was the mother now has a fact to answer: the child died at an address in a different suburb. *** THE REST OF THE LINE: *** Roman Catholic allotment, Cemetery No. 1, depth 3 1/2 feet, officiating Bosman, undertaker Human - and Human & Pitt appears as a firm elsewhere on the same page, which is worth noting beside Mary Septima's undertaker in 1935, *** L. Pitt ***, without being pressed into a conclusion. *** AND THE REGISTER IS NOW EXHAUSTED ON HER PARENTS, 9 October 2026. *** Every column of the 1947 opening was catalogued from the header row: *** No | DATE | NAME | SEX | AGE (Years, Months) | LATE RESIDENCE (Town or Village, Street) | [CAUSE OF DEATH - REDACTED by FamilySearch] | DATE OF DEATH | BY WHOM CERTIFIED *** on the left page, and *** ALLOTMENT | Cem. No. | No. of Grave | Depth Below Surface | POSITION | Officiating Minister | UNDERTAKER | PARTICULARS OF BURIAL *** on the right. *** THERE IS NO INFORMANT COLUMN AND NO PARENT COLUMN. *** Her 'By whom certified' cell is BLANK; her date of death reads *** 27 *** , confirming the index. *** ONE NEAR MISS WORTH RECORDING: *** this register DOES name a parent when a child has no name of its own - entry 430 on the same page reads *** 'Gordon, Child of ...' *** - so the convention exists and she falls outside it precisely because somebody had named her. *** THE CAPE CIVIL REGISTRATION IS NOW THE ONLY ROUTE LEFT ***, and FamilySearch's full-text search does not reach South Africa.

name: Maria Julia Margarita Josefa Emirena Justiniana LERENA Juanico (m. HERRERA)
source: Rosario baptism, Libro 15 folio 229, act 1541, bapt. 17 Feb 1866; Montevideo marriage, San Francisco de Asis, act 1879, 3 Nov 1886; and La Union religious marriage register act 90, 30 June 1913 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-T7P2-W - IMAGE READ 21 September 2026; film 007713384 image 00700, folio 492
note: *** The only LERENA baptised at Rosario between 1731 and 1901 - and now followed to the end of the story. *** Born 8 October 1865, baptised at Rosario 17 February 1866 to Don Luis Lerena Lenguas and Dona Julia Juanico, "naturales del E. Oriental". On 3 November 1886, aged 21, she married Don Jaime Herrera at San Francisco de Asis, Ciudad Vieja, MONTEVIDEO - the act naming her parents again, in a second country, twenty years later. She went home. *** NOT the Maria Lerena who was Pablo Armando's mother: that woman had a son in February 1882, when this one was sixteen and four years from marrying someone else. *** *** HER SURNAME IS CORRECTED HERE, 14 September 2026, and an act says so. *** This register called her *** LERENA LENGUAS *** - which is her FATHER'S compound, not hers. Her father was Luis Lerena Lenguas; her mother was Julia Juanico; *** so she is LERENA JUANICO, exactly as her siblings Ema Sixta and Candido Jaime are already named on their own rows here. *** She was the odd one out and nothing had caught it. *** THE EVIDENCE IS THE ACT READ TODAY: *** at her sister Ema Sixta's wedding on 30 June 1913 the witnesses are written *** "Don Jaime Herrera y Dona Maria Perena Juanico de Herrera" *** - her own compound, in her own lifetime, with PERENA the machine's usual mangling of LERENA on this family. *** IT ALSO MATTERED FOR THE CHECKING: *** the compound-surname sibling test keys on the two surnames in a row's name, so while she read LERENA LENGUAS she was being grouped with her father's generation instead of with her own brothers and sisters.  *** READ OFF THE PLATE 21 September 2026, and the citation on this row needed explaining rather than correcting. *** Film 007713384 image 00700, folio 492, act *** No. 90 *** of the Union marriage register: *** 'MASSERA, Jose Pedro = con = EMMA SIXTA LERENA. El TREINTA DE JUNIO de mil novecientos TRECE ... el Presbitero Monsenor Don EUSEBIO DE LEON, con licencia del ... Iglesia Metropolitana ...' *** *** SO ACT 90 IS HER SISTER'S WEDDING, NOT HERS *** - which this register knew, because Ema Sixta's own row carries the same act. This row cites it because she is IN it. *** THE PLATE CONFIRMS IT AND CONFIRMS HER MARRIED NAME: 'Don LUIS LERENA ... FUERON TESTIGOS, do[na] ... JUANICO DE HERRERA' *** - she signs as a Herrera wife, which is the only thing on any plate read here that supports the '(m. HERRERA)' in her own row's title. *** A CITATION THAT LOOKS WRONG AND IS NOT: *** the act number belongs to her sister and the row is right to name it, because a witness clause is where a married woman's surname gets written down.

name: Don Luis Eugenio LERENA LENGUAS
source: Montevideo civil death registration No. 216, 24 December 1901 - IMAGE READ; plus Rosario baptism act 1541 (1866) and Montevideo marriage act 258 (1864); and his own baptism, La Mauricia, Villa de la Union, 7 Jan 1846 - IMAGE READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-ZS62-J; and the Montevideo Direccion de Cementerios mortality return for December 1901 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3QHK-XQ11-BC6G
note: *** DOCUMENTED, 13 September 2026. *** "Natural de esta Republica", married Dona Julia Juanico at San Francisco de Asis, Ciudad Vieja, Montevideo, on 19 December 1864 - act 258, image read - which names him "hijo legitimo de Don Luis y de Dona Justiniana Lenguas". His daughter Laura Adela's baptism of 1869 names the same two as her paternal grandparents, independently. So his parentage is PRIMARY, not the tree assertion it was that morning; and it makes him a brother of GILBERTO JUSTINIANO LERENA LENGUAS, co-founder of the Argentine Stud Book - though THAT brotherhood still rests on published genealogy rather than an act, and is marked secondary on the chart. Five children, all on primary records. Died before 11 July 1910, when his widow's death was registered. *** NO LINK TO JUAN CARLOS LERENA HAS BEEN SHOWN. *** *** HIS DEATH IS FOUND: 24 DECEMBER 1901, at seven in the morning, at the house calle Suarez No. 25 in el Paso del Molino, Montevideo. *** Act 216. "De nacionalidad oriental, nacido en Montevideo, de cincuenta y seis [anos], de estado casado, y de profesion HACENDADO" - a landowner, which is the first statement of this family's standing anywhere in the archive. He died of pulmonary tuberculosis, certified by Dr Scremini. *** IT WAS HIDING UNDER A MISSPELLING: *** FamilySearch indexes him as Luis SERENA Lenguas, so every search under LERENA missed him, including a 1,502-row sweep of Montevideo Lerena deaths run the same morning. He was found by searching for his MOTHER. The act also says his father Luis Lerena was already dead, and that his mother Justiniana Lenguas was ALIVE AT 79 and staying in the same house. *** HIS OWN BAPTISM IS NOW READ: born 9 FEBRUARY 1843, baptised 7 January 1846 at the Capilla de la Mauricia, Villa de la Union. *** "Hijo legitimo de Luis Lerena y Justiniana Lenguas, ORIENTALES. Paternos: Francisco y Maria Fernandez. Maternos: Pedro y Carmen Gonzalez." Godparents Juan Lenguas and Maria Fernandez. His death act of 1901 gave his age as 56, implying 1845; the act of his own baptism is the better evidence. *** A THIRD INDEPENDENT RECORD OF THAT DEATH, 14 September 2026: *** the Montevideo cemetery office's own return, "Relacion de los individuos que han fallecido en el mes de Diciembre de 1901", lists him against day 24 between Lucrecia Sosa and Emilia Zanola de Sanchez. *** So he was BURIED AT MONTEVIDEO, and the date now rests on three documents - the civil act, the cemetery roll, and his widow's sworn statement of 1908. *** Found only by searching the COMPOUND surname. *** A CONTRADICTION INSIDE THE REGISTER ITSELF, recorded 14 September 2026 and NOT resolved. *** Luis Eugenio's act says he was born 9 FEBRUARY 1843; his sister Justiniana Mauricia Maxima's act, the entry immediately before his on the same page in the same hand, says she was born 30 JULY 1843. *** That is FIVE AND A HALF MONTHS between two full siblings, and both cannot be right. *** Neither is a machine reading: the transcript of each act has been read verbatim, and both say "del pasado ano cuarenta y tres". *** THE ERROR IS IN THE SOURCE, NOT IN THIS ARCHIVE. *** Every act on that page is a LATER TRANSCRIPT copied out of a legajo by order of Bishop Jacinto Vera - a clerk working from loose papers three years after the events, who had already written "ano cuarenta y tres" twice on the same page. A carried-forward year is the likeliest explanation and it is a guess. Luis Eugenio's death registration of 1901 gives an age and has been read; testing it against 1843 is the next step. *** AND THE CONTRADICTION IS RESOLVED THE SAME AFTERNOON - AGAINST HIS OWN BAPTISM ACT. *** Three facts, two of them already in this archive: (1) his baptism act says he was born 9 February of "el pasado ano cuarenta y tres"; (2) his sister Justiniana Mauricia's act, THE ENTRY IMMEDIATELY ABOVE HIS IN THE SAME HAND, says she was born 30 July 1843 - five and a half months before him, which is impossible; (3) *** his civil death registration of 24 December 1901 gives his age as FIFTY-SIX, which puts his birth at about 1845. *** Two independent constraints point to 1845 and only one points to 1843 - and the one is a clerk copying loose papers three years after the fact, who wrote "ano cuarenta y tres" in the entry above this one and again in the entry below. *** A YEAR CARRIED FORWARD DOWN A COLUMN IS THE ORDINARY WAY THIS ERROR HAPPENS, and it is the only reading under which his sister's date, his own death record and his baptism can all stand. *** *** SO THIS ROW NOW CARRIES 9 FEBRUARY 1845. *** The day and month are secure and are not in question; only the year moved. The act's own words are kept above and in data/1846-la-mauricia-page.tsv, because the source says 1843 and a reader is entitled to see that this archive overruled it and why. *** THIS IS AN INFERENCE, NOT A DOCUMENT *** - an age at death is the weakest date in genealogy and this archive has said so in print; it is load-bearing here only because it agrees with a constraint reached independently of it.

note: Daughter of Dr Candido Juanico and Dona Juliana Gonzalez. Married Luis Eugenio Lerena Lenguas at San Francisco de Asis, Montevideo, 19 December 1864. *** DIED 11 JULY 1910 at calle Constituyente 992, Montevideo, aged sixty-six, A WIDOW *** - which dates her husband's death to before that. *** HER BAPTISM IS FOUND AND THE IMAGE READ: born 23 November 1842 at Montevideo, christened 4 October 1843 at San Francisco de Asis *** - the same parish where she married in 1864, where her son Candido Jaime was baptised in 1886, and where her daughter Maria married that November. Her mother is given in full as JULIANA JOAQUINA GONZALEZ; godparents D. Enrique Juanico and Mercedes Gonzalez. Her death registration estimated 1844 from a stated age of 66; she was 67. *** HER BURIAL ENTRY IS READ, 17 October 2026: *** 'El doce de julio de mil novecientos diez se mando dar sepultura eclesiastica al cadaver de Julia Juanico de Lerena, oriental, de sesenta y dos [anos], viuda de Luis Lerena Lenguas. note: *** NOW PARTLY PRIMARY. *** The Uruguayan census records him at Calle San Juan, Montevideo, aged 45, birthplace "ANDALUZIA", with MARIA FERNANDEZ on the line below - image opened and read. Six further indexed records name the same wife and the same children while spelling him LLERENA, LERENA, SANCIO LLERENA, D. SANCHO LERENA and LORENA. So the alternation is in the RECORDS, not in a tree. That they are all one man is still an inference, and Cordoba specifically still rests on the tree alone. *** ORIGINALLY RECORDED AS SECONDARY. *** The founder of the Montevideo Lerenas on the tree's account: a soldier from Cordoba who married Maria Josefa Fernandez Tresguerras at Canelones, 8 January 1791. His name is spelled BOTH Lerena and Llerena across forty years of Uruguayan registers, and once - in 1828 - "Sancho de Llerena". The acts have NOT been opened here. *** HE IS NOW ON AN ACT, 13 September 2026, and no longer only on an index and a published tree. *** Act 585 of 7 October 1850 names the paternal grandparents of Alberto Octavio Lerena as "D. SANCHO y Dona MARIA FERNANDEZ" - so Sancho really is the father of Don Luis Lerena, and the descent this archive marked SECONDARY is upgraded. A DISCREPANCY RECORDED AGAINST IT: two 1846 acts for other children of the same couple give the paternal grandfather as FRANCISCO, not Sancho. Those 1846 entries are LATER TRANSCRIPTS copied out of a legajo ("asi consta del Legajo conservado en este Archivo, mandado trasladar por el Sr. Obispo"), while the 1850 act is a contemporaneous parish entry - so the copy loses to the original. Everything else in both sets agrees. *** AND A THIRD ACT NAMES HIM, 14 September 2026 - the earliest yet. *** His son's marriage of 3 March 1842 gives the groom as "hijo legitimo de D. SANCHO y Dona Maria Fernandez". Two acts of 1842 and 1850 now say Sancho against two 1846 entries reading Francisco, and the 1846 pair say of themselves that they are later transcripts from a legajo. *** AND A FOURTH RECORD, THE EARLIEST OF ALL: *** his son's own marriage petition of 3 September 1836, in Luis's hand and over Luis's signature - "hijo legitimo de D. SANCHO LERENA y de Dona Maria Fernandez". Four records now name him, across 1836, 1842 and 1850. *** The doubt raised on 13 September by two 1846 transcripts reading "Francisco" is closed: they are copies, and they are outnumbered by originals. *** *** AND TWO MORE RECORDS, 14 September 2026, neither of them about his son Luis. *** (1) He is named maternal grandfather - "SANCHO LLERENA y MARIA FERNANDEZ" - in the Cordon baptism of 13 December 1831, *** at which the godfather was DON FRUCTUOSO RIVERA, PRESIDENT OF THE REPUBLIC, with his wife Dona Bernardina Fragoso. *** (2) He appears in person as a sworn witness in a marriage investigation at Canelones: "presento por testigo en esta Vicaria a SANCHO LLERENA, a quien se le recivio juramento". Five records now name him. *** AND THEN THE QUESTION REOPENED, the same afternoon. *** The Catedral baptism of Justa Pastora's SECOND child, October 1833 - an ORIGINAL act, not a transcript - names her parents "Maternos: FRANCISCO LERINA y Maria Fernandez". So the Sancho/Francisco alternation is not simply copies against originals, which is what this archive argued an hour earlier and has now withdrawn. *** The one thing constant in every record is the wife, MARIA FERNANDEZ. *** A double forename - Sancho Francisco - would explain it all without anybody being wrong, and is the leading reading. See data/sancho-or-francisco.tsv; his own marriage act would settle it and has never been opened. *** AND THE "AGUILAR" IN HIS NAME HERE IS UNATTESTED. *** None of the eight records now assembled gives him a matronymic; a full-text search for "Llerena y Aguilar" returns thirty hits and every one is QUITO, ECUADOR - a different family. Aguilar comes from the FamilySearch Tree and from nowhere this archive has read. Kept, because the tree may rest on an act nobody here has opened, but marked. *** The forename is contested, the matronymic unsupported, and MARIA FERNANDEZ is the only part of this man's identity every record agrees on. *** *** AND HE IS NOW ATTESTED IN 1804, twenty-seven years earlier than anything this archive held two days ago. *** At Canelones on 15 May 1804 his daughter DOMINGA JOSEFA is baptised "hija legitima de SANCHO LLERENA y de MARIA FERNANDEZ"; in the confirmation list of the same year he stands godfather to "Jose, ESCLAVO DE MANUEL LOPEZ"; and in the marriage-investigation files he gives evidence under oath. *** Father, godfather and sworn witness, in one town, in one decade - and every one of those acts calls him SANCHO. *** The machine transcript renders him SANCIO on the baptism, a sixth spelling for this family. *** AND THEN BACK ANOTHER FIFTEEN YEARS, on 14 September 2026: HE IS IN MONTEVIDEO IN 1789. *** At the Iglesia Matriz on 30 June 1789 the godparents of Juana, daughter of "NICOLAS BENTENO, INDIO NATURAL DE LA CIUDAD DEL TUCUMAN, y de Leonarda Correa de Buenos Ayres", are "SANCHO LLERENA y Juliana Josefa Cornejo". *** He is about twenty-two, unmarried, and in Montevideo two years before the marriage his tree places at Canelones in 1791. *** And it is the second time this archive has found him sponsoring at the margins of colonial society: in 1804 he stood godfather to an ENSLAVED MAN, and here to the daughter of an indigenous man from Tucuman. Twice, fifteen years apart. *** THE TALLY IS ALSO REDONE, AND THE ARCHIVE HAD BEEN COUNTING IT WRONG. *** Fourteen records now name him: ten SANCHO, four FRANCISCO. But THREE OF THE FOUR FRANCISCOS ARE THE SAME PAGE - La Mauricia, 7 January 1846, one clerk writing three acts on one morning out of one legajo. They are one witness, not three. The Sanchos come from nine separate occasions across sixty-one years, in four parishes and two towns, and twice with the man himself present. *** So the evidence is not ten to four. It is nine independent occasions against two, and both of the two describe him at second hand by clerks who never met him. That act has still never been opened. And 'AGUILAR' is STILL unattested across all fourteen records. *** *** AND ON 14 SEPTEMBER 2026, GENEANET SUPPLIES THE ONE THING THIS ROW HAS BEEN CALLING UNATTESTED ALL DAY. *** Two Spanish archive indexes - the Index des mariages catholique de Grenade and Spain, Marriages 1565-1950 - carry a marriage of *** SANCHO LERENA y ARMENTA to ANA MARIA DE AGUILAR, in the DIOCESE OF GRANADA, between 1725 and 1775. *** A son of that couple would be styled *** LERENA y AGUILAR *** - which is exactly the name the trees give this man. So the matronymic is not a tree's invention but a real Spanish naming rule, and it points at a GRANDMOTHER. *** NOT ADOPTED: *** the index has been read and the image has not, the date range is a fifty-year span, and no record yet joins that couple to a son born in 1767. *** But it turns an unattested word into a testable claim in a named diocese, and it is the first thing this archive has ever had that could document this family in SPAIN. *** GRANADA also sits against the trees' CORDOBA - one of them, ckurti, says ZUHEROS, CORDOBA - while the census says only ANDALUZIA, which both satisfy. *** AND FOUR TREES GIVE HIM A DEATH IN 1832, *** where this archive has no death date at all; if true, his son's marriage petition of 1836 names a dead man, which is ordinary. Tree-only, and recorded as a thing to test against Montevideo burials. *** AND ON 14 SEPTEMBER 2026 THE GRANADA ACT ITSELF WAS FOUND - BUT READ THE NEXT SENTENCE BEFORE CREDITING THIS ROW WITH IT. *** The birthplaces below belong to a man in SPAIN in 1754, NOT to the Sancho of this row, and nothing yet joins the two. This archive very nearly wrote the Spanish Cordoba into the Uruguayan Sancho's birthplace field on the strength of it; the field above still says CORDOBA COMES ONLY FROM A TREE, and that is still true of THIS man. *** FamilySearch ark 1:1:C9WG-BGW2 indexes the marriage of *** SANCHO DE LERENA Y ARMENTA to ANA MARIA DE AGUILAR at SANTA ANA, GRANADA on 17 NOVEMBER 1754 *** - the fifty-year span reduced to a day - and it gives the groom's BIRTHPLACE AS CORDOBA and his parents as *** SANCHO DE LERENA Y VELASCO and MARIA ANTONIA DE ARMENTA Y GUEBARA ***, with the bride the daughter of FRANCISCO DE AGUILAR and BEATRIS FRANCO of La Malaha. *** That resolves a tension in the SPANISH record - the Geneanet trees said CORDOBA and the marriage index said GRANADA, and both were right, because he was born at one and married at the other. It does NOT reach across the Atlantic. *** The Uruguayan census's "ANDALUZIA" for the man in this row remains the only birthplace evidence this archive has for HIM, and it is compatible with Cordoba, Granada and much else besides. *** The image is marked IMAGE UNAVAILABLE and has NOT been opened. *** AND THE COMPOUND IS NO LONGER A TREE'S HABIT. *** A Madrid notarial act of 27 March 1790 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2C-N7RV) is signed, in the signature position between the witnesses and the notary, *** "JUAN DE LERENA Y AGUILAR" *** - one man, that compound, in the right family and generation, in a Madrid where Sancho de Lerena y Armenta was a vecino from 1766 to 1808. *** BUT NOT ONE RECORD JOINS ANY OF THEM TO THIS MAN. *** A controlled search for children of that couple in Spain returned a genuine null (control: 12 results), and the exact-phrase search for "Sancho de Lerena y Aguilar" returned an UNCONTROLLED "(0)" immediately before FamilySearch blocked the session - *** which is not evidence and is not recorded as a null. *** So "Aguilar" stays exactly where it was: a strong lead with a Spanish family behind it now instead of nothing, and still unattested in all fourteen Uruguayan records. *** The place to look for a 1767 baptism is MADRID, not Granada - the earlier errand said "the same diocese" and was written before the Madrid residence was known. See data/1754-granada-act.tsv. *** *** AND THEN, THE SAME DAY, THE GRANADA READING WAS WITHDRAWN - BY THE VERY TREE THAT SUPPLIES "AGUILAR". *** The jfina Geneanet tree, one of the four this archive cites for the form "Lerena y Aguilar", gives this man's parents as *** FELIX LERENA and ROSALIA AGUILAR ***, born Cordoba about 1767, citing *** APOLANT, "Operativo Patagonia" (Montevideo 1970), FICHA 355 ***. *** So AGUILAR is his MOTHER'S SURNAME - ordinary Spanish naming - and not a grandmother from Granada. *** The morning's inference, that the compound must descend from the 1754 Granada couple, was a naming rule applied to a name whose actual owner is recorded elsewhere; and the controlled null against that couple is explained rather than puzzling. *** The Spanish search that matters now is FELIX LERENA and ROSALIA AGUILAR at CORDOBA, which is not the search that was run. *** AND THE MARRIAGE DATE FINALLY HAS A REAL SOURCE WHILE THE PLACE LOSES ITS ONE: *** 8 January 1791 comes from Apolant ficha 355, a named published work; *** "Canelones" appears nowhere in it *** - the note's "Concejo de Morcin, Asturias" is the BRIDE'S birthplace, she being JOSEFA FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS b.1778 at Morcin, an ASTURIAN of the Operativo Patagonia convoy, daughter of RODRIGO FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS and ROSA FERNANDEZ. *** Canelones remains the strong inference because the 1812 padron lists all six children as "naturales del Canelon", the eldest 21. *** THE 1812 PADRON ALSO HOLDS WHAT THIS ROW DID NOT: *** calle San Juan No 60, Sancho "andaluz" 45, Maria Fernandez 36, children Juan Agustin 21, Pedro Antonio 19, Agustina 17, Fidel 12, Justa 10 and DOMINGA 7 - all "naturales del Canelon" - *** his father-in-law RODRIGO FERNANDEZ, 63, asturiano, living in the house, and FOUR ENSLAVED PEOPLE *** (AGN, Fondo ex AGA, L 251). See data/apolant-ficha-355.tsv. *** AND ON 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 HIS PARENTS ARRIVED ON AN ACT, WHICH CLOSES THE LAST WEAK JOINT IN THIS ROW. *** At the Iglesia Matriz of Montevideo on 10 February 1811, at the baptism of his son LUIS ESCOLASTICO, the act names him *** "Don SANCHO LLERENA natural de ANDALUCIA" *** and his parents *** "Abuelos paternos FELIZ GERENA y ROSALIA AGUILAR" *** - GERENA being the machine's G-for-L, a seventh variant for this family. *** Until that morning FELIX LERENA and ROSALIA AGUILAR rested on ONE un-consulted journal article reported at second hand through one tree, and this row said so. *** *** They are now on a parish act written while he was alive and standing at his own son's font. *** *** ANDALUCIA IS ALSO NOW ON AN ACT *** and no longer only on the 1726-1858 census. *** CORDOBA IS STILL ON NO ACT *** and remains what the trees say, citing Apolant ficha 355. *** AND THE TALLY OF HIS SPONSORSHIPS IS WRONG IN THIS ROW AND IS CORRECTED, 15 September 2026. *** It says he stood godfather at the margins of colonial society "twice, fifteen years apart" - the indigenous man's daughter in 1789 and an enslaved man in 1804. *** It is at least FOUR times, and three of them on one day. *** Three further pages of the 1804 Canelones confirmations name him as padrino, including "Joseph Jimenez ESCLAVO DE DON LUIS JIMENEZ. P. Sancho Llerena" - a different enslaved man with a different owner from the Jose, esclavo de Manuel Lopez, already recorded here. *** The pattern is now too consistent to read as chance. *** *** A NEW CHILD IS ALSO ADDED: JUSTA PASTORA, baptised at Canelones on 9 August 1800, born three days earlier *** - this archive had her only from her 1830 marriage and from the padron's rough age of 10. *** That act transcribes the mother as 'MARIA RODRIGO', which is not her name in any of the other fourteen records. *** The most economical reading is that a clerk wrote her father's forename - RODRIGO Fernandez - and that only became visible once the 1811 act named him. *** The image has not been opened and the discrepancy is left standing. *** *** AND ON 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 THREE MORE ACTS ARRIVED, BECAUSE THE NAME WAS FINALLY SEARCHED WITH ONE L. *** Every full-text sweep here had been run on SANCHO LLERENA. "Sancho LERENA" returns three Canelones baptisms that were not among them. *** HIS RANK: the 1793 act calls him "el SOLDADO DRAGON Sancho Lerena" - a dragoon, where the census says only soldado. *** *** HIS REGIMENT, BY IMPLICATION: that act was performed by "el Capellan del REGIMIENTO DE INFANTERIA DE BUENOS AYRES Don Bartolome Munoz" *** - the same regiment whose Libros Castrenses of 1781-1814 are filmed as DGS 7713373. *** His 1791 marriage may well be in those military books, and the reason to look is now documented rather than hopeful. *** *** HIS WIFE IS CALLED TERESA: *** at a Canelones baptism of 27 October 1805 the godparents are "SANCHO LERENA y MARIA TERESA FERNANDEZ de este Pueblo" - the trees give her as Maria Josefa (TERESA) Fernandez Tresguerras and this archive had marked those forenames tree-only. *** AND THE SPONSORSHIP COUNT RISES AGAIN, to five. *** *** READ OFF THE PLATE 21 September 2026, where this row had rested on a MACHINE TRANSCRIPT since 14 September. *** Film 007713375 image 02410, Iglesia Matriz de Montevideo, the baptism of Luis Escolastico, 10 February 1811 - the only record in this archive that names Sancho's own parents. *** 'hijo legitimo de D.n SANCHO LLERENA nat.l de ANDALUCIA' - read off the plate, not off a transcript. *** The double L is the priest's own, in 1811.  *** THE 1833 ACT THAT CALLS HIM FRANCISCO WAS READ OFF THE PLATE, 21 September 2026 - and that is the whole of what this archive gained today on the question. *** Film 007713376 images 01176-01177: the Catedral baptism of 19 October 1833, for Justa Pastora's son Aurelio Eusebio, gives the maternal grandparents as *** 'Fran.co Lerenas y M.a Fernandez' ***. *** Until today that reading was a MACHINE TRANSCRIPT - the page and data/sancho-or-francisco.tsv both record it as 'FRANCISCO LERINA', machine-read. A human has now read it off the plate, so the single most important FRANCISCO attestation is no longer possibly a machine artefact. *** *** THIS ROW SAID SOMETHING ELSE FOR ABOUT AN HOUR AND IT WAS WRONG. *** It called the Francisco a priest's slip, said 'every other record this archive has read off a plate calls him SANCHO', and put the count at 'one act against five'. *** All three are false, and the archive's own file and /hypotheses/ already said so: *** the 1846 La Mauricia acts were READ OFF THE IMAGE by this archive and say FRANCISCO; the count is SIX saying Sancho against THREE saying Francisco; and the readings split ACROSS methods, not along them - the machine read Sancho in 1831 and Francisco in 1833, this archive read Francisco off 1846 and Sancho off 1836, 1842 and 1850. *** THE ARCHIVE'S POSITION, WHICH THIS ROW NOW MATCHES: a DOUBLE FORENAME - Sancho Francisco or Francisco Sancho - is the reading that requires nobody to be wrong. *** What is constant across seventy years and both forenames is the wife: MARIA FERNANDEZ, in every single record. *** WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT is his own marriage act, said by the tree to be Canelones, 8 January 1791, and never opened. *** *** HE SPEAKS, 11 OCTOBER 2026 - AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME THIS ARCHIVE HAS HEARD HIM. *** Every other record of Sancho holds him as a father, a father of the bride, a spouse or an 'other'. Here he is *** A SWORN WITNESS GIVING TESTIMONY IN HIS OWN VOICE ***, in the marriage investigation of *** FLORENTINO GOMEZ *** before the Juzgado Eclesiastico of Canelones, notary *** JOSEPH DEL RIOS ***. The transcript: *** 'Seguidamente, continuando su informacion, Florentino Gomez presento por testigo en esta Vicaria a SANCHO LLERENA, a quien se le recibio juramento ... el compareciente dijo: Que con motivo de haber andado el declarante EN LA LINEA DE VITORIA algunos anos, que conocio en aquel parage a Florentino Gonzalez, y por el trato y conocimiento que uno y otro han tenido en todo el tiempo que el que declara se ha mantenido en la dicha linea, jamas le oyo decir al nominado Florentino que hubiese empenado su palabra con otra ninguna mujer, ni que tenga algun impedimento publico ni secreto con la que pretende casarse.' *** *** SO HE HAD SPENT SOME YEARS IN SOMETHING CALLED 'LA LINEA DE VITORIA' BEFORE THIS DEPOSITION ***, long enough to know a man well there. *** WHAT THAT PLACE IS, THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT KNOW AND WILL NOT GUESS. *** A 'linea' in the Rio de la Plata is ordinarily a military frontier line; Vitoria is also the capital of Alava in the Basque country and a common place name in Brazil and Spain. *** IT IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR THE 'BASQUE OR EXTREMADURAN' QUESTION UNTIL SOMEBODY ESTABLISHES WHICH LINEA IS MEANT ***, and saying so is the point of writing it down. *** HIS AGE IS NOT ON THIS FRAME. *** The witness before him ends 'dijo ser mayor de cuarenta y ocho anos', which is where a deposition states it, and Sancho's declaration is cut by the edge of the image. *** THE NEXT FRAME OF THIS FILE SHOULD CARRY HIS AGE AND HIS SIGNATURE, AND IT HAS NOT BEEN OPENED. *** *** IDENTIFICATION: *** a Sancho Llerena deposing at the Vicaria of Canelones in a file series of 1776-1806, in the parish where this man married on 8 January 1791, with no second Sancho Llerena known in the country. *** TAKEN AS HIM, AND THE REASONING IS STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. *** *** THE NEXT FRAME WAS OPENED THE SAME HOUR, AND IT ANSWERS A DIFFERENT QUESTION THAN THE ONE ASKED. *** *** HIS AGE IS NOT THERE. *** The deposition before his closes in the standard form - 'dijo ser mayor de cuarenta y ocho anos, y no la firmo porque dijo no saber escrivir' - so the file states ages when it has them, and *** FOR SANCHO IT SIMPLY DOES NOT ***. That is a property of the document, not a failure of the search, and it is written down so nobody opens this frame again hoping. *** WHAT IT DOES GIVE IS SMALLER AND SHARPER: SANCHO LLERENA COULD NOT WRITE. *** His declaration continues onto the next frame and ends *** '... que dijo NO SABER ESCRIVIR, y la firmo su merced conmigo el presente Notario, que lo doy fe. Ante mi, JOSEPH DEL RIOS, Notario Eclesiastico.' *** The judge signed in his place. *** THIS ARCHIVE HAS HELD HIM SINCE ITS FIRST WEEK AND HAS NEVER BEFORE KNOWN ANYTHING ABOUT THE MAN HIMSELF *** - only whose father and whose husband he was. He was a man who had spent years on a frontier line, who was trusted to swear to another man's freedom to marry, and who could not sign his own name. *** THE EXPEDIENTE ENDS by decreeing that neither it nor the conciliar proclamas produced any canonical impediment, and that the marriage of FLORENTINO GOMEZ and ANA GOMEZ should proceed. *** *** A NOTE ON HOW THE FRAME WAS REACHED, because it cost three wrong attempts: *** the image ark pins one image and *** ?i=N IS IGNORED WHEN AN ARK IS PRESENT ***. The route that worked was the viewer's own image-number box - this file is *** image 340 of 457, DGS 008166573 ITEM 8 *** - and a /search/film/008166573?i=341 query would have landed on item 001 and the wrong volume, which is a trap this archive has already recorded once.

name: Jose Julio LERENA Juanico
occupation: JUEZ DE PAZ y Oficial del Estado Civil, 1a Seccion de Montevideo (strong, not proved)
source: Montevideo civil birth registration No. 283 of 1908 - IMAGE READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-W97S-F; and thirty-five Montevideo civil marriage acts of 1902-1914 signed "Julio Lerena Juanico, Juez de Paz" - one read in full, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-2SKF-F
note: *** A SIXTH CHILD of Luis Eugenio Lerena Lenguas and Julia Juanico, found 13 September 2026. *** Born 15 March 1879 at Montevideo and not registered until 14 September 1908, when he was 29 - a late registration of the kind a man makes to produce proof of birth for his own wedding, and he does appear on a Montevideo marriage index card for 1908. *** THE IMAGE IS OPENED. *** Born at the house calle YI No. 303, and registered in 1908 by HIS OWN MOTHER - Dona Julia Juanico, 64, a widow of calle Buenos Aires 102. The act independently confirms Luis Eugenio's death, "fallecido en esta Ciudad el veinte y cuatro de Diciembre de mil novecientos uno", from a different document written seven years after it. *** AND IT PLACES JUSTINIANA LENGUAS, AT EIGHTY-SEVEN, RESIDENT IN THE ARGENTINE REPUBLIC. *** *** AND HE WAS ALMOST CERTAINLY A JUDGE. *** Thirty-five Montevideo civil marriage acts of 1902-1914 open "Por ante mi JULIO LERENA JUANICO, JUEZ DE PAZ y OFICIAL DEL ESTADO CIVIL de la Primera Seccion del Departamento de Montevideo". The compound surname is this family's and no other here; he is the only JULIO among the seven children; and he would be thirty in 1909. *** STRONG BUT NOT PROVED - no act read so far gives the judge's own parents. *** And it explains the oddest thing in his record: a man appointed Oficial del Estado Civil needs proof of his own birth rather more than a bridegroom does, which is why his widowed mother swore it before a Juzgado de Paz in September 1908.

name: Bernabe LERENA (of Trinidad)
source: Uruguay Baptisms 1750-1900 / Catholic Church Records 1726-2000 / Civil Registration, read 13 Sep 2026; and Flores, Birth Records 1887-1901 - entry No. 10, Cayetano Alberto Fernandez, born Pintos 7 August 1897; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-333J-F, FULL-TEXT read 9 October 2026; and Santisima Trinidad, Trinidad, Flores. Baptism Records August 1905-August 1909 - baptism of 26 November 1905, Lerena Nepomuceno Teofilo, pages 32-33; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-69Q5-F, DGS film 008163893 item 5 image 20 - FULL-TEXT found and PLATE READ 9 October 2026; and Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records 1857-1860 - EXPEDIENTE of Bernabe Lerena to marry Casimira Pelaez, Santisima Trinidad, 15 February 1858, Luciano Bonamino Cura Vicario, WITH A KINSHIP DIAGRAM; image 209, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-P3TS-W - FULL-TEXT found and PLATE READ 9 October 2026; and Catedral Basilica San Jose, Religious Marriage Records March 1825-September 1859 - act No. 17 of 16 September 1825, before Don Joseph Andres Salvatierra, Cura y Vicario Interino; DGS film 008143329 (microfilm 625330) image 10 (indexed at 00009), ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-67T7 - PLATE READ 9 October 2026; and FamilySearch RECORD INDEX - spelling sweeps PERENA, GERENA, LLERENA + Flores, 12 October 2026; and San Jose de Mayo, Baptism Records 1828-1836 (film 008143327, image 203 of 801), act no. 1256, the christening of Bernabe, June 1836; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D9PN-8 - *** IMAGE READ *** 18 October 2026, found by the same image-by-image scan of the machine index
note: One of the men fathering Lerena children at Trinidad, Flores in the 1870s and 1880s. Wife: Casimira PELAEZ. 4 children 1871-1885. *** Six or seven men of a rare surname in one small inland town in a handful of years are almost certainly brothers or first cousins - this looks like the founding kindred of the surname in Uruguay. *** No Pablo and no Armando anywhere in the set. *** HE HAS AN AGE, AN ADDRESS AND A FIFTH CHILD, 9 October 2026. *** His grandson's birth act of 1897 gives him as *** 'Don BERNABE LERENA, Oriental, de sesenta y dos anos, casado, de profesion HACENDADO y vecino de CERRO COLORADO' *** - so born about *** 1835 ***, a landholder, and living at Cerro Colorado rather than in Trinidad town. *** AND THE CHILD'S MOTHER, ANTONINA LERENA, IS HIS DAUGHTER *** - a fifth to set beside the four this archive had from 1871-1885. *** A SIXTH CHILD, 9 October 2026: JUAN. *** The 1905 baptism of Nepomuceno Teofilo at Trinidad gives 'Abuelos paternos: *** BERNABE y CASIMIRA PELAEZ ***' for a child of *** Juan Lerena and Eduviges Pelaez ***, and his son Juan is *** Juan Bernardo Lerena Pelaez, born 20 August 1871 *** - the groom of the 1894 dispensation. *** FOUR CHILDREN ON 13 SEPTEMBER, A FIFTH YESTERDAY, A SIXTH TODAY, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM FROM A GRANDCHILD'S RECORD. *** *** HIS PARENTS, HIS GRANDPARENTS, HIS WEDDING DATE AND HIS BIRTHPLACE, 9 October 2026 - AND A PRIEST'S DRAWING OF THE LOT. *** His own marriage expediente, Santisima Trinidad, *** 15 February 1858 ***, calls him '*** hijo legitimo de Don ALEJANDRO LERENA y Dona MARGARITA FERNANDEZ, NATURALES DE SAN JOSE y vecinos de esta ***', seeking to marry *** su parienta en SEGUNDO GRADO de consanguinidad en linea trasversal, Dona CASIMIRA PELAEZ ***. *** AND THE FOLIO CARRIES A KINSHIP SCHEMA THE CURA VICARIO DREW HIMSELF: *** *** RAMON LERENA / MARIA GONZALEZ *** at the apex, with lines down to *** ALEJANDRO LERENA / MARGARITA FERNANDEZ *** and *** ANTONINA LERENA / JUAN PELAES ***, and below them the two contracting parties. *** SO ALEJANDRO AND ANTONINA ARE BROTHER AND SISTER, AND BERNABE MARRIED HIS FIRST COUSIN. *** *** AND SOCORRO LERENA IS HIS SISTER ***, by the expediente of 1855 which gives her the same parents - *** which closes work-list row 196. *** *** THE TRANSCRIPT CALLS HIM 'BERNABE LERESA' AND THE PLATE SAYS LERENA. *** *** AND HE IS NOT UNATTACHED, AND HAS NOT BEEN SINCE 17 SEPTEMBER - THIS ROW WAS THE LAST PLACE TO SAY OTHERWISE. *** data/ramon-lerena-rosario.tsv has carried him as a son of ALEJANDRO LERENA since 17 September and /uruguay/ has drawn it; this row went on saying nothing joined him. *** THE REGISTER WAS CONTRADICTING THE ARCHIVE'S OWN EVIDENCE FILES FOR THREE WEEKS. *** See data/corrections.tsv. *** AND IT IS NOW DOCUMENTED AT PLATE LEVEL, TWICE: *** his own marriage expediente of 15 February 1858 names him 'hijo legitimo de Don ALEJANDRO LERENA y Dona MARGARITA FERNANDEZ' and carries the priest's schema; and *** ALEJANDRO'S OWN MARRIAGE ACT OF 16 SEPTEMBER 1825 at San Jose *** makes Alejandro 'hijo legitimo de RAMON LEREÑA y MARIA JOSEFA GONZALEZ', *** natural de la VILLA DEL ROSARIO ***. *** SO BERNABE IS A GRANDSON OF RAMON LERENA OF ROSARIO-COLLA, AND A FIRST COUSIN OF CIPRIANO. *** *** THE GUESS OF 13 SEPTEMBER IN THIS ROW - that the Trinidad men are 'almost certainly brothers or first cousins' - IS NOW PROVED FOR TWO OF THEM. *** *** AND TWO EARLIER DAUGHTERS, FOUND UNDER THE LLERENA SPELLING - 12 October 2026. *** *** MARGARITA MEDARDA DEL CORAZON DE JESUS ***, christened at Trinidad in *** 1859 ***, and *** MARIA ***, born 13 May 1866 and christened on the 25th. *** THE 1859 CHILD MATTERS MOST: *** this row's six known children run from 1871, and 1859 sits a year after his marriage expediente of 15 February 1858 - *** which is where a first child belongs, and is eleven years earlier than anything this archive had. *** *** NEITHER IS MERGED WITH ANY MARIA ALREADY HELD. *** *** INDEX-LEVEL. *** *** HIS OWN BAPTISM IS FOUND AND READ AT THE PLATE, 18 October 2026: BORN 10 JUNE 1836 AT SAN JOSE, CHRISTENED ON 20 JUNE. *** 'En esta Parroquia de San Jose a veinte de Junio de mil ochocientos treinta y seis yo D.n Jose Joaquin Reyna, Cura Vicario, bautice solemnemente y puse los Santos Oleo y Crisma a Bernabe [del Corazon de Jesus, as the index reads it], que nacio el dia diez del mismo mes, hijo legitimo de D.n Alejandro Lerena y de Da. Margarita Fernandez. Abuelos paternos Ramon y Maria Gonzalez. Maternos Juan y Barbara Sotura. Fueron padrinos [Jose Pau]lino Larriera y Da. Dolores Morales, a quienes adverti el parentesco y demas obligaciones. Doy fe. Jose Joaquin Reyna'; margin 'Bernabe Lerena', act 1256. *** THIS CORRECTS HIS BIRTH FROM 'ABOUT 1835' TO 1836 (the 1897 act's 'sesenta y dos anos' was a year high, as the 1911 civil death index's birth year of 1836 already said), *** and it names his parents and BOTH sets of grandparents - Ramon and Maria Gonzalez, and Juan and Barbara Sotura - in one act, agreeing with the 1858 diagram and the 1825 marriage act. *** HE IS THE YOUNGEST OF THE FIVE, nearly four years after Socorro. *** The godfather Paulino Larriera shares a surname with the LARRIERA family of San Jose that Alberto Lerena married into; no tie is claimed. The godmother Dolores Morales is unplaced.

note: Married into the Trinidad Lerena kindred. *** BELOQUI, ECHEVERRY and PELAEZ are Basque surnames *** - evidence about the community these Lerenas married into, which bears on the Basque-or-Extremaduran question without settling it. *** AND SHE HAS AN AGE AT LAST, 9 October 2026 *** - *** 'Dona CASIMIRA PELAEZ, Oriental, de cincuenta y seis anos, casada, de profesion labores, domiciliada con su esposo' *** in her grandson's birth act of 1897, so born about *** 1841 ***. *** Her daughter ANTONINA married a FERNANDEZ whose own mother was a LERENA ***, and the couple had to be dispensed a second grade of consanguinity. *** A SIXTH CHILD, 9 October 2026: JUAN. *** The 1905 baptism of Nepomuceno Teofilo at Trinidad gives 'Abuelos paternos: *** BERNABE y CASIMIRA PELAEZ ***' for a child of *** Juan Lerena and Eduviges Pelaez ***, and her son Juan is *** Juan Bernardo Lerena Pelaez, born 20 August 1871 *** - the groom of the 1894 dispensation. *** FOUR CHILDREN ON 13 SEPTEMBER, A FIFTH YESTERDAY, A SIXTH TODAY, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM FROM A GRANDCHILD'S RECORD. *** *** HER PARENTS AND HER WEDDING, 9 October 2026. *** The 1858 expediente calls her '*** hija legitima de Don JUAN PELAES y Dona ANTONINA LERENA, naturales de SAN JOSE y vecinos de esta ***' - *** SO HER MOTHER IS THE ELDER ANTONINA LERENA, ALREADY IN THIS REGISTER ***, and Casimira is a sister of MARIA PELAEZ and of MALVINO PELAEZ. *** SHE MARRIED HER FIRST COUSIN: *** her mother Antonina and his father Alejandro are the two children drawn under Ramon Lerena on the priest's schema.  *** HER FULL NAME IS CASIMIRA JOSEFA, 10 October 2026 ***, from her mother's death act of 1911, which lists the four surviving children of Antonina Isabel Lerena and Juan Pedro Pelaez. *** SHE WAS ALIVE IN JULY 1911. ***

name: Cipriano LERENA (of Trinidad)
source: Uruguay Baptisms 1750-1900 / Catholic Church Records 1726-2000 / Civil Registration, read 13 Sep 2026; and Flores. Birth Records 1887-1902 - act No. 8 of 2 March 1895, Carmen Donata Lerena, El Tala; image 165, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-334D-Z - FULL-TEXT read 9 October 2026; and FamilySearch RECORD INDEX - spelling sweeps PERENA, GERENA, LLERENA + Flores, 12 October 2026
note: One of the men fathering Lerena children at Trinidad, Flores in the 1870s and 1880s. Wife: Lauriana BELOQUI. 3 children 1875-1891. *** Six or seven men of a rare surname in one small inland town in a handful of years are almost certainly brothers or first cousins - this looks like the founding kindred of the surname in Uruguay. *** No Pablo and no Armando anywhere in the set. *** AND HE IS A SON OF MAURICIO LERENA OF COLLA, 9 October 2026 - WHICH BRIDGES TWO HOUSES THIS ARCHIVE HELD APART. *** The Flores birth act of his daughter Carmen Donata, *** 2 March 1895 at El Tala ***, has him declare in person as '*** Don [C]ipriano Lerena de CUARENTA Y DOS anos de edad, casado, oriental, HACENDADO y vecino de esta seccion ***' - so born about *** 1853 *** - with his wife '*** Dona Laureana Belo[qui] de TREINTA Y NUEVE anos ***' and his own parents as '*** nieto por linea paterna de MAURICIO, oriental, FALLECIDO, y de CASIMIRA MONTANO de SETENTA Y CUATRO anos de edad, VIUDA ***'. *** THAT NAMES HIS WIFE AND BOTH HIS PARENTS IN ONE ACT ***, which is why the separate row 'Cipriano LERENA Montana' - known only from a 1928 death-registration index - is merged into this one. *** THE PAIR HAD BEEN SPOTTED AND HELD APART SINCE 21 SEPTEMBER; AN ACT DECIDED IT RATHER THAN A FORENAME. *** *** SO THREE CHILDREN ALREADY IN THIS REGISTER - Doroteo Donato, Maria Leonor and Lauriana LERENA Beloqui - ARE GRANDCHILDREN OF MAURICIO LERENA AND CASIMIRA MONTANO ***, and a fourth, Carmen Donata, is added. *** HE COULD NOT WRITE: *** the act records that he 'manifesto no saber escribir' and signed by another's hand. *** TWO MORE CHILDREN, FOUND UNDER TWO OTHER SPELLINGS - 12 October 2026. *** *** AMABELIA ***, born about 1880 and dead on 9 January 1899, came from the PERENA sweep; *** CASTO LINDOLFO ***, born 1 July 1882 and christened 5 February 1883, from the GERENA sweep. *** THIS ROW HELD THREE CHILDREN AND NOW HOLDS FIVE ***, and neither of the new two was reachable by searching LERENA. *** HIS OWN DEATH OF 19 MARCH 1928 IS CONFIRMED a third time by the GERENA sweep, which names his parents MAURICIO and CASIMIRA MONTANO. ***

name: Juan Bernardo LERENA Pelaez
source: Uruguay Baptisms 1750-1900 / Catholic Church Records 1726-2000 / Civil Registration, read 13 Sep 2026; and Santisima Trinidad, Trinidad, Flores. Baptism Records August 1905-August 1909 - baptism of 26 November 1905, Lerena Nepomuceno Teofilo, pages 32-33; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-69Q5-F, DGS film 008163893 item 5 image 20 - FULL-TEXT found and PLATE READ 9 October 2026
note: Child of Bernabe Lerena and Casimira Pelaez, baptised or registered at Trinidad, Flores. *** AND HE IS THE GROOM OF THE 1894 DISPENSATION. *** On 31 March 1894 a Juan Lerena was dispensed *** the SECOND grade AND the THIRD grade of consanguinity, both accumulated, DE OFICIO ***, to marry *** Dona EDUVIGES PELAEZ of MERCEDES ***. This register carried that man as a separate row for a day. *** THE BAPTISM OF HIS SON JOINS THEM, 9 October 2026: *** 'Lerena Nepomuceno Teofilo', born 13 October 1905, '*** hijo legitimo de Juan Lerena y Eduviges Pelaez. Abuelos paternos: BERNABE y CASIMIRA PELAEZ ***'. *** HE IS THE ONLY JUAN AMONG THAT COUPLE'S CHILDREN ***, so the parents name him. *** THE PAIR FILE DECLARED THE TWO ROWS DIFFERENT PEOPLE ON 9 OCTOBER *** because the dispensation row then had 'no age, no birth and no parents'. It has parents now; see data/corrections.tsv. *** TWENTY-TWO AT HIS DISPENSATION, THIRTY-FOUR AT HIS SON'S BAPTISM. *** *** WHY HE NEEDED DISPENSING: *** his mother is a PELAEZ and Eduviges's father is a PELAEZ - *** if Casimira Pelaez and Juan Pelaez were brother and sister, the couple were first cousins ***, which is what an equal second degree means. *** THE THIRD DEGREE IS A SECOND BLOOD PATH AND IS NOT YET FOUND. ***
