name: Zelmira Carlota LERENA LARRIERA (m. Adolfo CORDERO)
source: San Jose de Mayo - baptism of 12 April 1905 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-Z7WR-1; and Uruguayan civil registration - her birth of 4 Nov 1880, her marriage of 28 Feb 1901 and her death of 4 Jan 1945 - indexes read 14 Sep 2026; and Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records 1856-1932 - image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-NXGJ, FULL-TEXT transcript read 9 October 2026; and La Union, Montevideo - Religious Marriage Records 1902-1934, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-TWWY-Y - FULL-TEXT transcript read 9 October 2026
note: *** TESTED AND PLACED, 14 September 2026 - and she is NOT ours. *** Born 4 NOVEMBER 1880 in the Departamento de SAN JOSE, daughter of *** ALBERTO LERENA and MARIA INES LARRIERA ***; married ADOLFO CORDERO at Montevideo on 28 FEBRUARY 1901; died at Montevideo 4 JANUARY 1945. Children ADOLFO ANGEL FAUSTINO (b.1905, the San Jose baptism that found her), MARIA ZELMIRA (b.1903, d.1984) and MARIA EUGENIA. *** She was flagged because the shape was right - a Uruguayan Lerena woman married to an Argentine in the decade this archive cares about. The shape was right and the substance is not: she has a father, a birthplace and a date, and none of them touches Pablo Armando. *** *** BUT HER FATHER IS WORTH A SECOND LOOK, AND IS NOT MERGED. *** ALBERTO LERENA, fathering a daughter in 1880, would be the right age to be ALBERTO OCTAVIO LERENA LENGUAS - born Montevideo 22 March 1850, son of Luis and Justiniana, and so a grandson of Sancho. He would be thirty. *** NOTHING JOINS THEM but a forename and an age, which is precisely the evidence that produced the two Arturos. *** If it held, Zelmira would be a great-granddaughter of Sancho - and that is a hypothesis to test, not a line to draw.  *** 'SHE IS NOT OURS' IS RETRACTED, 21 September 2026. SHE IS OURS. *** This row named the one test that would change its own verdict - who her father Alberto Lerena was - and guessed ALBERTO OCTAVIO LERENA LENGUAS. *** IT IS THE OTHER GRANDFATHER. *** Alberto Lerena's own Montevideo death registration of 2 March 1921, certificate 246, names his wife MARIA INES LARRIERA and his parents AVELINO LERENA and AMBROSIA TREIBEL. So her father is *** PEDRO ALBERTO YSABELINO LERENA TRAIBEL, baptised at the Aguada on 21 November 1852 ***, and *** ZELMIRA IS A GREAT-GRANDDAUGHTER OF SANCHO *** - which is what this row said would follow if the link held. It held by a different route. *** THE LINK IS ONE RECORD AND IT IS INDEX-LEVEL: *** the 1921 image has not been opened, and that is now an errand. See data/alberto-lerena-larriera.tsv.  *** AND THE LINK IS NO LONGER INDEX-LEVEL. *** Within the hour the 1921 image was opened - film 008165205 image 01604 - and it names her father's parents as AVELINO LERENA and AMBROSIA TREIBEL in his own hand-written act, *** and names HER among his nine children: 'Maria Adelina, ZELMIRA, Eleiza, Alberto, Carlos, Maria Ines, Maria Consuelo, Maria Antonieta y Miguel Avelino'. *** The chain from her to Sancho now rests on an image at every step that matters. *** AND HER MARRIAGE IS FOUND, 9 October 2026. *** Entry N. 7057, *** 1 FEBRUARY 1901 ***: the Archbishop dispensed *** DON ADOLFO CORDERO *** the impediment of *** THIRD GRADE of consanguinity WITH ATTINGENCY TO THE SECOND, by the unequal lateral line ***, with which he was declared bound to *** DONA ZELMIRA CARLOTA LERENA, feligresa de la METROPOLITANA ***. *** SHE MARRIED A BLOOD RELATIVE, AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT HER ANCESTRY RATHER THAN HER LIFE *** - the Church computed the degree before it would dispense, so the entry constrains her pedigree even though it names no parent. *** THIS ARCHIVE ONCE WROTE HER OFF *** as 'tested and placed - and she is not ours', and corrected that; here she is on a record of her own. *** AND HER MARRIAGE ACT WAS READ IN FULL ON 9 OCTOBER 2026, and it moves the date. *** Headed *** 'Matrimonio de Cordero y Lorena' ***: on *** 28 FEBRUARY 1904 *** at the Iglesia de *** Nuestra Senora de Lourdes ***, La Union, before Bishop *** Ricardo Jara ***, she married *** D. ADOLFO MAXIMO CORDERO - soltero, ARGENTINO, MEDICO, twenty-eight, of SAN JOSE, legitimate son of D. ADOLFO M. CORDERO and Dona CASIMIRA CHAVARRIA ***. She is *** soltera, oriental, TWENTY years old, of CALLE CERRO LARGO 230 ***, and *** hija legitima de D. Alberto [S]erena y Dona Maria Ines Larriera ***. *** THIS REGISTER SAYS SHE MARRIED IN 1901 AND THE ACT SAYS 1904 *** - same day, same month. The book runs 1902-1934 and the entry above it is dated May 1902, so *** 1901 is impossible and the act is primary ***. The dispensation of 1 February 1901 cleared them three years before they married. *** AND HER AGE DOES NOT FIT EITHER: *** twenty in February 1904 means born about 1883-84, not 4 November 1880. *** Both are recorded and neither is preferred. *** *** HER PARENTS ARE NOW ON A PRIMARY RECORD *** rather than an index - and the act writes her father SERENA and her mother, as a witness four lines later, LERENA.

Named in the Catedral baptism of 12 May 1827; his wife Dona Juana Suarez is already dead by then. *** ALSO NAMED IN 1840 *** - as "D. JOAQUIN RODRIGUEZ ... natural de la COLONIA DEL SACRAMENTO", the same man under the register's other spelling of the surname. So the Carvallos came to Montevideo from the Colonia del Sacramento. *** READ OFF THE PLATE 21 September 2026, where this row had rested on a MACHINE TRANSCRIPT. *** Film 007713376 image 00601, folio 150 - the baptism of 12 May 1827 at the Iglesia Matriz de San Felipe y Santiago de Montevideo. 'Nieta paterna del MAYOR D.n JOAQUIN RU[iz de Carvallo]' - his rank and his name, on the plate. *** THIS ROW WAS RIGHT AND ANOTHER ROW CONTRADICTED IT FOR THREE WEEKS - settled on the plate, 11 October 2026. *** It has always said he was 'ALSO NAMED IN 1840', while the register simultaneously carried a *** 'Don Domingo RODRIGUEZ (the elder, of la Colonia)' *** built from the same sentence of the same act. *** THE PLATE READS 'Nieto Pat.o de D. JOAQUIN RODRIG.z y D.a Juana del Espiritu S.to: AMBOS NAT.S DE LA COLONIA DEL SACRAM.TO' ***, and the act's own names panel gives 'Pats. A household that moved twice before it married into Sancho's.

name: Dona Juana SUAREZ
source: Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion, Montevideo - baptism of 12 May 1827 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-YSFQ-2 - IMAGE READ 21 September 2026; film 007713376 image 00601; and the Catedral baptism of her grandson Domingo Rodriguez de Carvallo, 25 October 1840 - ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-YSFY-L; and the SAME plate re-read 11 October 2026 during a site-wide audit - film 007713376 image 01689, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-YSFY-L, deepzoom apid TH-909-52377-68331-65
note: Wife of Mayor Don Joaquin Ruiz de Carvallo; "la finada" by May 1827. *** AND SHE IS THE "DONA JUANA DEL ESPIRITU SANTO" of the 1840 act - *** named there as Joaquin's wife and a native of the Colonia del Sacramento. A devotional epithet and a surname can belong to one woman. Recorded as a reading, not a finding - the two acts do not say so themselves. *** READ OFF THE PLATE 21 September 2026, where this row had rested on a MACHINE TRANSCRIPT. *** Film 007713376 image 00601, folio 150 - the baptism of 12 May 1827 at the Iglesia Matriz de San Felipe y Santiago de Montevideo. '...na SUAREZ. Materna...' - she survives the check as the paternal grandmother. *** 'PROBABLY' IS WITHDRAWN AND THE TWO ROWS ARE NOW ONE, 11 October 2026. *** This register carried her twice: here as JUANA SUAREZ, wife of Mayor Joaquin, and separately as *** 'Dona Juana del ESPIRITU SANTO' ***, entered as the wife of a *** 'Don Domingo Rodriguez' *** who turns out not to exist. *** THE PLATE OF THE 1840 ACT READS JOAQUIN, NOT DOMINGO *** - so both rows described the same slot, the mother of Capitan Antonio, and the obstacle to joining them was a misread forename rather than anything about her. *** BOTH ACTS NAME HER AS ANTONIO'S MOTHER: *** the 1827 baptism of her granddaughter Lucinda Gregoria gives the paternal grandparents as *** 'Joaquin Ruiz de Carvallo y Juana Suarez' ***; the 1840 baptism of her grandson Domingo gives them as *** 'D. Joaquin Rodrig.z y D.a Juana del Espiritu S.to, ambos nat.s de la COLONIA DEL SACRAMENTO' ***. *** SO SHE WAS BORN IN THE COLONIA, which this row did not know ***, and she was dead by May 1827 - 'la finada' - yet still named as a grandmother thirteen years later, which is ordinary. *** DEL ESPIRITU SANTO IS A DEVOTIONAL NAME AND SUAREZ IS THE INHERITED ONE ***, so the register keeps SUAREZ and /people/dona-juana-del-espiritu-santo redirects here. The devotional form is left in this prose so a search for it still finds her. *** AND IT ANSWERS THE QUESTION THE OTHER ROW RAISED: *** that row wondered whether 'del Espiritu Santo' marked a foundling. It does not - she had a surname.

source: Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion, Montevideo - baptism of 25 Oct 1840 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-YSFY-L - IMAGE READ 21 September 2026; film 007713376 image 01689; and the SAME plate re-read 11 October 2026 during a site-wide audit - film 007713376 image 01689, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-YSFY-L, deepzoom apid TH-909-52377-68331-65

Antonio Rodriguez de Carballo and Dona Dominga Lerena, and so a younger brother of Lucinda Gregoria (b.1827). *** He is the child whose existence made the two-Dominga problem, and the act that names him is the one that solved it. *** Godparents Don Joaquin Sosa and Dona Balvina Suarez.  *** READ OFF THE PLATE 21 September 2026, and every reading holds. *** Film 007713376 image 01689, margin *** 'Domingo Rodrig.z de Carvallo' ***: 'En VEINTE Y CINCO DE OCTUBRE de mil ochoc.s CUARENTA ... bautice solemnem.te a DOMINGO que NACIO EL CUATRO DE AGOSTO DEL PPTE. SANCHO LERENA y D.a M.a FERNANDEZ.' *** THREE THINGS THE TRANSCRIPT DID NOT CARRY INTO THIS REGISTER: *** his father is *** natural de la PROVINCIA DEL RIO *** and not of Montevideo; his paternal grandparents are *** DOMINGO RODRIGUEZ and JUANA DEL ESPIRITU SANTO, 'ambos naturales de la COLONIA' ***; and the act spells the father CARBALLO with a B where this register writes CARVALLO. *** THE MATERNAL SIDE IS SANCHO LERENA AND MARIA FERNANDEZ, named again *** - the seventh plate read today to say so. *** THE WORD IN SQUARE BRACKETS ON THIS ROW WAS WRONG, AND IT MANUFACTURED A PERSON - corrected 11 October 2026. *** This note used to read *** 'Nieto pat[erno de D. DOMINGO] RODRIG.z' ***, with the grandfather's forename supplied by the reader because the CHILD is called Domingo. *** THE PLATE SAYS JOAQUIN. *** Re-read at 4000px on the deepzoom tile: 'Nieto Pat.o de D. *** JOAQUIN *** RODRIG.z y D.a Juana del Espiritu S.to: ambos nat.s de la Colonia del Sacram.to'. name: Juan Agustin LERENA Fernandez
source: Padron de Montevideo de 1812 (AGN, Fondo ex AGA, L 251), transcribed in Apolant, "Operativo Patagonia" ficha 355 and quoted in the Geneanet tree of jfina; plus that tree's own child list
note: *** THE ELDEST, AND HE MATTERS FOR A SECOND REASON. *** *** ONE OF SANCHO'S SIX CHILDREN LISTED IN THE 1812 PADRON, and the first time any of them has been entered here. *** The household at calle San Juan No 60 held Sancho "andaluz" 45, Maria Fernandez 36, and six children all *** "naturales del CANELON" *** - Juan Agustin 21, Pedro Antonio 19, Agustina 17, Fidel 12, Justa 10 and Dominga 7 - together with Sancho's father-in-law RODRIGO FERNANDEZ, 63, asturiano, and four enslaved people. *** That all six were born at Canelones is the best support the 1791 marriage venue has, *** and it comes from a census rather than from a tree. *** NOT AN ACT: *** this row rests on a published transcription of a census, reported at second hand through a family tree. *** The act has not been opened here. *** *** THE 1812 PADRON GIVES HIM AS 21, so born about 1791 - the year of his parents' marriage. *** *** AND HE RESOLVES A MISREADING THIS ARCHIVE MADE AGAINST ITSELF. *** At the Montevideo baptism of 15 May 1812 the godparents are written "DON JUAN AGUSTIN SERENA y DONA AGUSTINA PERENA". This archive argued that "Juan Agustin cannot be Sancho's son, who would be a child in 1812" and talked itself out of the reading. *** He was twenty-one, and his sister Agustina was seventeen. *** The two names at that font are his and hers, and the child baptised was very likely their first cousin. *** So SERENA and PERENA are the machine's S-for-L again - the sixth time on this family. *** The tree gives his birth as 1792; the padron implies 1791. Both are kept.

note: *** ONE OF SANCHO'S SIX CHILDREN LISTED IN THE 1812 PADRON, and the first time any of them has been entered here. *** The household at calle San Juan No 60 held Sancho "andaluz" 45, Maria Fernandez 36, and six children all *** "naturales del CANELON" *** - Juan Agustin 21, Pedro Antonio 19, Agustina 17, Fidel 12, Justa 10 and Dominga 7 - together with Sancho's father-in-law RODRIGO FERNANDEZ, 63, asturiano, and four enslaved people. *** That all six were born at Canelones is the best support the 1791 marriage venue has, *** and it comes from a census rather than from a tree. *** NOT AN ACT: *** this row rests on a published transcription of a census, reported at second hand through a family tree. *** The act has not been opened here. *** *** Aged 17 in the 1812 padron, so born about 1795, which the tree gives exactly. *** *** She is the second half of the 1812 godparent pair *** - "Dona AGUSTINA PERENA" - standing with her elder brother Juan Agustin at a Fernandez grandchild's baptism. Her forename repeats his second, which is the ordinary Spanish habit of naming siblings from one saint. *** HER ACT IS FOUND, 15 September 2026, one day after she was entered here from a census age and a tree. *** Canelones, 30 August 1795: "bautice puse el Santo Oleo y Crisma a AGUSTINA RAMONA de tres dias nacida, hija legitima de Don Sancho Lerena y de Dona Maria Fernandez vecinos de la Villa". *** Born 27 August 1795, and her second forename is RAMONA. *** *** Her godfather was DON FIDEL REY of Montevideo - which is where her younger brother FIDEL got a forename that appears nowhere else in this family. ***  *** READ OFF THE PLATE 21 September 2026, AND SHE GAINS A SECOND FORENAME. *** Film 008166571 image 01017: 'a TREINTA DIAS DEL MES DE AGOSTO ... yo el Cura y Vic.o de esta Parroquia de los CANELONES ... bautize, puse el Santo Oleo y Crisma a *** AGUSTINA RAMONA, DE TRES DIAS NACIDA ***, hija legitima de D.n *** SANCHO LERENA *** y de D.a Maria Fernandez, *** VECINOS DE LA VILLA ***. Fueron sus padrinos D.n *** FIDEL REY, vecino de MONTEVIDEO ***, y D.a JOSEFA ... de la misma Villa.' *** 'DE TRES DIAS NACIDA' CONFIRMS THE BIRTH OF 27 AUGUST 1795 *** that this register carried from a tree and a padron. *** AND THE GODFATHER EXPLAINS A NAME THIS FAMILY USES: FIDEL. *** Sancho's next son but one was christened FIDEL, about 1799 - four years after Don Fidel Rey stood at this font. *** This family names children for whoever stands at the font, five times over in the acts read here ***, so the likeliest source of the forename FIDEL in the Lerena is this man. *** IT IS AN INFERENCE FROM A PATTERN, NOT FROM A RECORD, and it does not touch the separate question of whether the FIDEL LERENA who married Maria Ruedas is Sancho's son. *** The act also carries a scribal self-correction - the teniente cura is written 'D.r Christoval Munoz QUIERO DECIR ...' - and the Cura y Vicario signs JOSE MANUEL DE ROO, the same hand that signs Jose Loreto's act eleven years later.

name: Fidel LERENA Fernandez
source: Padron de Montevideo de 1812 (AGN, Fondo ex AGA, L 251), transcribed in Apolant, "Operativo Patagonia" ficha 355 and quoted in the Geneanet tree of jfina; plus that tree's own child list
note: *** ONE OF SANCHO'S SIX CHILDREN LISTED IN THE 1812 PADRON, and the first time any of them has been entered here. *** The household at calle San Juan No 60 held Sancho "andaluz" 45, Maria Fernandez 36, and six children all *** "naturales del CANELON" *** - Juan Agustin 21, Pedro Antonio 19, Agustina 17, Fidel 12, Justa 10 and Dominga 7 - together with Sancho's father-in-law RODRIGO FERNANDEZ, 63, asturiano, and four enslaved people. *** That all six were born at Canelones is the best support the 1791 marriage venue has, *** and it comes from a census rather than from a tree. *** NOT AN ACT: *** this row rests on a published transcription of a census, reported at second hand through a family tree. *** The act has not been opened here. *** *** Aged 12 in the 1812 padron, so born about 1800; the tree gives 1799 and a death in 1822, at twenty-two or twenty-three. *** *** If that death is right he is the only one of Sancho's children this archive can see dying young, *** and he died in the decade the family were serving the Portuguese occupation at Canelones. *** The death is tree-only and has not been tested against Montevideo burials. *** The tree's own prose says the couple had EIGHT children while listing seven, and it omits Dominga, whom the padron and a Canelones act of 1804 both attest - so its child list is incomplete and this row inherits that caution. *** AND HIS NAME IS EXPLAINED, 15 September 2026. *** It appears nowhere else in this family and this row could not account for it. *** His sister Agustina's baptism of 30 August 1795 gives her godfather as DON FIDEL REY, vecino de Montevideo. *** The child born four years later carries the godfather's name. *** An inference, not a statement - no act says the boy was named for him - but the coincidence of a rare forename and a recent sponsor in one household is a thin one to explain away. *** *** AND THAT DEATH HAS NOW BEEN TESTED AGAINST MONTEVIDEO BURIALS, 20 September 2026: IT IS NOT THERE. *** A search of Uruguayan deaths 1815-1840 for a Fidel Lerena returns nothing, against a control in the same window - Rodriguez - returning 62,026 records with burials of 1840 and 1844 on the first screen. *** The 1822 remains tree-only, and is now tree-only having been looked for. *** It can no longer be used to rule this man out of the 1889 death registration that names a FIDEL LERENA and MARIA RUEDAS as a grandfather and grandmother.

name: Felix LERENA (father of Sancho)
birthplace: Spain, presumably Andalusia (his son is "natural de Andalucia"; CORDOBA comes from a tree)
source: Montevideo, Iglesia Matriz, baptism of Luis Escolastico, 10 Feb 1811 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-X7F6-M; plus Geneanet trees citing Revista 15 IEGU - IMAGE READ 21 September 2026; film 007713375 image 02410
note: *** NAMED ON AN ACT, 15 September 2026 - the first time this archive has had a generation above Sancho on anything but a tree. *** The baptism of their grandson LUIS ESCOLASTICO at the Iglesia Matriz of Montevideo, 10 February 1811, gives *** "Abuelos paternos FELIZ GERENA y ROSALIA AGUILAR" *** in the same sentence that calls their son *** "Don SANCHO LLERENA natural de ANDALUCIA" *** . *** GERENA is the machine's G-for-L *** - a seventh spelling for this family, and the same mangling that produced the still-unresolved "Dona Andugara GERENA" in the Santa Rosa de Lima confirmations at Rosario. *** He is written FELIZ, the ordinary period spelling of FELIX. *** *** WHAT IS STILL NOT KNOWN ABOUT THEM: everything else. *** No dates, no places, no marriage, no other children. The Geneanet pages carry nothing but the line "Family: Revista 15 IEGU", and one Spanish tree offers Cordoba about 1725 and a marriage about 1753 - all values marked "about", with no source at all, and giving Sancho a birth of ca 1754 that the 1812 padron contradicts. *** So the PARENTAGE is documented and the PEOPLE are not. *** *** The search that follows from this is FELIX LERENA and ROSALIA AGUILAR in CORDOBA ***  and it has not been run against Spanish parish records. *** READ OFF THE PLATE 21 September 2026, where this row had rested on a MACHINE TRANSCRIPT since 14 September. *** Film 007713375 image 02410, Iglesia Matriz de Montevideo, the baptism of Luis Escolastico, 10 February 1811 - the only record in this archive that names Sancho's own parents. *** AND THE PLATE CORRECTS HIS SURNAME. *** The machine transcript read the line as 'Abuelos paternos FELIZ GERENA y ROS[A]LIA AGUILAR', and this archive inferred FELIX LERENA from it. The page itself reads *** 'Ab.s pat.s FELIX LLERENA y Ros[alia Aguilar]' *** - FELIX, with an X, and *** LLERENA WITH THE DOUBLE L ***, in the same hand that writes his son 'Sancho Llerena' two lines above. So the earliest Spanish generation this archive can name spelled it LLERENA.

name: Jose Loreto LERENA Fernandez
source: Canelones baptism, 11 Dec 1806 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2Z-W9KR-W - IMAGE READ 21 September 2026; film 008166571 image 01176
note: *** AN EIGHTH CHILD OF SANCHO AND MARIA FERNANDEZ, FOUND 15 September 2026, and he is in no tree and no census. *** Canelones, 11 December 1806: "bautizo solemnemente a un parvulo de un dia de edad y puso por nombre JOSE LORETO, hijo legitimo de Sancho Lorena y de Maria Fernandez vecinos de esta Villa, fue padrino Jose Martinez de la Vega vecino de Montevideo." *** He was found only because the surname was searched as LORENA. Under LLERENA and LERENA he does not appear. *** *** HE IS NOT IN THE 1812 PADRON, *** which lists six children and no boy of about five. *** The likeliest reading is that he died before 1812, which is what a household return's silence usually means about a small child - but no burial has been looked for and none is claimed here. *** *** The Geneanet tree's own prose says the couple had EIGHT children while naming seven. He may be the eighth. ***  *** READ OFF THE PLATE 21 September 2026, and the transcript had one word wrong. *** Film 008166571 image 01176. The act reads: 'bautizo solemnemente a un parvulo de un dia de edad y puso por nombre *** JOSE LORETO ***, hijo legitimo de *** SANCHO LERENA *** y de MARIA FERNANDEZ, *** VECINOS DE ESTA VILLA ***. Fue padrino *** JOSE MARTINEZ DE LA VEGA ***, vecino de *** MONTEVIDEO ***, a quien advirtio la obligacion y parentesco, y yo el Cura y Vicario propio de la expresada Parroquia lo firmo y certifico para que conste.' *** THIS ROW QUOTED THE TRANSCRIPT AS 'SANCHO LORENA'. THE PLATE SAYS LERENA. *** That is the fourth assertion about this family's spelling to turn out to be the machine's rather than the scribe's in one day. *** AND 'VECINOS DE ESTA VILLA' IS WORTH MORE THAN THE SPELLING. *** In December 1806 Sancho and Maria were RESIDENTS OF CANELONES, not visitors to it - which joins up with Agustina's baptism there in 1795, Dominga's in 1804 and Justa Pastora being called 'natural de Canelones' in 1831. *** The family lived at Canelones for at least eleven years and had moved to Montevideo, calle San Juan No 60, by the padron of 1812. *** The godfather was brought from Montevideo, which is the other direction.

name: Juan Carlos GONZALEZ LERENA (m. 1920s, Montevideo)
source: Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records 1856-1932, 8 Nov 192- - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-NNW8 - IMAGE READ 21 September 2026; film 007713367 image 02860, folio 391
note: *** CHECKED AND EXCLUDED, 15 September 2026 - he is the only 'Juan Carlos Lerena' in FamilySearch's entire full-text corpus apart from a 2001 death record. *** The Vicar General "dispenso a Don Juan Carlos Gonzalez Lerena las tres conciliares proclamas en el matrimonio que intenta contraer con ... Concepcion Petrona Urbano". *** LERENA IS HIS SECOND SURNAME - his mother's - not his father's. *** That is the same shape as the only Juan Carlos Lerena in all of Geneanet, a "del Campo Lerena". *** Pablo Armando's father must carry LERENA as the PATERNAL surname and must have been born by about the 1850s to father a son in 1882. This man is marrying in the 1920s. *** *** Recorded so that the next reader who runs this search does not have to spend an hour excluding him. ***  *** READ OFF THE PLATE 21 September 2026, AND THE COMPOUND SURNAME IS REALLY THERE. *** Film 007713367 image 02860, folio 391, entry *** No. 14610 ***: 'El OCHO DE NOVIEMBRE de mil novecientos VEINTE Y DOS, el Rmo. Sr. Vicario General ... en uso de sus facultades dispensó a Don *** JUAN CARLOS GONZALEZ LERENA *** las tres conciliares proclamas en el matrimonio que intenta contraer con ...'. *** So the date is 8 NOVEMBER 1922, not merely 'the 1920s', and the register of Montevideo dispensations numbers it 14610. *** THE BRIDE'S NAME IS ONLY PARTLY LEGIBLE *** and is not written down here as a reading: the words run '...cepcion Petrona' and then a surname this archive cannot settle between URBANO and a similar hand. *** IT IS NOT GUESSED. *** WHY THIS MAN IS IN THIS REGISTER AT ALL: he is a JUAN CARLOS, which is the forename this whole archive turns on *** - Pablo Armando's father is named Juan Carlos Lerena on the 1908 enrolment card. *** THIS IS NOT HIM AND WAS NEVER CLAIMED TO BE: *** this man carries GONZALEZ as his paternal surname and LERENA as his mother's, and he is marrying at Montevideo in 1922, forty years after Pablo Armando was born at Rosario. He is kept because a Juan Carlos with LERENA anywhere in his name is worth being able to rule out on the record rather than meeting again in five years' time.

name: Rafael LLERENA (Buenos Aires, b. c.1881)
source: San Nicolas de Bari, Retiro, Buenos Aires, baptism of his son, 30 Aug 1910 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:939D-GD9T-LM - IMAGE READ 21 September 2026; film 004571164 image 00201, folio 370
note: *** AN ARGENTINE-BORN LLERENA HOUSEHOLD IN BUENOS AIRES, found 15 September 2026 and new to this archive. *** "bautizo solemnemente ... a JUAN CARLOS que nacio el dia diez de Julio del ano mil novecientos diez, hijo legitimo de D. RAFAEL LLERENA natural del Pais de veinte y nueve anos de edad, y de Dona MARIA CARLOTA AMADEO LASTRA natural del Pais de veinte y siete anos, domiciliados en Calle Cerrito 535." *** His son is called JUAN CARLOS - which is why this record surfaced at all, in a search for Pablo Armando's father. *** *** The son is NOT that man: he was born in 1910. *** *** But the FATHER is the kind of person this archive has been looking for *** - a Llerena born in Argentina about 1881, within a year of Pablo Armando, living in central Buenos Aires. *** Nothing connects him here. He is recorded as a lead, not a relative. *** He sits beside the other unresolved Argentine namesake already in this register, Gilberto Lerena b.1879 who landed in 1928.  *** READ OFF THE PLATE 21 September 2026, and it is a printed form, filled in, at the PARROQUIA DE SAN NICOLAS, BUENOS AIRES, ANO DE 1910. *** Film 004571164 image 00201, folio 370. *** THE CHILD IS A JUAN CARLOS. *** 'bautizo solemnemente a JUAN CARLOS LLERENA, que nacio el dia DIEZ Y SEIS DE JULIO del ano mil novecientos diez, hijo legitimo de D.r D. RAMON LERENA. En dicho dia, mes y ano, Yo Don RAMON LERENA, Alcalde de la Santa Hermandad, notifique la providencia antecedente a Dona CELESTINA GONZALEZ en su persona, de que certifico A FALTA DE ESCRIBANO PUBLICO NI REAL, POR NO HABERLO EN ESTA JURISDICCION. RAMON LERENA.' *** *** SO: an ALCALDE DE LA SANTA HERMANDAD - a rural magistrate of the Spanish countryside jurisdiction - of a PARTIDO DEL ROSARIO, acting on 6 NOVEMBER 1800 *** in the estate of *** DON CLEMENTE GARCIA ***, notifying his widow *** DONA CELESTINA GONZALEZ *** about inventories of goods left to a minor. *** AND HE WROTE. *** He signs twice and certifies in his own hand because there was no notary in the district - which is a plain statement about how thinly governed that country was, and a contrast worth drawing with *** SANCHO LLERENA, who nine years earlier could not sign his name. *** *** IS IT THIS MAN? THE DATE FITS EXACTLY AND THE PLACE IS INDICATED BUT NOT PROVED. *** This row has him flourishing c.1800-1820 at *** ROSARIO ***, and the file elsewhere mentions a *** 'vecindad del partido ORIENTAL' ***, which points at the Banda Oriental and so at ROSARIO ORIENTAL in Colonia - this row's own Rosario. *** BUT THERE IS ALSO A PARTIDO DEL ROSARIO ON THE ARGENTINE SIDE ***, the probate was administered at Buenos Aires, which had viceregal jurisdiction over both banks, and *** THE OCR AROUND THE WORD 'ORIENTAL' IS BROKEN *** - the sentence cannot be read whole. *** NOT MERGED INTO THIS ROW AS FACT. *** *** THE TEST IS CHEAP AND NAMED: *** read further in the same file, where an alcalde's jurisdiction is normally stated in full, and check whether the Partido del Rosario it means is the Oriental one. *** 249 images, item 12 of image group #107093472, and only this frame has been read. *** *** THE PLACE IS SETTLED, AND BY THE COURT'S OWN WORDS - 11 October 2026, hours after this row said it was indicated and not proved. *** The providencia that set the whole business going is at image 22, and it addresses *** 'El Alcalde de la Santa Hermandad del PARTIDO DEL ROSARIO, EN LA OTRA BANDA ORIENTAL de este [Rio]' *** - so the Rosario is *** URUGUAYAN ***, not the Argentine Rosario and not Villa del Rosario in Cordoba. *** AND THE WIDOW IS 'VECINA DEL COLLA'. *** This row has called him 'of Rosario-Colla' since the archive's early weeks, on the strength of the 1858 kinship diagram. *** THE COURT PUTS HIM IN EXACTLY THAT PLACE, HOLDING OFFICE THERE, IN 1800. *** *** WHAT HE WAS DOING, across five weeks: *** *** JOSE RIERA, Alcalde Ordinario de Segundo Voto and Juez de Menores of Buenos Aires ***, ordered him to inventory the estate of *** DON CLEMENTE GARCIA *** because the widow *** DONA CELESTINA GONZALEZ *** was *** RESISTING *** it - she had *** 'pasado a segundas nupcias, teniendo hijo menor' ***. On *** 14 October 1800 *** Ramon went to her house with *** JUAN DE URDINARAN *** and *** FRANCISCO PEREZ DE CEBALLOS *** and notified her *** in the presence of her second husband ***; on the 15th he began at 'la nominada Villa del Rosario'; on *** 6 November *** he decreed and signed; on the *** 11th *** he went again with Perez de Ceballos, *** BARTOLOME PARTIA *** and *** ANDRES PAIS ***; and on the *** 12th *** the appraisal continued before *** NICOLAS YRIGOYEN *** as witness. *** THROUGHOUT HE CERTIFIES 'A FALTA DE ESCRIBANO PUBLICO NI REAL, POR NO HABERLO EN ESTA JURISDICCION' *** and signs his own name. *** AN OBSERVATION THAT IS NOT AN ARGUMENT: *** the 1858 diagram puts *** RAMON LERENA and MARIA GONZALEZ *** at the apex, and the woman at the centre of this file is a *** GONZALEZ of the Colla ***. *** GONZALEZ IS ONE OF THE COMMONEST SURNAMES IN THE RIO DE LA PLATA AND NO CONNECTION IS CLAIMED. *** *** HIS OFFICE GOES BACK FOUR YEARS FURTHER, AND BEFORE IT THERE IS A CAREER - 11 October 2026. *** *** 1796: *** a second probate, that of *** MANUEL CHABO and MARIA MARTA AGAICHU ***, closes *** 'Lo proveyo, mando y firmo D. RAMON LERENA, ALCALDE DE LA SANTA HERMANDAD DEL PARTIDO DEL ROSARIO, a veintiocho dias del mes de OCTUBRE DE MIL SETECIENTOS NOVENTA Y SEIS anos' ***. *** SO HE HELD THE OFFICE AT LEAST 1796-1800, NOT MERELY IN THE ONE YEAR THIS ARCHIVE HAD. *** *** 1794, AND HE IS NOT THE MAGISTRATE YET - THIS IS THE FIND THAT MATTERS. *** In the earlier file on the same estate, the alcalde of the day walks out to *** 'la ESTANCIA del finado Don CLEMENTE GARCIA' *** and there *** 'parecieron ante mi y testigos Don GERONIMO ALONSO y Don RAMON LERENA, SUJETOS NOMBRADOS POR LA VIUDA PARA CONTAR Y TASAR EL GANADO Y CABALLOS de dicha estancia' ***. They were told of the appointment, accepted, *** swore separately *** to do it faithfully, and signed. *** SO IN 1794 HE IS A MAN A WIDOW PICKS TO COUNT HER CATTLE, AND BY 1796 HE IS THE MAGISTRATE OF THE DISTRICT. *** That is the only thing resembling a biography this archive holds for anyone of this family before 1850 - not a birth, a marriage or a death, but *** a trade, a reputation and a rise ***. *** AND IT TELLS US WHAT HE WAS GOOD FOR: *** livestock. A man called in to value cattle and horses on an estancia is a man who knew stock, which is the ordinary competence of the Banda Oriental countryside and the likeliest reason the Santa Hermandad - a rural constabulary - wanted him. *** WHAT HE PRESIDED OVER IN 1796 IS NOT PRETTY, and is recorded because it is the only case of his this archive has read other than the Garcia estate: *** the Chabo petition argues that Maria Marta Agaichu gave her husband a power of attorney without understanding it - *** 'la pobre muchacha criada sin instruccion al lado de sus padres INDIOS GUARANIES, ignorando en todo lo que se le perjudica en el poder que le dio a su marido, TAL VEZ ATEMORIZADA' ***. *** THOSE PEOPLE ARE NOT IN THIS REGISTER AND SHOULD NOT BE *** - he was the official, not a party, which is the boundary written into tools/check-people-named.py the same day. *** A SECOND BAPTISM OF A SON READ AT THE PLATE, 17 October 2026: EUSEBIO CONGENIO, BORN 14 AUGUST 1816 AT THE CORDON. *** The act - 'hijo legitimo de [Ramon] Lerena, natural de MADRID, y de Maria de Leon Gonzalez [...]; abuelos paternos Salvador Lerena y Ana de Cubas; maternos Marcial de Leon Gonzalez y [Isabel ...]; padrino Mauricio de las Mercedes' - gives his birthplace as MADRID where the 1812 La Union act of Manuel Lorenzo has VALDEMORO EN CASTILLA LA NUEVA; the two agree, Valdemoro being a town in that region, and his parents Salvador Lerena and Ana de Cubas are named in both. *** HIS CHILDREN BY THE ACTS READ: *** Manuel Lorenzo (b. 14 November 1812, La Union), Eusebio Congenio (b. 14 August 1816, the Cordon), Luis Manuel (b. 1820, indexed), with Alejandro and Mauricio from their marriage acts. The 1812 and 1816 acts are at Montevideo, so the household moved between Montevideo and the interior in those years - not explained here.

The fuller form is kept here and the indexed form is recorded beside it, because they have not been reconciled on an image.  *** AND THE SAME CANDIDACY AS HER HUSBAND'S ROW, 9 October 2026. *** The Trinidad expedientes name *** MARIA GONZALEZ *** as the wife of Ramon Lerena and the grandmother of Socorro and Bernabe. *** INDEXED HERE AS 'MARIA GONZALES' ON THE 1837 ACT AND WRITTEN 'MARIA GONZALEZ' ON THE 1858 SCHEMA *** - the shorter form now appears in two independent documents, which is why the fuller 'Maria Josefa' is still carried but not relied on. *** NOT MERGED. ***  *** AND THE FULLER FORM IS CONFIRMED ON A PLATE, 9 October 2026. *** This row carried 'MARIA JOSEFA' from the archive's own notes while the 1837 index gave only 'Maria Gonzales', and said the two had 'not been reconciled on an image'. *** THEY ARE NOW: *** her son Alejandro's marriage act of 16 September 1825 writes her *** 'MARIA JOSEFA GONZALEZ' *** in the priest's hand. *** AND HER FAMILY STOOD AT THAT WEDDING: *** the godfather is *** MARCOS DE LEON GONZALEZ ***, which is the DE LEON GONZALEZ of her own parentage. *** NAMED IN A SECOND BAPTISM, 17 October 2026, AS 'MARIA DE LEON GONZALEZ' ***, the mother of Eusebio Congenio (born August 1816, the Cordon); her father is again Marcial de Leon Gonzalez, as in the 1812 act. note: *** A SON OF PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA AND VICENTA VEGA, new to this archive, and named for his father. *** Entered at 16 in household 229. *** The index reads him as 'Pedro a. Serena' - so the index entry that looks like his father is in fact HIM. *** Nothing else about him is known. *** AND ON 12 OCTOBER 2026 A CANDIDATE DEATH - AT MONTEVIDEO, WHICH IS WHERE HE SHOULD BE. *** A 'Pedro a Lerena' died 6 November 1896 aged 69 and was registered the next day as certificate 353 in *** Montevideo. Death Records 1896 ***, with his father given as Pedro A. Lerena and his mother as VICENTA DE LA VEGA - the same parents, and the same peculiar 'Pedro a' name-form this row already notes. His spouse is *** MANUELA LEMOS ***, and a second death, of a Pedro Antonio Lerena born 1875, names the same Manuela as his mother - so the identification would also hand him a wife and a son. *** This row first said the death was at ARTIGAS. It is not; that came from a place filter that falls back to the country, corrected the same day. *** *** NOT MERGED AND NOT TIERED. *** The two birth years disagree by a decade (c.1817 from an age of 16 in the census, 1827 from an age at death), and both are age-derived estimates rather than dates. *** The two birth years still disagree by a decade and both are age-derived, so it is not merged. *** But Montevideo is the city the census put him in, which makes the fit better than the Artigas reading did, not worse. Settled only by the death act itself, which has not been opened. *** AND THE SAME EVENING THE OTHER END OF IT TURNED UP. *** The 1896 death gives his spouse as *** MANUELA LEMOS *** - and this register entered a Manuela LEMOS on 11 October, wife of an unidentified 'Pedro A. LERENA', with children Felicia Clementina (b. c.1868) and Manuel Antonio (b. 31 March 1883), under an explicit note that *** which Pedro she married was not settled. *** *** Two questions asked from opposite ends meet on one record. *** And the age: a man born 1827 fathers a child in 1883 at fifty-six, one born 1817 at sixty-six - so the death record's estimate fits the children better than the census one, which is the reverse of how this row weighted them earlier today. *** Opening the 1896 death act is now the cheapest thing that would attach a whole Montevideo line to this archive's trunk. *** *** AND THE ACT WAS OPENED THE SAME EVENING. *** Acta 353: he died at five in the afternoon of 6 November 1896 at calle Rivera No. 163, of tisis pulmonar, certified by Dr Vitale, before Vicente Carricaonde, Juez de Paz of the 15th section. The act reads: *** 'nacido en Montevideo', 'de sesenta y nueve anos de edad', 'hijo legitimo de Don PEDRO A. LERENA, oriental, fallecido, y de Dona VICENTA DE LA VEGA, oriental, fallecida'. *** His wife is named as Dona Manuela, oriental, 53, and the children as *** Antonio, Carlos Teodoro and Manuel Antonio ***, with the first declarant - Don Pedro A. Lerena, soltero, empleado - declared to be the dead man's son. *** SO THE ATTACHMENT IS NO LONGER A CANDIDATE: the act names his parents. *** What is now in doubt is the CENSUS DATE. Sixty-nine in 1896 means born about 1827, and a man born in 1827 is six in 1833, not sixteen - he is sixteen in 1843. *** Either household 229 is later than this archive dates it, or the sixteen-year-old is a different son of the same couple. *** *** THE CENSUS IS THE PADRON OF 1850, NOT c.1833 - CORRECTED 12 OCTOBER 2026. *** The catalogue lists film 7499042 item by item: item 1 is libro 263, 1843; *** item 2, where this household sits, is LIBRO 264, 1850. *** *** So this birth year moved seventeen years later. *** And the head of the household, entered at forty, was born about 1810 - *** not the Pedro Antonio Lerena born 31 July 1793 whom this archive had read him as. *** Either the census age is badly wrong or the household belongs to a different Pedro A. Lerena married to a different Vicenta Vega; under the neighbouring book, 1843, he would still be born about 1803 and still not be the man of 1793. See data/corrections.tsv. His burial is entered at the Cordon on 8 November 1896: 'Pedro Lerena [the transcript has Lorena], de sesenta y nueve anos, casado con Manuela Lemos [Loma], orientales. Fallecio ayer.' Name, age and wife agree with the civil act. The burial says 'ayer' on the 8th and the civil act says he died on the 6th, so the 'ayer' is not a date. *** HIS BAPTISM IS FOUND AND READ AT THE PLATE, 17 October 2026, AND IT SETTLES HIS BIRTH YEAR: BORN 1 DECEMBER 1828. *** 'En doze de Diciembre del ano de mil ochocientos veinte y ocho yo D. Benito Alonso Covian Teniente Cura en esta Vice Parroquia de Nra Sra del Carmen la Mayor en el Cordon extramuros de Monte Video bautice solemnemente a Pedro Antonio Natalio, que nacio el dia primero del corriente, hijo [legitimo] de Dn Pedro Antonio Llerena, natural de Canelones, y de Da Vicenta Vega, natural de Monte Video. Fueron padrinos Ygnacio Perez y Gregoria Silba.' The margin reads 'Pedro Antonio Natalio Llerena, Parvulo'. *** HIS CENSUS AGE OF 16 IN 1850 WAS SIX YEARS LATE (it gave c.1834), and the 'c.1817' of an earlier reading was eleven years early; the age at death, 69 in 1896, would give 1827 - one year off. *** *** HIS FULL NAME IS PEDRO ANTONIO NATALIO, *** and that briefly made him a candidate for the 'Pedro Antonio Lerena' who was Teresa Leonar's husband. *** HE IS NOT: *** the 1864 christening of Teresa's daughter Manuela names her husband's parents as Pedro and Maria Pereyra, and this man's mother was Vicenta Vega. His own baptism names no grandparents. *** A THIRD CANDIDATE FOR THE CORDON FATHER OF 1862-63, 18 October 2026: *** a 'D. Pedro A. Lerena' with a wife 'Da. Trinidad Morales, orientales' baptised a daughter Amelia (born 2 May 1862) at the Cordon on 8 February 1863. He cannot be Teresa Leonard's husband (the dispensation of June 1861 and the christening of their daughter in 1864 have him with Teresa), and may be THIS man - 'Pedro A.', baptised at the Cordon in 1828, with a first wife Trinidad Morales before Manuela Lemos - but no act says whose son he is, so he is entered apart and NOT MERGED.

name: Maria LLERENA (Espanola, 60, head of Casa 2)

name: Justo LERENA (of the Cordon)
source: Uruguay, registros parroquiales, 1726-2000 - burial of Carmen Lerena, Cementerio del Cordon, Montevideo, 14 August 1841; ark 1:1:XSXM-CN7Q, *** IMAGE READ *** film 007713392 image 2511, 20 September 2026
note: *** A LERENA FATHER THIS ARCHIVE HAD NEVER MET, found 20 September 2026. *** Named on the burial act of his daughter Carmen at the Cementerio del Cordon on 14 August 1841: *** "hija legitima de Justo Lerena y de Juana Quinta[na]" ***, read off the image. So he was a married man with a three-year-old in Montevideo in 1841, which puts his own birth somewhere around 1810 or earlier. *** NOTHING TIES HIM TO SANCHO. *** Sancho had a daughter JUSTA born about 1802 and the forename echoes; that is an echo and not an argument. The 1812 padron lists six children and no Justo, but the published child lists for that couple are demonstrably incomplete - the prose claims eight and names seven, and omits Dominga, whom a census and an act both attest - so he can be neither placed nor excluded. *** He was found by a search for something else entirely: *** a sweep of Uruguayan deaths 1815-1840 looking for Fidel.

source: Uruguay, registros parroquiales, 1726-2000 - burial of Carmen Lerena, Cementerio del Cordon, Montevideo, 14 August 1841; ark 1:1:XSXM-CN7Q, *** IMAGE READ *** film 007713392 image 2511, 20 September 2026

name: Carlos LERENA (of Mendoza, m. Adela CAMIGLIA)
source: Argentina, Mendoza, Catholic Church Records - baptism of Avelino Carlos Lerena, San Nicolas de Tolentino, 12 Mar 1904, naming the parents; and Santiago Apostol y San Nicolas (Iglesia Matriz de Mendoza), Baptism Records 1899-1901 - baptism of 6 January 1900; DGS film 004597291 image 69, waypoint Q633-3DR, ark 3:1:939X-HF9M-7S - PLATE READ 9 October 2026; and Santiago Apostol y San Nicolas (Iglesia Matriz de Mendoza), Baptism Records 1901-1903 - printed-form baptism of 23 April 1902; DGS film 004597291 item 003 image 95, ark 3:1:939X-HFTB-Z - PLATE READ 9 October 2026
note: *** A SECOND CARLOS LERENA, AND THE REGISTER HAS SAID SO SINCE 14 SEPTEMBER WITHOUT GIVING HIM A ROW. *** He is named with *** ADELA CAMIGLIA *** as the parents of AVELINO CARLOS LERENA, baptised at San Nicolas de Tolentino, Mendoza, on 12 March 1904. *** HE IS NOT CARLOS AUGUSTO FEDERICO LERENA SALVANACH, *** the son of Gilberto who married Rosa Maria Eppens at Retiro in 1914: that act calls its groom *** SOLTERO *** at thirty, and Mendoza is a long way from Buenos Aires. The distinction was made on the Eppens row - "two men, one name" - but the relationship file went on attaching Adela and Avelino to the wrong man until the two rows were merged on 20 September and the disagreement became visible. *** NOTHING IS KNOWN OF HIM BEYOND THE ACT *** - not a birth, not a marriage, not a place of origin. *** HE IS ORIENTAL - URUGUAYAN - AND THAT ANSWERS ONE OF THE FOUR OPEN QUESTIONS ON /open-questions/, 9 October 2026. *** The baptism of his daughter *** MARIA ADELA *** at the Iglesia Matriz de Mendoza on 6 January 1900 calls the parents '*** orientales, domiciliados en este Curato ***'. data/cajon-985-origins.tsv had his origin as 'Not established'. *** SO FOUR OF THE CAJON 985 FATHERS ARE NOW TRACEABLE AND EVERY ONE IS URUGUAYAN OR MARRIED IN URUGUAY ***, which is a base rate that bears on Juan Carlos Lerena without naming him. *** AND AN AVELINO LERENA STOOD GODFATHER TO HIS DAUGHTER, BY PROXY: *** 'padrinos Domingo Simois *** por ABELINO LERENA ***'. This register holds *** FOUR *** men of that name and the act gives him no age, no patronymic and no residence - *** SO HE IS NOT PLACED IN ANY BRANCH, AND THE REASON IS ON THE RECORD: *** the Arturo Lerena row of that same file was once written as a son of Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel and withdrawn the same day as a conflation. *** THE NAME OF HIS WIFE IS ALSO WRONG IN THIS ROW'S TITLE: *** the act and the army index both write *** CARNIGLIA ***, with an r. *** AND THE CITY, AN HOUR AFTER THE COUNTRY. *** His second daughter's baptism of 23 April 1902 is on a PRINTED FORM - 'Partidas de Bautismos de la Parroquia Matriz de Mendoza' - with a *** 'natural de' blank for each parent ***, and it reads '*** Hija legitima de D. CARLOS LERENA, natural de MONTEVIDEO ***'. *** THE 1900 ACT COULD ONLY SAY 'ORIENTALES' BECAUSE IT WAS PROSE; THE 1902 FORM ASKS THE QUESTION. *** *** SO HE IS A MONTEVIDEAN IN MENDOZA ***, and the fourth traceable father of Cajon 985 - none of whom is Argentine. *** AND A SECOND LERENA STOOD GODPARENT TO A CHILD OF HIS, AGAIN BY PROXY: *** *** MERCEDES LERENA DE MARTINEZ ***, represented by the child's own mother. *** TWO LERENA GODPARENTS, NEITHER PRESENT - which is what relatives in another country do. ***

name: Avelino Eduardo LERENA Traibel
source: Uruguay, registros parroquiales 1726-2000 - christening of Avelino Pedro Joaquin Silvestre, Union, Montevideo, 5 Mar 1866, ark 1:1:6D7Z-JGH2; and of Pedro Gualberto, Cordon, Montevideo, 15 Jan 1870; index read 20 September 2026; and named as GODFATHER at the Iglesia Matriz christening of Angelica Maria Lerena Villademoros, 29 September 1872 - ark 1:1:6DFQ-YF26 - IMAGE READ 27 September 2026; film 004298263 image 03147; and Uruguay, Civil Registration - Montevideo, 4a seccion, MARRIAGE act No. 83 of 20 November 1897, folio 42, expediente No. 94 - *** PLATE READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-N35B-M; index ark 1:1:XS6K-MYFD; volume 'Montevideo. Marriage Records 1896-1897, 1900, 1898-1899'
note: *** A FORK THIS ARCHIVE REFUSED TO CHOOSE IS NOW DECIDED, 20 September 2026. *** On 16 September a working log found a branch indexed *** LERENA VILLADEMOROS *** and set out two readings without picking one: either *** Avelino Lerena Fernandez (b.1815) married twice ***, Ambrosia Traibel and then Celedonia Villademoros, *** or Avelino Eduardo is a SON of his. *** It is the son. Two separate parish acts give this man's own father as *** AVELINO SERENA/LERENA *** with *** AMBROSIA TRAIBEL *** named on the record - so he is a child of that marriage, and the Villademoros children are Sancho's great-grandchildren. *** HE IS THEREFORE A NEW CHILD OF AVELINO AND AMBROSIA, *** beside Alejandro, Josefa, Ana Rosario, Alfredo Justiniano and Mercedes. He married *** CELEDONIA VILLADEMOROS ***, daughter of Pedro Villademoros and Angelica Mendez. *** INDEX-LEVEL: *** both acts are machine-indexed and neither image has been opened here. *** AND THE TEST NAMED ABOVE WAS RUN THE SAME EVENING AND CAME BACK EMPTY. *** LERENA with spouse surname VILLADEMOROS, Uruguay: 6,352 records, and *** not one of them is a marriage act. *** Every hit is a parent entry on somebody else's baptism or civil registration. *** The control is the one that worked two hours earlier: *** the same query shape on LERENA with spouse JUANICO puts the marriage act of 19 December 1864 at RANK ONE. So the shape finds a marriage when there is one to find. *** NEITHER VILLADEMOROS MARRIAGE IS IN THE INDEXED RECORD, *** and the brothers-and-sisters reading stays an inference. It would be settled by the parish marriage books of the Cordon and Union, which have not been walked.  *** AND HE HAS MORE CHILDREN THAN THIS ARCHIVE COULD SEE, FOUND 21 September 2026 BY DELETING A SEARCH PARAMETER. *** A parent-pair query on him with CELEDONIA VILLADEMOROS returns *** ZERO ***. Dropping the mother's SURNAME and keeping only 'Celedonia' returns *** SEVEN *** - including the two christenings this archive already held, which is how the zero was known to be false. The seven add: *** PEDRO SEGUNDO LERENA VILLADEMOROS, who died at Montevideo on 23 August 1936 aged 66, certificate 150, married to PAULINA PRANDO ALGAR ***; *** an AVELINO LERENA who died at Montevideo on 5 January 1914 aged 45, certificate 9, married to CARMEN LORENTE ***, whose mother is written CELEDONIA VILLADEMORO without the s; and marriage registrations of 1921 for both Avelino Pedro Joaquin Silvestre and Pedro Gualberto. *** WHETHER THAT IS FOUR CHILDREN OR TWO IS NOT SETTLED AND IS NOT GUESSED HERE. *** Pedro Segundo's estimated 1870 sits on Pedro Gualberto's birth of 19 October 1869; the 1914 Avelino's estimated 1869 sits four years off Avelino Pedro Joaquin Silvestre's December 1865 - and a man who died in 1914 cannot register a marriage in 1921. *** The ages come from death certificates and are the weakest field there is. *** TEST: the two 1921 marriage registrations, which would show which of these men were alive to marry. *** HE IS ARGENTINO ON THE PLATE, 27 September 2026, and that is new. *** The Iglesia Matriz act of 29 September 1872 calls him 'AVELINO LERENA, *** argentino ***' and his wife 'CELEDONIA VILLADEMOROS, *** argentina ***'. *** AND IT NAMES HIS PARENTS: 'Abuelos paternos AVELINO y AMBROSIA TRAIBEL' *** - so his descent from Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel is on a parish act and no longer rests on the index alone. A THIRD CHILD is added from it: Angelica Maria, born 8 April 1872. *** HE HAS A DEATH AT LAST, AND IT IS IN CANELONES - 11 October 2026. *** His daughter Angelica's marriage act of 20 November 1897 describes him as *** 'Don AVELINO, ORIENTAL, FALLECIDO EN CANELONES EN EL ANO DE 1895' *** - and his widow Celedonia is party to the same act, so the statement is hers. *** SO HE DIED IN 1895, IN THE DEPARTMENT OF CANELONES ***, not at Montevideo where this archive has always had the family. *** AND IT BEARS ON A READING THIS ARCHIVE WITHDREW, WITHOUT REVIVING IT. *** On 22 September the claim that *** AVELINO LERENA FERNANDEZ *** - his FATHER - died at “La Paz, Canelones” was withdrawn, because the father died at Montevideo on 22 August 1890. *** THAT RETRACTION STANDS. *** But the secondary tree file it came from now looks less like invention and more like *** A CONFUSION OF FATHER WITH SON ***: there IS an Avelino Lerena who died in Canelones, and it is this one. *** THE PRECISE PLACE WITHIN CANELONES IS NOT STATED HERE *** and nothing in this act says La Paz. *** THE NEXT RECORD TO FIND IS HIS OWN DEATH ACT, Canelones, 1895. ***

name: Celedonia VILLADEMOROS (wife of Avelino Eduardo)
source: Uruguay, registros parroquiales 1726-2000 - christening of Avelino Pedro Joaquin Silvestre, Union, Montevideo, 5 Mar 1866, ark 1:1:6D7Z-JGH2; and of Pedro Gualberto, Cordon, Montevideo, 15 Jan 1870; index read 20 September 2026; and named as GODFATHER at the Iglesia Matriz christening of Angelica Maria Lerena Villademoros, 29 September 1872 - ark 1:1:6DFQ-YF26 - IMAGE READ 27 September 2026; film 004298263 image 03147; and Uruguay, Civil Registration - Montevideo, 4a seccion, MARRIAGE act No. 83 of 20 November 1897, folio 42, expediente No. 94 - *** PLATE READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-N35B-M; index ark 1:1:XS6K-MYFD; volume 'Montevideo. Marriage Records 1896-1897, 1900, 1898-1899'; and Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, Cordon, Montevideo - RELIGIOUS MARRIAGE of 28 December 1871 - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-B3DF-C, volume 'Religious Marriage Records January 1866-May 1872'
note: Wife of *** AVELINO EDUARDO LERENA TRAIBEL ***, and daughter of *** PEDRO VILLADEMOROS and ANGELICA MENDEZ ***. Mother of Avelino Pedro Joaquin Silvestre (b. December 1865), Pedro Gualberto (b. 19 October 1869) and, on civil registration indexes, Pedro Segundo and Angelica Maria. *** The surname is a notable Uruguayan one and no claim is made about that here. *** Index-level. *** ARGENTINA, on the Iglesia Matriz act of 29 September 1872 ***, where her daughter Angelica Maria is baptised and her own parents are named as *** PEDRO and ANGELICA MENDEZ ***. Her sister or kinswoman ELISA VILLADEMOROS stood godmother, with ALEJANDRO M. LERENA. *** A WIDOW BY 1897, AND AN AGE. *** Her daughter Angelica's marriage act of 20 November 1897 gives *** 'Dona CELEDONIA VILLADEMOROS, de 55 anos, de estado VIUDA, de profesion labores de su sexo, de nacionalidad ARGENTINA, domiciliada en esta Ciudad' *** - so born about *** 1842 ***, *** ARGENTINE *** as the 1872 baptism also says, and *** WIDOWED *** by her husband's death in Canelones in 1895. She was living at Montevideo in 1897. *** HER NAME IS SPELLED IN FULL AND CORRECTLY ON THIS ACT ***, which is worth saying of an index that turned her husband into 'Arabia Larena Lerena' and 'Ardino Serena'. *** HER SISTER'S MARRIAGE ACT PROVES THE SISTERHOOD, 11 October 2026. *** The Cordon act of 28 December 1871 makes *** ELISA VILLADEMOROS *** the daughter of *** the late D. PEDRO and Dona ANGELICA VILLADEMOROS ***, which is this row's own couple. *** SO ELISA IS HER SISTER AND ALEJANDRO MAXIMO LERENA IS HER BROTHER-IN-LAW TWICE OVER *** - he is also her husband's brother. *** AND IT ESTABLISHES A PATTERN THIS ARCHIVE HAS NOW SEEN TWICE IN ONE DAY: TWO BROTHERS MARRIED TWO SISTERS. *** *** ALEJANDRO MAXIMO LERENA *** and *** AVELINO EDUARDO LERENA TRAIBEL *** are both sons of *** AVELINO LERENA FERNANDEZ and AMBROSIA TRAIBEL ***; *** ELISA *** and *** CELEDONIA VILLADEMOROS *** are both daughters of *** PEDRO VILLADEMOROS and ANGELICA ***. *** SO THE LERENA VILLADEMOROS COUSINS ARE DOUBLE FIRST COUSINS *** - exactly the structure that forced a dispensation at Trinidad in 1911, here produced in Montevideo a generation earlier. *** NO DISPENSATION OF KINSHIP WAS NEEDED FOR THE MARRIAGES THEMSELVES ***, because the two families were not related before them; what was dispensed in 1871 was *** TWO CONCILIAR BANNS ***, a dispensation of notice and not of blood.

source: Uruguay, registros parroquiales 1726-2000 - christening of Alejandro Joaquin Narciso Lerena, Cordon, Montevideo, 29 May 1873; ark 1:1:6D3Z-WTXR; index read 20 September 2026 - IMAGE READ 27 September 2026; film 007713388 image 02091; and named as GODFATHER at the Iglesia Matriz christening of Angelica Maria Lerena Villademoros, 29 September 1872 - ark 1:1:6DFQ-YF26 - IMAGE READ 27 September 2026; film 004298263 image 03147; and the Cordon christening of his daughter Jacinta Mercedes Gregoria, 26 December 1877 - ark 1:1:6D3Z-WP5Z - IMAGE READ 27 September 2026; film 007713388 image 02455; and Argentina, Cordoba, Catholic Church Records 1557-1974 - his marriage at Inmaculada Concepcion, Bell Ville, Union, Cordoba, 1907; index read 27 September 2026; and named as a deceased parent on her son's marriage act, Cordoba, 20 June 1907 - IMAGE READ 27 September 2026; film 004484760 image 00123; and Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, Cordon, Montevideo - RELIGIOUS MARRIAGE of 28 December 1871 - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-B3DF-C, volume 'Religious Marriage Records January 1866-May 1872'
note: Named as the mother at the Cordon christening of *** ALEJANDRO JOAQUIN NARCISO LERENA *** on 29 May 1873. *** Probably a sister of CELEDONIA VILLADEMOROS ***, who married Avelino Eduardo Lerena in the same decade - see his row and her husband's. The spelling VILLARDEMOROS is the index's; Celedonia is indexed VILLADEMOROS. Index-level. *** SHE IS NAMED BESIDE ALEJANDRO M. LERENA AT A FONT IN 1872, *** as godmother to Angelica Maria, daughter of her kinswoman Celedonia. *** IF SHE IS THE FIRST WIFE OF THE ALEJANDRO M. LERENA WHO WAS A WIDOWER IN NOVEMBER 1886, THEN SHE DIED BETWEEN 1873 AND 1886 *** - and a Montevideo death in that window is a findable record and is the next thing to look for. Her surname is written VILLADEMOROS on the 1872 act and VILLARDEMOROS in the 1873 index. *** HER DEATH IS NOW BRACKETED TO FIFTEEN MONTHS, 27 September 2026. *** The Cordon act of 26 December 1877 calls her *** '(hoy finada)' *** - dead that day - and her daughter Jacinta Mercedes Gregoria was born *** 19 September 1876 ***. *** SO ELISA VILLADEMOROS DIED BETWEEN 19 SEPTEMBER 1876 AND 26 DECEMBER 1877 ***, and a Montevideo burial in that window is a findable record. That death is what makes Alejandro M. Lerena a WIDOWER on the acts of 1886 and 1888, nine years later. *** HER DEATH IS NOT IN THE INDEXED CORPUS, AND THAT IS EXPECTED RATHER THAN PUZZLING. *** Searched 27 September 2026 across Uruguayan records 1874-1880: no death or burial for an Elisa Villademoros. *** SHE DIED BETWEEN SEPTEMBER 1876 AND DECEMBER 1877, WHICH IS BEFORE URUGUAY HAD CIVIL REGISTRATION AT ALL *** - the registers begin in 1879. So her death is a PARISH BURIAL, in books this archive has on its work list to walk by image and has not walked. *** THE WINDOW IS FIFTEEN MONTHS AND THE PARISH IS ALMOST CERTAINLY THE CORDON ***, where both her children were baptised. That is a cheap walk and it would name her parents. *** HER NAME REACHES ARGENTINA IN 1907, thirty years after her death ***, on her son's marriage act at Bell Ville, Cordoba - spelled *** VILLADEMORAS ***, a fourth variant after Villademoros, Villardemoros and Villademores. *** AND THE CORDOBA ACT OF 1907 CONFIRMS HER DEATH ON A PLATE ***, thirty years after the Cordon christening that first recorded it: 'hijo legitimo de Alejandro M. [Lerena] y *** ELISA VILLADEMORAS (FINADOS) ***'. *** HER PARENTS ARE NAMED AND THE SISTERHOOD IS NO LONGER A GUESS, 11 October 2026. *** Her marriage act of *** 28 December 1871 *** gives her as *** 'Dona ELISA VILLADEMOROS, del mismo estado y oriundez, hija de los finados D. PEDRO y Dona ANGELICA VILLADEMOROS' *** - so *** SOLTERA ***, *** NATURAL DE MONTEVIDEO *** like her husband, and *** THE DAUGHTER OF A PEDRO AND AN ANGELICA WHO WERE BOTH ALREADY DEAD ***. *** CELEDONIA VILLADEMOROS IS THE DAUGHTER OF PEDRO VILLADEMOROS AND ANGELICA MENDEZ. *** Same father, same mother, same city. *** THEY ARE SISTERS, AND THIS ROW HAS SAID 'PROBABLY' SINCE SEPTEMBER. *** *** AND IT SETTLES THE 1873 GODMOTHER TOO: *** this register holds a 'Dona Angelica Villademoros' standing at the font for Elisa's son in May 1873. *** SHE CANNOT BE THE MOTHER, WHO WAS DEAD BY DECEMBER 1871 *** - so she is a third sister, which is what this archive had reasoned and could not prove. *** AND IT ESTABLISHES A PATTERN THIS ARCHIVE HAS NOW SEEN TWICE IN ONE DAY: TWO BROTHERS MARRIED TWO SISTERS. *** *** ALEJANDRO MAXIMO LERENA *** and *** AVELINO EDUARDO LERENA TRAIBEL *** are both sons of *** AVELINO LERENA FERNANDEZ and AMBROSIA TRAIBEL ***; *** ELISA *** and *** CELEDONIA VILLADEMOROS *** are both daughters of *** PEDRO VILLADEMOROS and ANGELICA ***. *** SO THE LERENA VILLADEMOROS COUSINS ARE DOUBLE FIRST COUSINS *** - exactly the structure that forced a dispensation at Trinidad in 1911, here produced in Montevideo a generation earlier. *** NO DISPENSATION OF KINSHIP WAS NEEDED FOR THE MARRIAGES THEMSELVES ***, because the two families were not related before them; what was dispensed in 1871 was *** TWO CONCILIAR BANNS ***, a dispensation of notice and not of blood.

name: Alejandro Joaquin Narciso LERENA Villardemoros
source: Uruguay, registros parroquiales 1726-2000 - christening of Alejandro Joaquin Narciso Lerena, Cordon, Montevideo, 29 May 1873; ark 1:1:6D3Z-WTXR; index read 20 September 2026 - IMAGE READ 27 September 2026; film 007713388 image 02091; and Argentina, Cordoba, Catholic Church Records 1557-1974 - his marriage at Inmaculada Concepcion, Bell Ville, Union, Cordoba, 1907; index read 27 September 2026 - IMAGE READ 27 September 2026; film 004484760 image 00123, entry N 282, Parroquia de San Jeronimo, Cordoba
note: Born *** 29 October 1872 *** and christened at the *** Iglesia del Cordon on 29 May 1873 ***, son of Alejandro Lerena and Elisa Villardemoros. *** His godparents are the interesting part: *** JOAQUIN REGUSA Y GARCIA and *** ANGELICA VILLADEMOROS ***. The first is almost certainly the JOAQUIN REQUENA named on the 1866 christening of Avelino Pedro Joaquin Silvestre, his probable first cousin; the second carries his mother's surname. *** The child's own second forename is JOAQUIN ***, for the godfather, which is how this family names. Index-level. *** READ OFF THE PLATE 27 September 2026. *** 'En veinte y nueve de Mayo [de 1873] el Cura y Vicario bautizo solemnemente a ALEJANDRO JOAQUIN NARCISO, nacido el veinte y nueve de Octubre, hijo legitimo de D. ALEJANDRO LERENA [y Da. ELISA VILLADEMOROS], orientales. Padrinos D. JOAQUIN REGUSA y Da. ANGELICA VILLADEMOROS.' *** NO GRANDPARENTS ARE NAMED ***, which is the one thing this plate was opened for. *** HE CROSSED TO ARGENTINA AND MARRIED THERE, found 27 September 2026. *** Marriage 1907 at the *** Inmaculada Concepcion, BELL VILLE, departamento Union, CORDOBA *** - to *** AMALIA CASAS ***, with his parents given as 'ALEJANDRO M LERENA' and 'ELISA VILLADEMORAS'. *** SO THE SON OF THE FIRST MARRIAGE WENT TO ARGENTINA TOO. *** His half-brothers and half-sisters by Julia Bassani were born at Montevideo, then Misiones, then Buenos Aires; he is in CORDOBA. *** INDEX ONLY - no image opened. *** A marriage act names the groom's parents, his age and often his birthplace, so this plate is worth opening: it would be a FOURTH independent statement of his father's name and might date him. *** READ OFF THE PLATE 27 September 2026, and it gives four things the index did not. *** The act, entry N 282: 'El dia *** VEINTE DE JUNIO *** del ano mil novecientos y siete ... el Teniente Pbro. autorizado por el infrascripto Cura del Curato de *** SAN JERONIMO ***, Provincia y Obispado de Cordoba, en la [Iglesia - struck out] *** CASA PARTICULAR DE LA NOVIA ***, *** DISPENSADAS *** las moniciones canonicas, autorizo el matrimonio de ALEJANDRO JOAQUIN *** LERENA ***, de *** TREINTA Y CUATRO *** anos de edad, *** NATURAL DE MONTEVIDEO, REPUBLICA ORIENTAL ***, domiciliado en este Curato, e hijo legitimo de *** ALEJANDRO M. [LERENA] y ELISA VILLADEMORAS (FINADOS) ***, con *** AMALIA CASAS ***, vecina de este pueblo, hija legitima de *** CORNELIO CASAS y RAIMUNDA PEREDA ***.' *** THE INDEX SAID ONLY '1907' AND 'Inmaculada Concepcion, Bell Ville'; THE PLATE SAYS 20 JUNE AND SAN JERONIMO. *** And the index read the surname *** SERENA ***: on the plate the initial is a clear L, set beside the scribe's own S in 'San Jeronimo' on the same opening. *** SIXTH S-FOR-L. *** Age 34 in June 1907 fits his birth of 29 October 1872. *** THE BANNS WERE DISPENSED AND THEY MARRIED IN THE BRIDE'S HOUSE RATHER THAN THE CHURCH, which is what haste or illness looks like on a parish form. ***

note: *** THE ALEJANDRO M. LERENA OF THE ARMY ENROLMENT CARDS, CAJON 985 - and the M. is on the acts, in the clerk's hand, not only in the index. *** He appeared in person twice: on 6 November 1886, "parecieron don Alejandro M. Lerena, de cuarenta y dos anos de edad, viudo, escribano, oriental, domiciliado en la calle San Jose N 17"; and again in March 1888, "comparecieron don Alejandro M. Lerena de 43 anos de edad de estado viudo de nacionalidad Oriental". *** TWO AGES SIXTEEN MONTHS APART, CONSISTENT WITH EACH OTHER, PUT HIS BIRTH BETWEEN 17 MARCH AND 6 NOVEMBER 1844. *** The tree's "born Uruguay 1839" is five years out on both acts and is a tree value, not a record. *** HE IS A WIDOWER IN 1886 *** while Julia Bassani is twenty-two and soltera, so there is an earlier marriage and an earlier death in Montevideo - and a marriage act names the groom's parents, which is now the shortest route to his parentage. *** THE 1888 ACT IS A PRINTED FORM WHOSE RULED LINE READS "Que es nieta por linea paterna de ______" AND THE LINE IS BLANK. *** So is the maternal one. The form asked this archive's question and nobody wrote the answer on it. *** NOT MERGED with Alejandro LERENA TRAIBEL *** (b. 1843 or 1845, son of Avelino) - the ages miss both of that man's candidate dates by one year, in opposite directions, which cannot choose between them. See data/the-three-alejandros.tsv. *** MAXIMO IS NOW ATTESTED ON A PLATE, 22 September 2026, and not only in the tree. *** His son Hector's marriage act of 25 February 1911 at San Carlos, Buenos Aires, names him in the priest's hand as "D. *** ALEJANDRO MAXIMO *** [Lerena], natural de la Rep. Oriental". So the bare "M." of the two Montevideo birth acts expands to MAXIMO, and the *** Alejandro M. Lerena of army Cajon 985 has the same expansion ***. He was still being named as a living father's name in Buenos Aires in 1911. *** AND HIS FIRST WIFE MAY BE NAMED AT LAST, 27 September 2026. *** He is *** viudo *** on both Montevideo acts of 1886 and 1888, and this archive has been hunting the marriage that made him one. The Iglesia Matriz act of 29 September 1872 names the godparents of a Lerena Traibel child as *** 'ALEJANDRO M. LERENA y ELISA VILLADEMOROS, a quienes instruyo' *** - read off the plate. *** THE M. IS THE TELL: *** no other Alejandro in this register carries it, and the archive's separate row 'Alejandro LERENA (m. Elisa VILLARDEMOROS)' has a son christened at the Cordon on 29 May 1873. *** THIS IS NOT YET A MERGE *** - the two rows still stand, and data/_person-pairs.txt has been rewritten to say why the old reason for keeping them apart was wrong. A man who is a WIDOWER in 1886 and a husband in 1872 is one man with two wives in sequence, which is the ordinary case and is exactly what this archive mistook for two men. *** ANSWERED, 27 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND IT IS THE QUESTION THIS ARCHIVE HAS CARRIED SINCE 14 SEPTEMBER. *** data/the-three-alejandros.tsv called his parentage 'NOT KNOWN ... This is the whole obstacle'. *** HIS PARENTS ARE AVELINO LERENA AND AMBROSIA TRAIBEL. *** The Cordon act of 26 December 1877, read off film 007713388 image 02455: 'hija legitima de D. ALEJANDRO M. LERENA y de D.a ELISA [VILLADEMOROS] (hoy finada), orientales. *** ABUELOS PATERNOS D. AVELINO y D.a AMBROSIA TRAIBEL ***'. *** SO THE ALEJANDRO M. LERENA OF ARMY DRAWER CAJON 985 IS A LERENA TRAIBEL *** - a grandson of Sancho Llerena, and a brother of Josefa, Alberto, Alfredo Justiniano, Ana Rosario and the rest. *** AND THE WIDOWHOOD IS DATED. *** Elisa is 'HOY FINADA' on 26 December 1877 and her daughter was born 19 September 1876, so she died inside those fifteen months - which is why he is 'viudo' on both Montevideo acts of 1886 and 1888. *** WHAT REMAINS IS ONE ROW, NOT ONE QUESTION: *** this register also holds ALEJANDRO LERENA TRAIBEL, baptised at La Mauricia on 7 January 1846, a son of the same couple with the same forename, whose birth the act puts at 29 May 1843 or 1845 against the 1844 these acts give. Same parents, same name, compatible dates. They are almost certainly one man and are not yet merged; see data/_person-pairs.txt. *** AND HIS MARRIAGE TO ELISA IS A CONTROLLED NULL, 27 September 2026. *** Searched under LERENA and under *** SERENA *** - the spelling that hid the 1877 act - for a marriage to a Villademoros in Uruguay: nothing. *** THE CONTROL PASSED IN THE SAME MINUTES: *** the Montevideo parish marriage of Luis Lerena and Julia Juanico, 19 December 1864 at San Francisco de Asis, returns with the groom's parents attached - so marriages of that era and city ARE indexed, and they DO carry the parents. *** THE NULL THEREFORE MEANS THE ACT IS NOT IN THE INDEXED CORPUS, NOT THAT IT DOES NOT EXIST. *** Their eldest known child was born 29 October 1872, so the marriage falls about 1868-1872, most likely at the Cordon. It would name his parents a second time and give his AGE, which is the one thing that would separate the 1843 reading from the 1845. *** AND A THIRD RECORD PAIRS HIM WITH ELISA VILLADEMOROS, this time in ARGENTINA. *** His son Alejandro Joaquin married at Bell Ville, Cordoba, in 1907, and the act names the groom's parents as *** 'ALEJANDRO M LERENA' and 'ELISA VILLADEMORAS' ***. The Montevideo font of 1872, the Cordon christening of 1877 and now a Cordoba marriage of 1907 all carry the same couple and the same initial. *** AND HE WAS DEAD BY 20 JUNE 1907, WHICH IS THE FIRST EVIDENCE OF HIS DEATH FROM ANY RECORD. *** His son Alejandro Joaquin's marriage at San Jeronimo, Cordoba, names the groom 'hijo legitimo de *** ALEJANDRO M. [LERENA] y ELISA VILLADEMORAS (FINADOS) ***' - both parents deceased, on the plate. *** SO HIS DEATH FALLS BETWEEN MARCH 1888, when he appeared in person at Montevideo to register Emilia Alberta, AND JUNE 1907. *** The family tree's '1903' sits inside that bracket and now has a record-based ceiling for the first time, though the tree's date itself is still only a tree's. *** AND THE ACT IS A FOURTH INDEPENDENT STATEMENT OF HIS NAME WITH THE M. *** - Montevideo 1872, the Cordon 1877, Buenos Aires 1911, and now Cordoba 1907. *** AND ON 9 OCTOBER 2026 HE WAS MERGED WITH THE 'ALEJANDRO LERENA (m. ELISA VILLARDEMOROS)' THIS REGISTER CARRIED SEPARATELY. *** They were *** PROVED THE SAME MAN ON 27 SEPTEMBER *** and kept apart for twelve days afterwards for a reason the pair file states in terms: *** 'a merge touches slugs, last-attested-alive.tsv, relations.tsv and the CHECKED_PAIRS in tools/consistency.py, and a half-done merge is worse than an honest pair. THIS LINE IS A DEBT, NOT A JUDGEMENT.' *** The debt is paid. *** WHAT PROVED IT: *** the Cordon act of 26 December 1877, film 007713388 image 02455, names *** 'D. ALEJANDRO M. LERENA y ... D.a ELISA [VILLADEMOROS] (hoy finada)' *** as the parents of Jacinta Mercedes Gregoria, and gives his own parents as *** 'D. AVELINO y D.a AMBROSIA TRAIBEL'. *** Same wife, same initial, one man - and the 1886 act calls him *** viudo *** while Julia Bassani is *** soltera ***, which is the second marriage this merged name now carries. *** A SECOND LERENA MARRIED A SECOND VILLADEMOROS, and the two marriages are probably one alliance. *** He and *** ELISA VILLARDEMOROS *** had a son christened at the Cordon on 29 May 1873. In the same decade *** AVELINO EDUARDO LERENA *** - documented as a son of Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel - married *** CELEDONIA VILLADEMOROS ***. *** THREE THINGS TIE THE TWO BAPTISMS TOGETHER: *** the surname on both mothers; a *** JOAQUIN *** standing godfather at each, indexed "Joaquin Requena" on one and "Joaquin Regusa y Garcia" on the other, which is one name and one machine mangling it; and the godmother here is *** ANGELICA VILLADEMOROS ***, while Celedonia's mother is ANGELICA MENDEZ - a daughter named for her. *** THE INFERENCE: two Lerena brothers married two Villademoros sisters, *** which is the same shape as the two Lerena siblings who married two Cardozo siblings and produced the 1911 dispensation. *** WHAT IS NOT DOCUMENTED: *** this act does NOT name his own parents, so he is NOT joined to Alejandro Lerena Traibel here, though the age fits - that man was born 1843 or 1845 and would be twenty-seven or twenty-nine. *** THE TEST: *** the two marriage acts, or any record naming this Alejandro's father. *** AND THE TEST NAMED ABOVE WAS RUN THE SAME EVENING AND CAME BACK EMPTY. *** LERENA with spouse surname VILLADEMOROS, Uruguay: 6,352 records, and *** not one of them is a marriage act. *** Every hit is a parent entry on somebody else's baptism or civil registration. *** The control is the one that worked two hours earlier: *** the same query shape on LERENA with spouse JUANICO puts the marriage act of 19 December 1864 at RANK ONE. So the shape finds a marriage when there is one to find. *** NEITHER VILLADEMOROS MARRIAGE IS IN THE INDEXED RECORD, *** and the brothers-and-sisters reading stays an inference. It would be settled by the parish marriage books of the Cordon and Union, which have not been walked.  *** THE NULL PUBLISHED AGAINST THIS ROW RESTS ON A CONTROL THAT DID NOT CONTROL FOR THE RIGHT RISK - noted 21 September 2026, and the null is NOT withdrawn. *** The finding was that LERENA with spouse surname VILLADEMOROS returns 6,352 records and not one marriage act, controlled by LERENA with spouse JUANICO, which put the 1864 marriage at rank one. *** JUANICO HAS ONE SPELLING AND VILLADEMOROS HAS AT LEAST THREE. *** This register already holds VILLADEMOROS, VILLARDEMOROS and, from a death registration read today, VILLADEMORO. And on the same day a parent-pair query on this surname returned a ZERO that a single deleted parameter turned into SEVEN. *** So the control proved the query SHAPE works; it did not prove that this SURNAME is reachable through it. *** The two marriage acts may be absent from the index, or they may be present under a spelling nobody asked for. Until the Cordon and Union marriage books are walked, the difference is not known - and that is a weaker claim than the one this archive published. *** READ OFF THE PLATE 27 September 2026, and it settles his birthplace and not his parents. *** The Cordon act of 29 May 1873 reads 'hijo legitimo de D. ALEJANDRO LERENA [y Da. Elisa Villademoros], *** ORIENTALES ***. Padrinos D. JOAQUIN REGUSA y Da. ANGELICA VILLADEMOROS.' *** THE ACT NAMES NO GRANDPARENTS *** - this parish's 1873 form does not recite them - so the plate that would have answered the whole question does not. What it does give is ORIENTAL, Uruguayan-born, which matches the 'oriental' of the 1886 and 1888 acts of Alejandro M. Lerena. See the note on that row: the two may be one man. *** AND THE 1877 ACT SPELLS HIM WITH THE M., AND NAMES HIS PARENTS. *** 'D. ALEJANDRO M. LERENA ... abuelos paternos D. AVELINO y D.a AMBROSIA TRAIBEL'. *** THIS ROW AND 'Alejandro M. LERENA (with Julia BASSANI)' ARE THE SAME MAN *** - the same wife, the same initial, and now the same parents - and they remain two rows only until the merge is done properly. See data/_person-pairs.txt. *** HIS FIRST MARRIAGE IS FOUND, 11 OCTOBER 2026, AND THE 'M.' IS MAXIMO. *** He married *** ELISA VILLADEMOROS *** at *** Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, CORDON, Montevideo, on 28 DECEMBER 1871 *** - a date work-list row 185 had sought since September and had concluded 'must be walked by image'. *** IT WAS NOT IN THE RECORD INDEX AND IT IS IN THE FULL-TEXT CORPUS ***, which is a different instrument. The act reads: *** 'En veinte y ocho de Diciembre de mil ochocientos setenta y uno, el Senor Canonigo D. MARTIN PINERO, con mi consentimiento, autorizo el matrimonio que, DISPENSADAS por el Yltmo. Senor Obispo Vicario Apostolico DOS CONCILIARES PROCLAMAS, publicada una, y previa la confesion sacramental, contrajo in facie Ecclesiae D. ALEJANDRO MAXIMO SERENA, soltero, natural de MONTEVIDEO, hijo de D. AVELINO y de Dona AMBROSIA TRAIBEL, con Dona ELISA VILLADEMOROS, del mismo estado y oriundez, hija de los finados D. PEDRO y Dona ANGELICA VILLADEMOROS. Testigos: el Doctor D. JOAQUIN REQUENA y Dona AMBROSIA T. de SERENA. De que certifico Yo el Parroco, JOSE M. OJEDA.' *** *** WHAT IT GIVES: *** his full name *** ALEJANDRO MAXIMO ***; that he was *** SOLTERO *** and *** NATURAL DE MONTEVIDEO ***; and his parents *** AVELINO *** and *** AMBROSIA TRAIBEL *** named a second time and independently of the enrolment cards. *** HIS MOTHER STOOD AS A WITNESS AT HIS WEDDING *** - 'Dona AMBROSIA T. de SERENA' - so she was living in December 1871. *** WHAT IT DOES NOT GIVE, AND ROW 185 WANTED IT MOST: HIS AGE. *** The act states his status and his birthplace and no number, so *** THE 1843-AGAINST-1845 QUESTION ON THE LA MAURICIA ACT IS UNTOUCHED BY THIS FIND *** and remains open. *** AND IT ESTABLISHES A PATTERN THIS ARCHIVE HAS NOW SEEN TWICE IN ONE DAY: TWO BROTHERS MARRIED TWO SISTERS. *** *** ALEJANDRO MAXIMO LERENA *** and *** AVELINO EDUARDO LERENA TRAIBEL *** are both sons of *** AVELINO LERENA FERNANDEZ and AMBROSIA TRAIBEL ***; *** ELISA *** and *** CELEDONIA VILLADEMOROS *** are both daughters of *** PEDRO VILLADEMOROS and ANGELICA ***. *** SO THE LERENA VILLADEMOROS COUSINS ARE DOUBLE FIRST COUSINS *** - exactly the structure that forced a dispensation at Trinidad in 1911, here produced in Montevideo a generation earlier. *** NO DISPENSATION OF KINSHIP WAS NEEDED FOR THE MARRIAGES THEMSELVES ***, because the two families were not related before them; what was dispensed in 1871 was *** TWO CONCILIAR BANNS ***, a dispensation of notice and not of blood.

note: Born *** 29 October 1886 *** and registered at Montevideo on 6 November, act N 424, page 14. Son of Alejandro M. Lerena and Julia Bassani, "hijo de los declarantes". *** HE IS THE EVIDENCE THAT THIS FAMILY WAS IN MONTEVIDEO BEFORE IT WAS IN BUENOS AIRES *** - the Argentine records for these parents begin with a baptism in 1905, nineteen years later. Appears again in Argentine military records 1911-1936 and in Capital Federal parish records, both attached in the FamilySearch tree to the same man, L8GL-F8B. *** MERGED 22 SEPTEMBER 2026 WITH THE ROW THAT STOOD HERE AS "Hector LERENA" *** - an Argentine of Buenos Aires who married AMALIA PACHECO and had a daughter Emilia Cecilia on 20 December 1915. They are one man, and the merge is made on the ACT and not on the tree's attachment. The San Carlos marriage of 25 February 1911 was opened: "hijo legitimo de D. *** ALEJANDRO MAXIMO *** [Lerena] ... y de dona *** JULIA BA[SSANI] ***, natural de Italia ... con dona *** AMALIA PA[CHECO] ***". *** THREE THINGS AGREE AT ONCE - the wife the old row carried, the parents this row carries, and the age. *** He is "de la Rep. Oriental, de veinte y cuatro" on 25 February 1911, which puts his birth between 26 February 1886 and 25 February 1887 and fits 29 October 1886 exactly. *** AND IT CORRECTS THE INDEX, WHICH HAS HIM BORN 1887 AT ALMAGRO, BUENOS AIRES. *** The act says ORIENTAL. The indexer defaulted the birthplace to the event place, which is a thing this collection's index does. His trade on the act is *** dibujante ***, draughtsman, and he lived at calle Gurruchaga 1388. *** HE IS ALSO "hijo LEGITIMO" IN 1911, THOUGH HIS MONTEVIDEO BIRTH ACT OF 1886 RECORDS NO MARRIAGE *** - his father was a widower and his mother soltera. Either Alejandro and Julia married between 1888 and 1911, or the parish wrote the ordinary word. This archive does not know which, and the marriage of those two has not been found.
