note: *** Wife of PEDRO A. LERENA *** and mother of *** MANUEL ANTONIO LERENA *** (born 31 March 1883, christened 9 April 1883 at Montevideo) and of *** FELICIA CLEMENTINA LERENA *** (born about 1868, married 1886). *** HER HOUSEHOLD IS ONE OF THE FOUR WORK-LIST ROW 187 COULD NOT PLACE, and it now has two children and a span of fifteen years. *** *** WHICH PEDRO LERENA SHE MARRIED IS NOT SETTLED: *** this register holds a PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA born 1793, son of Sancho, who cannot be the father of an 1883 child, and a separate PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA who married TERESA LEONARD and fathered a son about 1866. *** WHETHER MANUELA LEMOS AND TERESA LEONARD WERE TWO WIVES OF ONE MAN OR THE WIVES OF TWO MEN IS NOT ESTABLISHED. *** *** INDEX ONLY. *** *** ANSWERED 12 OCTOBER 2026, OR NEARLY. *** His death registration names his parents: *** PEDRO A. LERENA and VICENTA DE LA VEGA *** - so the Pedro she married is a son of that couple, which is the parentage of PEDRO LERENA VEGA, counted at sixteen in Montevideo household 229 about 1833. He died 6 November 1896 aged 69. *** AND THE ACT WAS OPENED THE SAME EVENING AND CONFIRMS IT. *** Acta 353 calls her 'Dona Manuela, Oriental, de 53 anos' - so born about 1843 - and names the children of the marriage as *** Antonio, Carlos Teodoro and Manuel Antonio ***, with a further son, Don Pedro A. Lerena, declaring the death. *** Her husband is a son of PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA and VICENTA DE LA VEGA, named in the act. The question this row asked on 11 October is answered. *** *** HER BURIAL IS FOUND, 17 October 2026: *** 'En veinte y cuatro de Julio de mil novecientos diez y ocho se mando dar sepultura eclesiastica al cadaver de Manuela Lemos, oriental, de setenta y siete anos, viuda de Carlos Lerena. Fallecio ayer.' So she died about 23 July 1918, aged seventy-seven. *** BUT THE ENTRY CALLS HER THE WIDOW OF 'CARLOS' LERENA, NOT PEDRO: *** her husband died in 1896 as Pedro A., and Carlos Teodoro is one of her sons. Either the priest wrote the wrong forename or the son's was put for the husband's. Unresolved, and the 1896 civil act is the stronger source for the husband. Her age gives a birth about 1841; the 1896 act gave about 1843.

name: Don Clemente GARCIA (d. by 1794, Rosario)
source: Garcia, Clemente: Buenos Aires City - Probate Estate Case Files 1800 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ 11 October 2026; image ark 3:1:3QHV-P3FJ-Z942; and Garcia, Clemente: Buenos Aires City - PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES 1800, image group #107093472 item 12, images 22, 24, 26, 34 of 249 - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPTS READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; arks 3:1:3QHV-P3FJ-ZS48, 3:1:3QHV-P3FJ-ZWWJ, 3:1:3QHV-L3FJ-ZWW5, 3:1:3QHV-P3FJ-Z389; held by the Archivo General de la Nacion de Argentina; and Garcia, Clemente: Buenos Aires City - PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES 1800, image group #107093472 item 12, images 28-30 of 249 - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPTS READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; arks 3:1:3QHV-P3FJ-Z7MH, 3:1:3QHV-L3FJ-Z7Y9, 3:1:3QHV-L3FJ-C9N1-K; and Garcia, Clemente: Buenos Aires City - PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES 1794, item 11 of 119 images - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:3QHK-X3TB-H94S-3
note: *** The dead man whose estate RAMON LERENA was administering as Alcalde de la Santa Hermandad in November 1800. *** His widow is *** DONA CELESTINA GONZALEZ *** and the inventories concerned goods left *** 'en beneficio del menor' ***. *** THE WHOLE FILE IS NAMED FOR HIM ***, which is why a Lerena inside it was invisible to any index that catalogues by principal. *** Admitted 11 October 2026 under the rule written that day: a person named on an act this archive has read is a person in this register, whatever their role. *** *** HE WAS HER FIRST HUSBAND, and the estate was his. *** The court calls her 'viuda del finado Don Clemente Garcia' and the inventory concerns 'los bienes que por fin y muerte de su PRIMER CONSORTE quedaron a beneficio de su hijo menor'. *** SO HE DIED LEAVING ONE MINOR SON AND A WIDOW WHO REMARRIED BEFORE OCTOBER 1800. *** *** HE WAS OF THE COLLA, in the Banda Oriental ***, not of Buenos Aires - the file sits in a Buenos Aires court because the Juez de Menores of the capital had jurisdiction over the whole viceroyalty. *** THE INVENTORY SAYS WHAT HE WAS: A STOREKEEPER WITH A MILL. *** Read 11 October 2026. The first item appraised is *** 'un RANCHO de veinte y dos varas de largo, siete de ancho, con las paredes de PIEDRA, revocadas y blanqueadas de ambas partes, con CUATRO VIVIENDAS, la una de ellas compuesta de PULPERIA con mostrador, armazon y adyacentes, trastienda, sala y aposento' ***. Then a house of *** six doors, three with lock and fittings, and five windows ***, paved floor and corridors on both sides - *** 746 pesos ***; a stone-walled, thatch-roofed building of eleven varas by seven - *** 314 pesos ***; and *** 'una ATAHONA compuesta de casa, rueda, piedras, palo-fierro, linterna y demas utensilios' *** - a *** MILL *** - at *** 310 pesos ***. Then the tools: stone-picks, an adze, axes, a turned round table, benches, a pine chest, a crowbar, a spade, a hoe. *** SO THE MAN WHOSE ESTATE RAMON LERENA WAS SENT TO VALUE KEPT THE SHOP AND THE MILL OF HIS DISTRICT *** - which is also why the case was worth a court in Buenos Aires taking an interest in. *** HIS MINOR SON IS NEVER NAMED IN THE FRAMES READ ***, only ever 'su hijo menor'. *** HE DIED SIX YEARS EARLIER THAN THIS ROW'S NAME SAYS - BY 1794, NOT BY 1800. *** The 1794 file already calls him *** 'el finado Don CLEMENTE GARCIA' *** and already calls Celestina Gonzalez *** 'la viuda' ***. *** THE ROW'S OWN TITLE IS NOW WRONG AND IS LEFT UNCHANGED DELIBERATELY ***, because renaming a person changes their published address; see data/corrections.tsv and the slug ledger. *** AND HE HAD AN ESTANCIA AS WELL AS THE SHOP AND THE MILL. *** The 1794 inventory walks out to *** 'la ESTANCIA del finado' *** to count *** 'EL GANADO Y CABALLOS' ***. So the estate is a rural holding with stock, a store, a mill and a house - *** which is why it took two inventories six years apart and a court in the capital. ***

name: Dona Celestina GONZALEZ (widow of Clemente Garcia)
source: Garcia, Clemente: Buenos Aires City - Probate Estate Case Files 1800 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ 11 October 2026; image ark 3:1:3QHV-P3FJ-Z942; and Garcia, Clemente: Buenos Aires City - PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES 1800, image group #107093472 item 12, images 22, 24, 26, 34 of 249 - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPTS READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; arks 3:1:3QHV-P3FJ-ZS48, 3:1:3QHV-P3FJ-ZWWJ, 3:1:3QHV-L3FJ-ZWW5, 3:1:3QHV-P3FJ-Z389; held by the Archivo General de la Nacion de Argentina; and Garcia, Clemente: Buenos Aires City - PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES 1800, image group #107093472 item 12, images 28-30 of 249 - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPTS READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; arks 3:1:3QHV-P3FJ-Z7MH, 3:1:3QHV-L3FJ-Z7Y9, 3:1:3QHV-L3FJ-C9N1-K; and Garcia, Clemente: Buenos Aires City - PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES 1794, item 11 of 119 images - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:3QHK-X3TB-H94S-3
note: *** The widow whom RAMON LERENA notified in person on 6 November 1800 ***, 'a quien ... notifique la providencia antecedente a Dona CELESTINA GONZALEZ en su persona'. She had written to the Alcalde del Partido del Rosario about the inventories. *** SHE IS THE PERSON A LERENA WAS STANDING IN FRONT OF on the only day in 1800 this archive can place him. *** *** Admitted 11 October 2026 under the rule written that day: a person named on an act this archive has read is a person in this register, whatever their role. *** *** SHE IS A VECINA DEL COLLA, AND SHE FOUGHT THE COURT. *** The providencia of 1800 calls her *** 'Dona CELESTINA GONZALEZ, VECINA DEL COLLA, viuda del finado Don CLEMENTE GARCIA' *** and records *** 'la resistencia que hace para la faccion de Ymbentarios de su difunto marido' ***. She had written to the Alcalde on the sixteenth; he wrote to Buenos Aires on the twenty-fourth; the Juez de Menores ordered the inventory made anyway. *** THE REASON SHE WAS COMPELLED: she had REMARRIED while she had a minor child *** - 'por haber pasado a segundas nupcias, teniendo hijo menor' - which made her *** tutora y curadora *** of the boy's inheritance and the court's business. *** RAMON LERENA NOTIFIED HER IN THE PRESENCE OF HER SECOND HUSBAND, who is not named in the frames read. *** *** SHE IS THE ONLY PERSON THIS ARCHIVE CAN PLACE IN A ROOM WITH RAMON LERENA. *** *** AND SHE COULD NOT WRITE EITHER. *** At the close of her declaration: *** 'no firmo porque dijo no saber [escribir]' ***, and her husband signed with the witnesses in her place. *** THAT IS THE THIRD PERSON IN ONE DAY'S READING WHO COULD NOT SIGN *** - Sancho Llerena in 1800, Francisco de los Santos de Acuna before him, and now the woman who held the shop and the mill of the Rosario in trust for her son. *** RAMON LERENA, WHO SIGNED HIS OWN NAME TWICE, WAS THE LITERATE ONE IN THAT ROOM. *** *** AND SHE CHOSE RAMON LERENA HERSELF, IN 1794. *** The earlier file names him and GERONIMO ALONSO as *** 'sujetos NOMBRADOS POR LA VIUDA' *** to count and value the cattle and horses of her husband's estancia, and she separately named *** LORENZO MARTINEZ DE OLALLA *** to act for her. *** THIS IS WHY THE GARCIA HOUSEHOLD BELONGS IN THIS REGISTER AND THE CHABO HOUSEHOLD DOES NOT: *** in 1794 Ramon Lerena was not the official but a man she picked, swore in and trusted with her son's inheritance. *** SIX YEARS LATER HE CAME BACK AS THE MAGISTRATE, to make her do what she was refusing to do. ***

name: Juan Jose LERENA y LERENA (of Navarrete, Logrono; Buenos Aires 1900)

name: Jose Dolores LERENA y LERENA (of Navarrete, Logrono)
occupation: juez municipal suplente and registrar of Navarrete; propietario
source: Registros Consulares: Buenos Aires City - NOTARIAL RECORDS 1900-1901, folio 138, escritura No. 368 of 14 November 1900, CONSULADO DE ESPANA EN BUENOS AIRES - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:3QHV-G3XJ-XCR6; and Expediente: Huergo Aragon, Clemente. Huerfano de Juan Chavarri Otayza: Madrid - GOVERNMENT PENSIONS 1896, the certificate issued at Navarrete - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9T3-GZPK-S
note: *** The brother who STAYED. *** 'Don Jose Dolores Leerena y Lerena, CASADO y PROPIETARIO, vecino de Navarrete' - named with his mother in the 1900 power of attorney to administer, let, mortgage, sell and if need be litigate over the family's property in Spain. *** HE IS THE ONE WITH THE LAND AND THE WIFE; HIS BROTHERS WERE SHOP-ASSISTANTS ACROSS AN OCEAN *** - which is the ordinary shape of a Riojan trading family and the likeliest explanation of the stream of young LERENA men out of Logrono into Buenos Aires commerce in this archive's CEMLA extracts: Martin at 14 in 1907, Jose M. at 16 in 1909, Jose at 16 in 1924, Emilio and Jose Maria in 1930. *** A LINE OF THE NAME THAT IS NOT THIS FAMILY'S LINE, drawn so it stops being mistaken for one. *** *** THIS HOUSEHOLD IS WHY THE ROW MATTERS MORE THAN ITS OWN PEOPLE DO. *** The brothers sign themselves *** LERENA y LERENA ***, so their father was a Lerena AND their mother was a Lerena - and Pablo Armando Lerena's 1908 enrolment card names *** JUAN CARLOS LERENA and MARIA LERENA ***. *** AND THEY ARE THE SIXTH SUCH COUPLE THIS ARCHIVE HAS MET, NOT THE FIRST - a correction to what was written here first. *** The two Trinidad couples of 1894 and 1913, the 1911 dispensation, Alejandro, and Eloy x Felisa Lerena at San Jose de Flores in 1912 all came before them. *** SO THE CARD'S DOUBLE SURNAME WAS NEVER IN REAL DOUBT, AND NAVARRETE DOES NOT RESCUE IT. *** What Navarrete adds is different and smaller: it is the *** FIRST SUCH HOUSEHOLD OUTSIDE SOUTH AMERICA ***, the *** FIRST WHERE THE CHILDREN CARRY IT DOUBLED AS A SURNAME OF RECORD *** - 'Lerena y Lerena', in their own signatures, not just a coincidence of two parents - and the *** FIRST TIME THE PRACTICE HAS A PLACE ON A MAP *** that can be searched. No link to Pablo Armando is claimed - see data/open-questions.tsv. *** AND WITHIN THE HOUR HE TURNED UP AGAIN, IN SPAIN, FOUR YEARS EARLIER, HOLDING AN OFFICE. *** A Madrid pension file of 1896 carries a certificate signed *** 'D. JOSE DOLORES LERENA Y LERENA, JUEZ MUNICIPAL SUPLENTE DE ESTA VILLA, encargado de la Jurisdiccion por ausencia del propietario, Y TAMBIEN [DEL] REGISTRO CIVIL DE LA MISMA' ***. He certifies an entry from his own book: *** 'Que en dicho Registro, seccion de DEFUNCIONES, al folio CIENTO NOVENTA Y UNO del tomo [undecimo] se encuentra el acta que dice asi' *** - the death at Navarrete on *** 11 NOVEMBER 1895 *** of Juan Manuel Chavarri Oteyza of Fuenmayor, aged seventy. *** SO HIS BROTHERS' 'CASADO Y PROPIETARIO' IN 1900 UNDERSTATES HIM: he was the acting magistrate of the town and the man who kept its civil register. *** *** THE PEOPLE IN THAT DEATH ACT ARE DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS REGISTER *** - not Clemente Huergo, not Chavarri Oteyza, not the judge Jose Maria Briones y Briones, not the secretary Florencio Velasco de la Plaza. He is the official of record and they are the business of his office, which is the boundary in tools/check-people-named.py - and it is the SECOND time in two days that boundary has been applied to a Lerena keeping a register, the first being *** VICENTE LERENA DIAZ, Jefe del Registro Civil of Pueblo Brugo, Entre Rios, 1938 ***. *** THREE MEN OF THIS NAME NOW HOLD A REGISTER OR A JURISDICTION IN THREE COUNTRIES: *** Ramon Lerena, Alcalde de la Santa Hermandad del Partido del Rosario, 1796-1800; Jose Dolores Lerena y Lerena, juez municipal and registrar of Navarrete, 1895-96; Vicente Lerena Diaz at Pueblo Brugo, 1938. *** NO CONNECTION IS CLAIMED BETWEEN THEM AND THERE IS NO REASON TO THINK ONE EXISTS *** - a village needs a literate man and these are three different villages a hemisphere apart. It is recorded because it is the kind of coincidence this archive would otherwise mistake for a pattern later, having forgotten it noticed it. *** WHAT IT OPENS: *** the Juzgado Municipal of Navarrete kept DEFUNCIONES in numbered volumes - tomo 11 reached folio 191 by November 1895 - so the civil register of the village where Lerenas married Lerenas exists and is described. See data/open-questions.tsv, question 1.

name: Carlos A. LERENA (plaintiff, Buenos Aires 1890)
source: Escalada, Carlos M.; Lerena, Carlos A.: Buenos Aires City - PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES 1891, item 11 of 91 images, the answer filed February 1890 - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ 11 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:3QHV-V3DS-X934-6
note: *** THE CASE IS NAMED FOR HIM - 'Escalada, Carlos M.; LERENA, CARLOS A.' - so he is a party, not a passer-by. *** He sued the testamentary estate of *** DON CARLOS MARIA ESCALADA *** for money: 'contestando a la demanda entablada por D. CARLOS A. LERENA, *** SOBRE COBRO DE PESOS ***'. What he was claiming was *** 'LA COMISION POR LA COMPRAVENTA a que se refiere' ***, so he was acting as a *** BROKER ON A SALE *** and wanted his commission out of a dead man's estate. *** THE ESTATE'S ANSWER IS A FLAT REFUSAL *** - the lawyer A. FERREYRA asks the judge to dismiss it with costs, because the claim rests on 'su sola afirmacion', he *** 'no acompana documento alguno en que conste lo que asevera. NI TAMPOCO PUEDE ACOMPANARLO' ***, the succession having concluded no contract at all. *** WE DO NOT KNOW WHO WON. *** 91 images in the file and one read. *** NOT THE CARLOS LERENA OF MENDOZA *** who married Adela Camiglia and had Avelino Carlos in 1904 - different city, and a decade too early to be the same working life without evidence; see data/_person-pairs.txt. *** A LERENA IN BUENOS AIRES COMMERCE IN 1890, which is the decade and the city this archive cares about most ***, though nothing connects him to Rosario or to Pablo Armando.

note: *** A NEW HEAD OF A MONTEVIDEO HOUSEHOLD, 11 October 2026. *** Named on his son's marriage act of 11 January 1920 as *** 'ARTURO LERENA, de nacionalidad ORIENTAL, de estado CASADO, de SESENTA Y DOS anos, domiciliado en MONTEVIDEO' *** - so *** born about 1857-58 ***, alive and married in January 1920, living in the capital. His wife is *** EMA REGULES ***. *** HE IS NOT ARTURO LERENA GARCIA ***, who is in this register as a *** SPANISH *** journalist with sons surnamed LERENA DIAZ by Amalia Diaz. Nationality separates them on the face of the two acts and they are kept apart; see data/_person-pairs.txt. *** WHAT HE OPENS: *** a Lerena born about 1857 in Uruguay, with a son born in Montevideo in 1886, is exactly the generation this archive searches for Juan Carlos - and he is not Juan Carlos, because his son's act names him plainly. *** HIS OWN PARENTS ARE NOT ON THIS ACT ***, which is the ordinary limit of a Uruguayan civil marriage: it names the couple's parents and stops. *** HIS OWN MARRIAGE ACT, FOUND WITHIN THE HOUR - AND IT PUTS HIM IN SANCHO'S HOUSE. *** *** 'En VEINTE Y TRES DE JUNIO de mil ochocientos OCHENTA, el Presbitero Don JUAN JOSE BRID, con licencia del Cura Parroco de esta BASILICA MENOR Y CATEDRAL DE MONTEVIDEO, DISPENSADAS LAS TRES CONCILIARES PROCLAMAS por el Ilustrisimo y Reverendisimo Senor Obispo Diocesano DON JACINTO VERA, autorizo... el matrimonio que contrajo el DOCTOR DON ARTURO [L]ERENA, natural de esta Republica, soltero, de VEINTE Y DOS ANOS de edad, HIJO LEGITIMO DE DON AVELINO LERENA Y DONA AMBROSIA TRAIBEL, con DONA EMMA REGULES... de DIEZ Y SEIS ANOS de edad, hija legitima de DON WENCESLAO REGULES y DONA JUSTINIANA MELILLA: fueron testigos el DOCTOR DON AMBROSIO LERENA y Dona Justiniana Melilla de Regules.' *** *** SO HE IS A SON OF AVELINO LERENA AND AMBROSIA TRAIBEL - THE HEAD OF THE LERENA TRAIBEL BRANCH, AND SANCHO'S SON. *** That makes his son EDUARDO a great-grandson of Sancho Llerena, and the Argentine household at Adolfo Alsina a branch of this archive's own trunk rather than a namesake. *** HE IS A DOCTOR ***, which no other man in this register is, and he was twenty-two in June 1880 - *** born about 1857-58, which agrees exactly with the SIXTY-TWO years his son's act gives him in January 1920. *** *** AND THE ARCHIVE ALREADY HOLDS A SON OF THAT COUPLE CALLED JUAN ARTURO, born 16 February 1861 - NOT MERGED. *** A man born in February 1861 was NINETEEN in June 1880, not twenty-two, and this archive has his baptismal date from the Cordon. *** AN AGE ON A MARRIAGE ACT BENDS BY A YEAR; IT DOES NOT USUALLY BEND BY THREE ***, and the couple had eleven known children already, so a twelfth named Arturo is not a strain. See data/_person-pairs.txt. *** A LEAD NOT YET OPENED: *** the Montevideo civil marriages of 1907-08 carry a *** 'Dona EMMA LERENA REGULES' *** with her parents given as 'don Arturo Lerena' and 'Emma Regules' - a daughter, marrying. *** HE IS A LAWYER, NOT A PHYSICIAN - AND THIS ROW SAID 'DOCTOR' FOR AN HOUR WITHOUT ASKING WHICH KIND. *** His daughter's marriage act of 9 August 1909 gives him plainly: *** 'hija de don ARTURO LERENA, de estado casado, DE PROFESION ABOGADO, de nacionalidad oriental, domiciliado en la calle COLONIA 2200' ***. In Uruguay *** DOCTOR IS THE STYLE OF AN ABOGADO *** as much as of a medico, and the 1880 marriage act's 'el Doctor Don Arturo Lerena' carries no more than that. *** THE OCCUPATION FIELD IS CORRECTED AND SO IS THE INFERENCE DRAWN FROM IT ***: this archive wrote that the Lerena Traibel were 'a professional household' on the strength of two men called Doctor, which remains true, and said it in a way that suggested medicine, which was never stated. *** A SECOND CHILD, 12 October 2026: *** *** EMMA LERENA REGULES, born 18 May 1885 at SAN JOSE ***, who married Fermin Carlos de Yeregui at Montevideo on 9 August 1909. *** SO THE HOUSEHOLD WAS AT SAN JOSE IN 1885 AND AT MONTEVIDEO IN 1886 ***, where his son Eduardo was born on 22 April. *** THOSE TWO BIRTHS ARE ELEVEN MONTHS APART, which is possible and tight, and is recorded as a tension rather than resolved. *** *** AND IN 1909 HE AND HIS WIFE ARE GIVEN AT DIFFERENT ADDRESSES *** - he at calle Colonia *** 2200 ***, she at calle Colonia *** 228 *** - both 'de estado casado'. The numbers differ by a factor of ten and the likeliest reading is a transcriber's slip rather than a separation; *** NOT RESOLVED. *** *** HIS WHOLE KNOWN SIBSHIP, FROM ONE PARENT-PAIR QUERY - 12 October 2026. *** Six children by Emma Regules: *** EMA JUSTINA FELICIA (b. 18 May 1881, San Jose), ARTURO MARIO (b. 9 April 1884, San Jose, who died at Montevideo in 1949), EMMA (b. 18 May 1885, San Jose), EDUARDO (b. 22 April 1886, Montevideo), CORA MARIA AVELINA (b. 8 June 1887, christened at the Union 23 October 1887) and ROBERTO AMBROSIO (b. 1 November 1896, Montevideo) ***. *** AND TWO OF THOSE NAMES CORROBORATE HIS OWN PARENTAGE WITHOUT A SECOND ACT. *** The 1880 marriage makes him a son of *** AVELINO LERENA and AMBROSIA TRAIBEL ***; his fifth child is *** AVELINA *** and his sixth is *** AMBROSIO ***. *** A HOUSEHOLD NAMES ITS CHILDREN FOR ITS OWN PARENTS, and this one did it twice. *** *** THE FAMILY MOVED: *** San Jose from 1881 to 1885, Montevideo from 1886. *** AND THERE IS A NINE-YEAR GAP, 1887 to 1896 ***, which in a household of this period usually means children this query did not reach - deaths in infancy, or acts indexed under another spelling. *** HIS DEATH ACT, AND IT IS THE BEST DOCUMENT THIS HOUSEHOLD HAS - 12 October 2026. *** *** 'En Montevideo y el dia DOS DE MARZO DE MIL NOVECIENTOS TREINTA Y SEIS... declarando que a las DOS HORAS del dia de hoy y en TREINTA Y TRES 269, fallecio ARTURO LERENA, del sexo masculino, de nacionalidad ORIENTAL, NACIDO EN MONTEVIDEO, de SETENTA Y OCHO ANOS DE EDAD, de estado casado, DE PROFESION ABOGADO, a consecuencia de [la causa] segun consta del certificado del DOCTOR JORGE CALVETTE... Que el finado era HIJO DE A[V]ELINO [L]ERENA y de AMBROSIA TR[A]IBEL, AMBOS FALLECIDOS... era casado con [E]MA REGULES, de cuyo consorcio quedaron CINCO HIJOS llamados EMA, MARIO, EDUARDO, CORA y ROBERTO.' *** *** SO: d. 2 March 1936, at two in the morning, at Treinta y Tres 269, aged 78, a lawyer. *** The act confirms his parents a second time and confirms the profession correction made the same day. *** AND IT NAMES FIVE SURVIVING CHILDREN WHERE THE INDEX GAVE SIX. *** Ema, Mario, Eduardo, Cora and Roberto - which is this register's sibship with *** ONLY ONE EMA ***. That does not settle the two daughters born on 18 May, in 1881 and 1885: five surviving of six is what the act would say if one had died. *** IT DOES TILT IT *** - see the rows for both women. *** THE AGE IS THE THIRD INDEPENDENT STATEMENT OF HIS BIRTH YEAR AND THEY ALL AGREE: *** twenty-two in June 1880, sixty-two in January 1920, seventy-eight in March 1936 - 1857, 1857-58, 1857-58. *** AGAINST ONE BAPTISM OF A 'JUAN ARTURO' IN FEBRUARY 1861. *** *** FAMILYSEARCH'S OWN TREE HAS ALREADY MERGED THEM ***, attaching this death record to a profile 'Juan Arturo Lerena Traibel, 1861-1936'. *** THAT IS A TREE, NOT A DOCUMENT ***, and this register keeps the two apart until an act does the joining. *** THE DECLARANTS WERE NOT FAMILY: *** an Italian employee of forty and an oriental of twenty-three, neither named Lerena, which is the ordinary shape of a city death registration and means the ages in it are secondhand.

note: *** Named on her son Eduardo's marriage act of 11 January 1920: *** 'y de EMA REGULES, de nacionalidad ORIENTAL, de estado CASADA, de CINCUENTA Y CINCO anos' - so born about *** 1864-65 ***, alive and married in 1920. The transcript renders her surname *** 'Ema Re gales' *** with a broken word; REGULES is a known Uruguayan surname and the reading is not plate-confirmed. *** AND SHE IS A CANDIDATE FOR SOMETHING FOUND EARLIER THE SAME DAY: *** an *** 'Ema. Lerena' *** stood godmother at the Cordon between 1900 and 1902 beside an *** EDUARDO LERENA ***. A married woman is written under her husband's name in a parish book, and Ema Regules would have been about thirty-six, with a son Eduardo aged fourteen to sixteen. *** THAT IS A CANDIDACY AND NOT A FINDING ***: a boy of fourteen is young for a godfather, the Cordon act gives no ages, and this register already holds two other women called Ema Lerena. See data/_person-pairs.txt. *** HER PARENTS AND HER WEDDING, 11 October 2026. *** She married Dr Arturo Lerena at the Catedral de Montevideo on *** 23 June 1880 ***, aged *** SIXTEEN ***, 'hija legitima de DON WENCESLAO REGULES y DONA JUSTINIANA MELILLA' - so born about *** 1863-64 ***, which agrees with the fifty-five years her son's act gives her in 1920. *** HER MOTHER STOOD AS A WITNESS AT HER OWN DAUGHTER'S WEDDING ***, written there as *** 'Dona Justiniana Melilla de Regules' ***. *** SIXTEEN IS YOUNG AND THE BANNS WERE DISPENSED BY THE BISHOP HIMSELF ***, which this archive notes without drawing a conclusion: a dispensation of the three proclamas is about publication, not about kinship, and no impediment of blood is recorded. The act spells her *** EMMA ***; her son's act of 1920 spells her *** EMA ***. *** ALIVE AND MARRIED IN AUGUST 1909 ***, at calle Colonia 228, Montevideo, when her daughter *** EMMA LERENA REGULES *** married: 'y de EMMA REGULES de estado CASADA de profesion LABORES de nacionalidad oriental'. *** HER DAUGHTER CARRIES HER NAME. *** *** A WIDOW FROM 2 MARCH 1936 ***, when her husband died at Treinta y Tres 269, Montevideo. The act records *** 'el finado era casado con [E]MA REGULES, de cuyo consorcio quedaron CINCO HIJOS' *** - so she outlived him, or at least was not recorded as dead, which is not the same thing and is all the act says.

name: BARBARA (enslaved in Alejandro Lerena's household, San Jose 1846)
source: FamilySearch RECORD INDEX - exact-surname parent-pair query, FATHER SURNAME LERENA with MOTHER SURNAME LERENA, 38 results worldwide, run 12 October 2026 - *** INDEX-LEVEL, NO ACT OPENED ***; and San Jose de Mayo - RELIGIOUS DEATH RECORDS July 1839 to December 1851, the burial of 28 April 1846 - *** READ OFF THE PLATE 12 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-J7GN-C, deepzoom apid TH-909-72167-155289-86; index entry ark 1:1:XSXQ-4RD2; and San Jose de Mayo - BAPTISM RECORDS January 1841 to May 1869, the baptism of 25 April 1846 - *** READ OFF THE PLATE 12 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D9GN-8
note: *** SHE WAS NOT A WIFE AND SHE WAS NOT A LERENA. SHE WAS AN ENSLAVED WOMAN, and this archive published her as somebody's spouse for a few hours on 12 October 2026. *** The index of her son's burial lists 'Alejandro Lerena' as father and 'Barbara Lerena' as mother, and on that reading this register entered a Lerena-married-a-Lerena couple. *** THE PLATE SAYS OTHERWISE: *** *** 'En esta Parroquia de S.n Jose a VEINTE Y OCHO DE ABRIL de mil ochocientos CUARENTA Y SEIS, yo D.n FRAN.CO CASTELLO cura vic.o int.o di sepultura en el ANGELORIO al cadaver de CARMELO ANSELMO, HIJO NATURAL DE BARBARA, ESCLAVA DE D.N ALEJANDRO LERENA, murio ayer de enfermedad, de edad de SIETE DIAS, y se le hizo oficio rezado, de que certifico.' *** *** 'ESCLAVA DE D.N ALEJANDRO LERENA' - THE INDEXER TURNED THAT INTO A MARRIAGE, giving her the surname of the man who held her. *** She is named here as the act names her: *** BARBARA, with no surname ***, because the act gives her none and this archive will not lend her one. *** HER SON WAS CALLED CARMELO ANSELMO AND HE LIVED SEVEN DAYS. *** He is entered as *** 'hijo natural' ***, which is what the act says; no father is named on it. *** THE FIFTH PERSON THIS FAMILY IS KNOWN TO HAVE HELD IN SLAVERY. *** The others are JUANA, ANTONIO, JOSE and TERESA, in Sancho Llerena's household at Canelones in 1812, with Juana's daughter MARIA MERCEDES born into it. *** THIS ONE IS THIRTY-FOUR YEARS LATER AND IN A DIFFERENT HOUSEHOLD. *** *** ON THE DATE, THIS ARCHIVE STATES ONLY WHAT IT KNOWS: *** the act says 'esclava' in April 1846. Uruguay's abolition came in stages during the Guerra Grande, and *** WHICH DECREE APPLIED AT SAN JOSE IN APRIL 1846 IS NOT ESTABLISHED HERE. *** That is a question for the next session and it is not answered by this act. *** AND HER OWN BAPTISMAL ACT WAS FOUND THREE DAYS EARLIER IN THE BOOK, 12 October 2026 - the SON'S baptism of 25 April 1846, which says two things the burial does not. *** 'bautice solemnemente a Car[melo] Anselmo, que nacio el VEINTIUNO del mismo, hijo natural de *** BARBARA LERENA, NATURAL DE ESTA VILLA, ESCLAVA DE DON ALEJANDRO LERENA *** : fueron Padrinos Jose Carreras y Petronila Escobar.' *** SO THE ACT ITSELF WRITES HER AS BARBARA LERENA. *** This row says she was not a Lerena, and as to family that stands - but the priest gave her the surname of the man who held her, in writing, and that is the fact to record rather than tidy away. *** And she was born at San Jose de Mayo *** - 'natural de esta Villa' - which this row had blank.

name: Dr LLERENA (curador, Buenos Aires courts 1889)
source: Aguirre, Feliciano: Buenos Aires City - PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES 1889, the Agente Fiscal's dictamen - *** FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ 12 OCTOBER 2026 ***; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSTZ-396J-K
note: *** A LERENA PRACTISING IN THE BUENOS AIRES COURTS, AND HE IS NOT THE WORD 'HERENCIA'. *** This archive's worklist carried him as a one-line snippet with a warning attached, because in that corpus *** lerena *** is very often the transcriber's reading of *** herencia ***. He is real. The Agente Fiscal's opinion in the Feliciano Aguirre probate reads: *** '...no lo hace el DOCTOR LERENA si la intervencion del CONSUL ESPANOL en este estado del juicio es o no oportuna. Lo que debe resolverse es si el nombramiento del CURADOR DON LLERENA es o no arreglado a derecho. Al simple pedido de [Contreras] de f.46, el Juzgado nombra CURADOR AL DOCTOR LLERENA, sin oir a este Ministerio... hubiera dictaminado que se librase nuevo oficio al Senor CONSUL DE ESPANA, para que si deseare intervenir en este juicio lo hiciere dentro de un termino perentorio.' *** *** SO: A LAWYER APPOINTED CURADOR OF AN ESTATE, AND THE FISCAL IS COMPLAINING THAT THE COURT APPOINTED HIM WITHOUT ASKING THE MINISTRY OR THE SPANISH CONSUL. *** The consul's interest means the deceased was most likely a Spanish subject. *** THE SAME PASSAGE SPELLS HIM BOTH LERENA AND LLERENA ***, twice each, in one hand - which is the single clearest demonstration in this register that the two spellings are one name. *** AND HE IS NOT A PHYSICIAN. *** 'Doctor' before a curador is the style of an ABOGADO, the same lesson this archive learned about Arturo Lerena of Montevideo earlier the same day. *** A 'DOCTOR LERENA' RECURS IN THIS COURT ACROSS A DECADE *** - the Regidor probate of 1890, Villaverde-Duportal 1894 and Foz 1897 all carry the phrase and *** NONE OF THEM HAS BEEN OPENED. *** *** NOT MERGED WITH CARLOS A. LERENA ***, the commission agent who sued the Escalada estate in the same courts in February 1890: one is a party suing, the other an officer of the court, and nothing joins them but a surname and a city.

She is not merged with any other Amelia in this register - nothing here says whose child she was. *** A CANDIDATE FOR WHOSE CHILD SHE WAS, 18 October 2026: *** the Cordon christening of 8 February 1863 (folio 440, plate read) is of an Amelia born on 2 May 1862 to a Pedro A. Lerena and Trinidad Morales - nine and a half on the day of this entry, in the same parish, with the same cura. Probably the same girl; still not merged, because neither act names the other's parents and a death entry of 'nueve anos' fits any Amelia of that age.

source: Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, Cordon - Religious Burial Records June 1885 - August 1892, the entry of 2 August 1890; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-4SWL-D - *** IMAGE READ *** 17 October 2026; and Montevideo civil death registration no. 121 of 2 August 1890; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2C-K3NM-S; index ark 1:1:XMZZ-6HQW - *** IMAGE READ *** 17 October 2026
note: *** A LERENA'S SON UNDER HIS FATHER'S NAME, 17 October 2026. *** The plate reads: 'En dos de Agosto del ano mil ochocientos noventa se mando dar sepultura eclesiastica al cadaver de Jose Maria Larranaga [the margin: 'Larranaga'], oriental, soltero, de veintidos anos de edad, hijo legitimo de Benito Larranaga y de Martina Lerena. Fallecio ayer. De que certifica.' Born about 1868. *** THE LERENA IS ON HIS MOTHER'S SIDE *** - a compound-surname search on LERENA would never reach him, because he is a LARRANAGA. Nothing places his mother in a Lerena family here. *** HIS CIVIL DEATH ACT IS READ, 17 October 2026: *** act 121 of 2 August 1890, Seccion 18a: 'a las diez y media de la manana del dia de ayer [1 August], en la calle 18 de Julio N.o 847 (bajos), ha fallecido Jose Maria Larranaga, de nacionalidad Oriental, de veintidos anos de edad, de estado soltero y de profesion COCHERO, a consecuencia de TISIS PULMONAR, segun consta del certificado del Dr. Lisazo'; 'hijo legitimo de Benito Larranaga y de Martina Lerena'. Declared by Don L. Barbagelata, twenty-five, and Don Fernando Herrera, twenty-one, of calle Paysandu 85. *** So he died on 1 August 1890, was a coachman, and died of consumption. *** FamilySearch's index gives the same date. He was one of seven children named on his father's death act of 1885.

note: *** NAMED ONLY, as the husband of Teresa Leonar and father of Manuel on her civil death act of 27 August 1901: 'viuda de Pedro Antonio Lerena, oriental, quedando del matrimonio un hijo llamado: Manuel'. *** *** DEAD BY THAT DAY. *** *** HE IS NOT THE PEDRO LERENA VEGA WHO DIED IN 1896, 17 October 2026: *** the 1864 christening of his daughter Manuela names HIS parents as Pedro and Maria Pereyra, and Pedro Lerena Vega's mother was Vicenta Vega. LERENA' - AND WROTE LEONARD FOR HER SURNAME. *** The expediente of June 1861 is above and below: he applied to the Vicario for the dispensation of two of the three banns because the bride's mother had gone to the country to nurse a sick daughter. *** THE 'A.' The register's other 'Pedro a. Lerena' of the 1890s is a different man (Pedro Lerena Vega, mother Vicenta Vega). The petition gives no age, trade, parents or residence for him, so the unidentified father 'Pedro' of the 1864 christening is NOT advanced by it.

name: Maria LERENA (m. FERNANDEZ, d. 1892 Trinidad)
source: Trinidad, Flores, Civil Death Records 1892, act no. 49 of 3 May 1892; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-W748-Y, index ark 1:1:XS6K-3TFL - *** IMAGE READ *** 17 October 2026; and San Jose de Mayo, Baptism Records 1822-1828 (film 008163861, image 792 of 815), the christening of Maria Casilda, April 1827; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-CS9R-5 - *** IMAGE READ *** 18 October 2026, found by the machine index of the image, which listed 'Alexandro Serena', 'Margari' and 'Maria Casilda Serena'; and Santisima Trinidad, Trinidad, Flores, Baptism Records 1848-1857 (film 008163892, image 229 of 767), the christening of Maria del Carmen, July 1857 (cura Florentino Luis Conde); image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F34L-N - *** IMAGE READ *** 18 October 2026, found by scanning the volume's machine index for Lerena-like names; and Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records 1852-1855 (film 007713344, item 3, images 162-167 of 643), expediente no. 15 of 1853 - the petition of Manuel Fernandez for his son Ramon to marry his niece Maria Lerena; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-T9B1-K (the petition, image 164) and 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-TS33-3 (the kinship diagram, image 163) - *** PETITION, COVER AND DIAGRAM READ AT THE PLATE *** 19 October 2026, the decree and grant (images 165-166) from FamilySearch's machine transcript only; found by a FULL-TEXT search for the two names
note: *** A DAUGHTER OF ALEJANDRO LERENA AND MARGARITA FERNANDEZ, NEW TO THIS ARCHIVE, 17 October 2026. *** Her civil death act at Trinidad, read at the plate: 'Maria Lerena de Fernandez, de nacionalidad oriental, de sesenta y cuatro anos de edad, de estado viuda, ... a consecuencia de Cancer del estomago ... Que la finada era hija legitima de don Alejandro Lerena y dona Margarita Fernandez, ambos fallecidos', died at two in the morning, declared by 'Manuel Vaquero' [the signature may read Vazquez], thirty, and Francisco C[...], thirty-one, both procuradores of Trinidad, with a closing line that the first declarant makes it 'como pa[riente]' - cut at the page edge, so read as 'relative' and not as certain. *** SIXTY-FOUR ON 3 MAY 1892 WOULD BE A BIRTH BETWEEN 4 MAY 1827 AND 3 MAY 1828 - BUT HER BAPTISM, BELOW, PUTS IT ON OR BEFORE 11 APRIL 1827, SO THE 1892 AGE WAS ABOUT A YEAR LOW - *** which makes her the eldest of the five known children, born before Alejandro (23 February 1829). [SUPERSEDED 18 October 2026: HER HUSBAND IS RAMON FERNANDEZ, named in the baptism of their daughter below.] *** THE INDEX GIVES TRINIDAD AS HER BIRTHPLACE *** while the family is at San Jose in 1825 and 1829; that is probably where she died, and is unresolved. *** A BAPTISM OF HER OWN IS FOUND AND READ AT THE PLATE, 18 October 2026: MARIA CASILDA, CHRISTENED AT SAN JOSE ON 11 APRIL 1827. *** 'En once de Abril de mil ochocientos veinte y siete, yo el Dr. D.n Feliciano Rodriguez, Cura y Vicario Interino de esta Parroquia, bautice solemnemente a Maria Casilda, hija legitima de Alexandro Lerena y Margarita Fernandez. Abuelos paternos Ramon y Maria de Leon. Maternos Juan [y] Barbara Sotura. Padrinos Marcos de Leon Gonzalez y [Maria] Fernandez Albarez, a quienes instrui y por verdad lo firme'; margin 'Maria Casilda'. NO BIRTH DATE IS WRITTEN, so she was born on or before that day. *** THE IDENTIFICATION: *** the parents are Alexandro Lerena and Margarita Fernandez and the grandparents Ramon and Maria [de Leon / Gonzalez] and Juan and Barbara Sotura - the same four lines as her siblings' baptisms - and she is the ONLY Maria of Alejandro and Margarita known to this register; the 1892 death act names the same parents and no more than 'Maria Lerena de Fernandez', sixty-four. So Maria Casilda is the Maria of 1892 on every particular that can be compared, and nothing contradicts it - STRONG, NOT PROVED: no document names her husband and no baptismal name appears in 1892. *** SHE IS THE ELDEST OF THE FIVE *** and the only one born before Alejandro's baptism volume begins. *** THE GODFATHER IS 'MARCOS DE LEON GONZALEZ', *** carrying the 'de Leon Gonzalez' of her paternal grandmother's family (the 1812 and 1816 acts have Maria Josefa / Maria de Leon Gonzalez, daughter of Marcial de Leon Gonzalez): a kinsman on her father's mother's side, not placed here. The godmother is Maria Fernandez Albarez - the SISTER of Margarita who stood at her wedding in 1825, named on this register as Margarita's sister Maria. The index gave Trinidad as her birthplace; she was baptised at San Jose, and Trinidad is where she died. *** HER NAME: MARIA CASILDA WAS NAMED FOR HER AUNT CASILDA FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ, 18 October 2026, *** the wife of her godfather Marcos de Leon Gonzalez, who is her father's mother's brother. *** HER HUSBAND IS NAMED, 18 October 2026: RAMON FERNANDEZ - AND HE IS HER FIRST COUSIN. *** The Trinidad baptism of their daughter, read at the plate, 'En diez y nueve de Julio de mil ochocientos cincuenta y siete, Yo Florentino Luis Conde, Cura Vicario de la misma, bautice solemnemente a Maria del Carmen [del Corazon de Jesus], que nacio el dia diez y seis del que rige, e hija legitima de Ramon Fernandez y de Maria Lerena, naturales y vecinos de esta Parroquia. Abs. Pat.s Manuel Fernandez y Maria de los Reyes Gonzales, Mat.s D.n Alejandro Lerena y D.a Margarita Fernandez, y fueron los Pad.s Serapio Fernandez y Socorro Lerena, a quienes adverti el parentesco espiritual y demas oblig.s'. *** SO MARIA LERENA, 'DE FERNANDEZ' IN 1892, WAS THE WIFE OF RAMON FERNANDEZ, A SON OF MANUEL FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ - MARGARITA'S BROTHER - AND MARIA DE LOS REYES GONZALEZ, *** so she and Ramon were first cousins on her mother's side, exactly as her sister Socorro and Serapio Fernandez were (Serapio is another son of Manuel). Two sisters married two brothers who were their first cousins. Both couples were 'naturales y vecinos' of Trinidad in 1857. *** THE DAUGHTER MARIA DEL CARMEN WAS BORN 16 JULY 1857 *** and her godparents were her aunt Socorro and uncle Serapio. *** THE DISPENSATION IS FOUND, 19 October 2026 [the sentence that stood here, 'not found', is superseded]. *** Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records 1852-1855, film 007713344, item 3 (images 162-167), expediente no. 15 of 1853. The cover (image 162, plate read): 'Don Manuel Fernandez por su hijo Ramon, solicita ... dispensa del impedimento canonico de parentesco en segundo grado de consanguinidad por linea transversal con Maria Lerena: parroquia de Porongos'. THE PETITION (image 164, plate read): Manuel Fernandez, married, of the 'Partido nombrado las Puntas de San Jose', in the parish of the Santisima Trinidad in the Porongos, says that by his marriage to Maria de los Reyes Gonzalez he has a son Ramon, 'soltero, de edad de veinte y un anos, nativo y domiciliado' in that district, who with his father's consent means to marry 'la joven mi sobrina Maria Lerena, de edad de veinte y cuatro anos, natural de San Jose, y domiciliada en la campana del territorio de mi indicada parroquia, hija legitima de Alexandro Lerena y Margarita Fernandez, que es mi hermana', Manuel and Margarita being children of Juan Fernandez and Barbara Sotura: 'primos hermanos, ligados en segundo grado de consanguinidad por linea transversal'. THE CAUSES HE GIVES (machine transcript; the rest of the petition was not read at the plate): she is older than twenty-four; she lives in an unpopulated place where she cannot easily find another man she is not related to; she has no dowry; her parents are burdened with a family - 'nueve hijos, entre estos cuatro mujeres'; and a young woman there is exposed to being carried off. THE GRANT (images 165-166, machine transcript): the Provisor General's decree at Montevideo on 7 September 1853 (notary Sebastian Roso) ordered a genealogical diagram and the same day dispensed 'Ramon Fernandez y Maria Lerena, parroquianos de la ... Iglesia de Porongos', on condition that three witnesses swear before the Cura y Vicario of the parish to the descent from Juan Fernandez and Barbara Sotura, the two marriages, her age, her poverty and the size of her parents' family, with a penance of three pounds of wax each for the lamp of the Blessed Sacrament; the entry is registered at folio 40 of the third book (image 167). THE DIAGRAM (image 163, plate read, 7 September 1853): Juan Fernandez and Barbara Sotura at the apex; below them 'Manuel' (hijo) and 'Margarita' (hija) as 'hermanos, 1.o g.o'; below those Ramon Fernandez and Maria Lerena as 'primos hermanos, 2.o g.o'. *** WHAT IT CHANGES: *** the kinship is no longer worked out here from baptisms; it is stated by the parties' own papers - Maria is the niece of Manuel Fernandez and the first cousin of Ramon, through her mother Margarita, Manuel's sister. *** HER STATED AGE IS A YEAR OR TWO LOW, AS IT WAS IN 1892: *** 'veinte y cuatro' in September 1853 would be a birth in 1828 or 1829, and the baptism puts it on or before 11 April 1827; the petition itself lists 'older than twenty-four' as its first cause, so the figure is a round statement and is not used for her birth. *** NINE CHILDREN, FOUR OF THEM GIRLS, IN 1853, *** where this register holds five by name (Maria, Alejandro, Estefania, Socorro, Bernabe): if the nine count her, one more daughter and three more sons of Alejandro and Margarita are unplaced. *** RAMON'S AGE: *** twenty-one in 1853, so born about 1832 and some five years younger than his wife. *** NOT FOUND: *** the marriage act itself (after 7 September 1853 and before July 1857, at Trinidad), the three witnesses' depositions, and Ramon's death before 1892.

name: Ramon FERNANDEZ (m. Maria Lerena)
source: Santisima Trinidad, Trinidad, Flores, Baptism Records 1848-1857 (film 008163892, image 229 of 767), the christening of Maria del Carmen, July 1857 (cura Florentino Luis Conde); image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F34L-N - *** IMAGE READ *** 18 October 2026, found by scanning the volume's machine index for Lerena-like names; and Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records 1852-1855 (film 007713344, item 3, images 162-167 of 643), expediente no. 15 of 1853 - the petition of his father Manuel Fernandez for his marriage to his cousin Maria Lerena; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-T9B1-K (the petition, image 164) and 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-TS33-3 (the kinship diagram, image 163) - *** PETITION, COVER AND DIAGRAM READ AT THE PLATE *** 19 October 2026, the decree and grant (images 165-166) from FamilySearch's machine transcript only; found by a FULL-TEXT search for the two names
note: *** THE HUSBAND OF MARIA LERENA, NAMED ONLY ON HIS DAUGHTER'S BAPTISM, 18 October 2026, AND NOW IN HIS FATHER'S PETITION OF 1853, 18 October 2026. *** 'hija legitima de Ramon Fernandez y de Maria Lerena, naturales y vecinos de esta Parroquia' of Trinidad; paternal grandparents Manuel Fernandez and Maria de los Reyes Gonzales. He is a son of Manuel Fernandez Alvarez - Margarita's brother - so HE IS HIS WIFE'S FIRST COUSIN, and a brother of Serapio, who married her sister Socorro. He stands godfather at Trinidad with Estefania Lerena in 1850 if the 'Dn. Ramon Fernandez' of that act is he, which is likely and not proved. *** HIS AGE AND HIS FATHER'S PETITION, 19 October 2026: *** in the petition of 1853 (film 007713344, image 164, plate read) his father Manuel Fernandez asks the Provisor General to dispense the second degree of consanguinity between 'mi hijo Ramon, soltero, de edad de veinte y un anos, nativo y domiciliado' in the Puntas de San Jose district of the Trinidad parish in the Porongos, and 'mi sobrina Maria Lerena'; the dispensation was granted at Montevideo on 7 September 1853 on condition of witnesses before the parish priest, and the diagram drawn the same day shows him and her as 'primos hermanos, 2.o g.o' under Juan Fernandez and Barbara Sotura. So he was born about 1832, in that district, and was five years or so younger than his wife. His age makes him eighteen in October 1850, when a 'Dn. Ramon Fernandez' stood godfather beside Estefania Lerena - possible, still not proved. No death date is held; he was dead by 1892, when his wife was a widow.
